# Done plans

only grows: search it with grep, or read one entry by its line range. Never read it whole.

## Done

### GTK 4 suite extraction: isolate switch declarations (planned 2026-11-12 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-12 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` is still one large `TestGtk4Theme` class.
Move the nine `test_switch_*` declaration checks (about 51 lines at this
plan's base commit) into their own module, the same way the landed OSD
(`tests/test_gtk4_osd.py`), scale (`tests/test_gtk4_scale.py`), spinbutton
(`tests/test_gtk4_spinbutton.py`), disabled (`tests/test_gtk4_disabled.py`),
emoji, entry and notebook parts moved theirs. This is independent of the
waiting "GTK 4 suite extraction: isolate scrollbar declarations" entry (that
entry moves only `test_scrollbar_*` methods; the two method sets do not
overlap and neither entry edits the other's invariants rows, though both edit
`tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` and `docs/invariants.md`). At implementation
re-grep every anchor this entry names. No stylesheet or production behavior
changes.

**Approach and files.**
- Create `tests/test_gtk4_switch.py` with
  `class TestGtk4Switch(Gtk4SheetRuleCases, unittest.TestCase)` and a one-line
  module docstring on the landed extraction modules' pattern. Move every
  `TestGtk4Theme` method whose name starts with `test_switch_` plus the bare
  `test_switch`, keeping each method's body and docstring unchanged:
  `test_switch`, `test_switch_osd_checked_track_color`,
  `test_switch_track_transition`, `test_switch_focus_outline_color`,
  `test_switch_interaction_track_faces`, `test_switch_checked_thumb_face`,
  `test_switch_interaction_thumb_face`, `test_switch_disabled_filter` and
  `test_switch_track_padding`. The first eight are contiguous in the file
  between `test_levelbar_directional_block_corners` and
  `test_tabbar_backdrop_filter`, which stay; `test_switch_track_padding` sits
  later between `test_tabgrid_card_focus` and `test_toggle_group_corners`,
  which stay. No other method shares the prefix; method names that only
  contain `switch` mid-name (none at this plan's base commit) stay. The landed
  GTK 3 switch checks live in `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` and stay
  there. Never import `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` or inherit `TestGtk4Theme`.
- The new module imports exactly the names the moved bodies use: `WHITE`
  from `support.platinum_palette` (the source module
  `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`'s import block draws it from). Every assertion
  helper the bodies call comes with `Gtk4SheetRuleCases` and its base classes:
  `assert_rule` and `assert_switch` on `support.gtk_rule_cases.py`'s
  `GtkSheetRuleCases`, and `assert_scale_focus_outline` on
  `tests/support/gtk4_sheet.py` (grep-checked at this plan's base commit);
  the `self.rules` and `self.selectors` attributes come the same way, and the
  moved bodies call no other support name (no `gtk_css`, `parse_css`, `HEX`,
  mock, tempfile, symlink helper or `re` use). `WHITE` is still referenced by
  `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` after the move (whole-file count 6 vs the moved
  body's 1), so its import block needs no change.
- In `docs/invariants.md`, rewrite each dotted anchor
  `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_switch…` to
  `tests/test_gtk4_switch.py::TestGtk4Switch::test_switch…` (`grep -o
  'TestGtk4Theme::test_switch[a-z_]*' docs/invariants.md` finds eleven member
  mentions on nine rows at this plan's base commit — `test_switch` and
  `test_switch_osd_checked_track_color` each appear twice). On the rows that
  also name members staying in `TestGtk4Theme` (the shared OSD container row
  names `test_video_osd_image_corners`, `test_progressbar_osd_trough_paint`,
  `test_progressbar_osd_trough_thickness` and `test_infobar`) rewrite only the
  `test_switch*` members and leave the others and the row prose alone. Do not
  rewrite history in PLANS-DONE.md or BUGS-FIXED.md.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unittest discovery lists each of the nine moved methods exactly once, under
  `test_gtk4_switch.TestGtk4Switch`, and none of them under
  `test_gtk4_theme.TestGtk4Theme`. Every other `TestGtk4Theme` method is still
  listed there.
- For each moved method, the AST of its function definition is identical to
  the original's at this plan's base commit, checked once during the run (for
  example by comparing `ast.dump` output). This is a run-time check, not a new
  committed test.
- `grep -n 'TestGtk4Theme::test_switch' docs/invariants.md` prints nothing,
  every staying member on the shared rows still reads its original module, and
  the invariants checker inside `make check` resolves every new anchor.
- `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` shrinks by at least 45 lines, and
  `tests/test_gtk4_switch.py` stays under about 250 lines.
- `git diff --stat` touches only `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`,
  `tests/test_gtk4_switch.py` and `docs/invariants.md`. `make check` passes
  after the final edit.

### GTK 4 suite extraction: isolate entry declarations (planned 2026-11-12 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-12 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` is still about 4,900 lines in one `TestGtk4Theme`
class. That breaks the principle that a file is small enough to read in one sitting.
Move the five `test_entry_*` declaration checks (about 140 lines at this plan's base
commit) into their own module, the same way the landed OSD (`tests/test_gtk4_osd.py`)
and scale (`tests/test_gtk4_scale.py`) parts moved theirs. This is independent of
"README split, part 5/5" (that entry moves user-facing prose) and of the two waiting
"GTK 4 suite extraction: isolate spinbutton declarations" and "… isolate emoji
declarations" entries (those move only `test_spinbutton_*` and `test_emoji_*`
methods; no method set overlaps and neither entry edits this entry's invariants
rows). This is the one extraction entry that prunes a `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`
import, so at implementation re-grep every anchor and every constant this entry
names. No stylesheet or production behavior changes.

**Approach and files.**
- Create `tests/test_gtk4_entry.py` with
  `class TestGtk4Entry(Gtk4SheetRuleCases, unittest.TestCase)` and a one-line
  module docstring (model it on `tests/test_gtk4_scale.py`). Move every
  `TestGtk4Theme` method whose name starts with `test_entry_` into it, keeping
  each method's body and comments unchanged: `test_entry_focus_outline_color`,
  `test_entry_focus_transition`, `test_entry_colour_classes`,
  `test_entry_image_inks` and `test_entry_progress`. Entry-named methods that do
  not start with `test_entry_` stay where they are: `test_flat_entry_fields`,
  `test_treeview_entry_fields` and `test_caps_lock_indicator` (plus the spin
  field methods the spinbutton plan already scoped out). `test_label_error_colour_class`
  stays in `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`: the label colour-class row keeps its
  anchor to it and only swaps this entry's member.
- The new module imports exactly the names the moved bodies use:
  `ENTRY_PROGRESS_GTK4` from `support.gtk_theme_spec` and `BLACK` from
  `support.platinum_palette`. Every assertion helper the bodies call
  (`assert_rule`, `assert_rule_after`, `assert_exact_rule_once`,
  `assert_scale_focus_outline`, `assert_scale_slider_transition`) and the
  `self.rules`/`self.selectors` attributes come with `Gtk4SheetRuleCases` and its
  base classes (grep-checked at this plan's base commit: all five helpers are
  defined in `tests/support/gtk4_sheet.py` or `tests/support/gtk_rule_cases.py`).
  The moved bodies call no other support name (no `gtk_css`, `strip_comments`,
  `parse_css`, `HEX`, mock, tempfile or `re` use), and no other constant:
  unlike the spinbutton and emoji extractions, this move empties one import —
  `grep -n 'ENTRY_PROGRESS_GTK4' tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` at this plan's base
  commit prints only the import and the one moved use in `test_entry_progress` —
  so prune `ENTRY_PROGRESS_GTK4` from `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`'s
  `support.gtk_theme_spec` import in the same change and import it in the new
  module. `BLACK` stays in `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`'s import block: the whole
  file still far out-references the moved bodies' five uses. Never import
  `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` or inherit `TestGtk4Theme`.
- In `docs/invariants.md`, rewrite each dotted anchor
  `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_entry_…` to
  `tests/test_gtk4_entry.py::TestGtk4Entry::test_entry_…` (`grep -n
  'TestGtk4Theme::test_entry' docs/invariants.md` finds six anchors across five
  rows at this plan's base commit: the focus-outline row, the focus-transition
  row, the entry-progress row, the entry colour-class row, the label colour-class
  row and the entry-icon-ink row). In the entry-progress row rewrite only the
  GTK 4 member and leave its two GTK 3 `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`
  anchors and the row's prose alone; in the label colour-class row rewrite only
  this entry's member and leave the `test_label_error_colour_class` anchor alone.
  Do not rewrite history in PLANS-DONE.md or BUGS-FIXED.md.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unittest discovery lists each of the five moved methods exactly once, under
  `test_gtk4_entry.TestGtk4Entry`, and none of them under
  `test_gtk4_theme.TestGtk4Theme`. Every other `TestGtk4Theme` method is still
  listed there, including `test_flat_entry_fields`, `test_treeview_entry_fields`,
  `test_caps_lock_indicator` and `test_label_error_colour_class`.
- For each moved method, the AST of its function definition is identical to the
  original's at this plan's base commit, checked once during the run (for example
  by comparing `ast.dump` output). This is a run-time check, not a new committed
  test.
- `grep -n 'TestGtk4Theme::test_entry' docs/invariants.md` prints nothing, and
  the invariants checker inside `make check` resolves every new anchor; the
  progress row's GTK 3 anchors and the label row's `test_label_error_colour_class`
  anchor are still present and resolve.
- `grep -n 'ENTRY_PROGRESS_GTK4' tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` prints nothing.
- `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` shrinks by at least 130 lines, and
  `tests/test_gtk4_entry.py` stays under about 300 lines.
- `git diff --stat` touches only `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`,
  `tests/test_gtk4_entry.py` and `docs/invariants.md`. `make check` passes after
  the final edit.

search directories; ground these platform keys against upstream Konsole source and
record the source/version in the installation guide. Write only `[Appearance] Font`,
using part 2/3's exact QFont value and the existing bounded `run_required`/`kwriteconfig6`
command pattern. For a profile in a system data directory, first copy it to the user's

`Parent=FALLBACK/` and the font, then select that filename in `konsolerc`. Refuse unsafe
profile names (absolute paths, separators or traversal), symlink destinations and an
unresolvable explicitly named profile, with an actionable diagnostic rather than guessing.

profile's font; uninstall continues to preserve user configuration. Update

opening a window in the user's session. Keep this run to the helper, wiring, tests and

### README split, part 1/5: let the README tests follow links into docs/ guides (planned 2026-11-12 by the director role) — done 2026-11-12 by the feature role

**Goal.** On 2026-11-12 the user asked to shorten README.md (1,934 lines) by moving its longest sections into separate markdown files and linking to them. Parts 2/5–5/5 each move one section into a `docs/<topic>.md` guide. About a dozen tests read README.md text and would fail or quietly lose coverage once that text moves. This part adds the shared reader those parts retarget to, and it extends the link checker across files. It moves no prose.

**Approach.**
- New `tests/support/user_docs.py`:
  - `linked_guides(readme_text) -> list[str]` returns the repo-relative `docs/*.md` paths that README's inline links point at (`](docs/<name>.md)` or `](docs/<name>.md#frag)`, outside fenced code), deduplicated, in first-seen order.
  - `read_user_docs() -> str` returns README.md's text followed by each linked guide's text, joined with `"\n\n"`. Every read goes through `containment.read_text(path, ROOT, encoding="utf-8")`, the same guard the README readers use.
  - The corpus is whatever README links to, so a guide joins it when README links it. A guide that README does not link is not user documentation. README links neither `docs/invariants.md` nor `docs/principles-rationale.md` today, so they stay out.
- `tests/test_readme_links.py`:
  - Keep `local_link_errors` for same-document `(#frag)` links. Run it on README and on each linked guide.
  - Add `cross_file_link_errors(source_path, text)`. It resolves `](<relpath>.md#frag)` and `](<relpath>.md)` targets relative to the source file and returns a target in either of two cases: the file does not exist, or the fragment matches no heading slug or explicit anchor in that file. Reuse the existing `_slug`/heading/anchor logic: refactor its destination collection into a helper that both functions call, without changing current results. Ignore links with a URL scheme.
  - Apply it to README → guide links and to guide → `../README.md#frag` links.
- `docs/invariants.md`: update the `tests/test_readme_links.py::TestReadmeLinks` row. It now says "no network or cross-file validation"; make it describe the cross-file check over README and its linked guides.

**Files.** `tests/support/user_docs.py` (new), `tests/test_readme_links.py`, a new `tests/test_user_docs.py` (or new cases in `tests/test_readme_links.py`), `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In unit tests on temporary files, `linked_guides` returns a linked guide once for text that links it twice, once bare and once with a fragment (the fixtures name the real `docs/principles-rationale.md` and `docs/invariants.md` rather than hypothetical guides). It ignores a link inside a fenced code block and links with a URL scheme (`https://example.com/elsewhere/b.md`, `mailto:`).
- `cross_file_link_errors` reports a link to a missing file, and a link whose fragment matches no heading in an existing file. It reports nothing for a link whose fragment matches a heading slug.
- `read_user_docs()` on the current tree equals README.md's text, because README links no guide yet. A symlinked guide that escapes the repository is refused, like the existing README containment tests.
- README.md is unchanged. `make check` passes after the final edit.

### Antialiased text and hand cursors: draw the I-beam and pointing hand as vector art (planned 2026-11-12 by the plan role; "requires Antialiased cursors part 3/3 landed") — done 2026-11-12 by the feature role

**Goal.** This is the next cursor family the BUGS.md cursor report routes: the text I-beam (`xterm`, aliases `text` and `ibeam`) and the pointing hand (`hand2`, aliases `hand1`, `pointer` and `pointing_hand`). They are the cursors users see most after the arrow. Redraw both as smooth, original, antialiased vector art, rendered natively at 16, 24 and 32 through the `VectorCursor` path that part 2/3 adds to `tools/make_cursors.py`. This entry adds no generator change.

**Approach.**
- **Art.** In `tools/cursor_art_pointers.py`, replace `XTERM_GRID` and `HAND2_GRID` with `XTERM_ART` and `HAND2_ART`. Both are `VectorCursor(face=…, outline_width=2, design_size=32)`. Set `XTERM_HOTSPOT = (15, 15)` and `HAND2_HOTSPOT = (14, 4)` in design units. Delete the two grids: they are bound only in `tools/cursor_art.py` (checked with grep), and no other grid reuses their cells. Rewrite their comments. These polygons are the design decision, listed in order:
  - I-beam: `(10,4) (20,4) (20,6) (16,6) (16,26) (20,26) (20,28) (10,28) (10,26) (14,26) (14,6) (10,6)`. The stem is 2 units wide, with serifs 10 units wide, and the shape is symmetric about x=15. The stem edges fall on pixel boundaries at 16 and 32, so it stays crisp there.
  - Hand: `(13,3) (15,3) (16,5) (16,12) (17,11) (19,11) (20,12) (21,11.5) (23,12) (24,14) (24,24) (21,28) (12,28) (9,25) (9,21) (6.5,17) (6.5,15.5) (8,14.5) (12,17) (12,5)`. This is a raised index finger 4 units wide, with knuckle bumps along the palm top, a thumb on the left and a rounded heel. The implementer may move a vertex by at most 1 unit, and only to satisfy a criterion below.
- **Binding.** In `tools/cursor_art.py`, import the two `*_ART` constants and bind `xterm` and `hand2` to them with the same aliases. Update the module docstring to say these two are also antialiased vector art.
- **Regenerate** with `python3 tools/make_cursors.py`.
- **Tests.**
  - `tests/test_cursors_theme.py`:
    - Update `HOTSPOTS` for both cursors to the values below.
    - Move `xterm` and `hand2` out of the grid-cell `PINNED_PIXELS` check into the per-size vector pins below. Use the same mechanism part 3/3 uses for `left_ptr`; if part 3/3 kept `left_ptr` in `PINNED_PIXELS` some other way, follow that shape.
    - In every `cursor_art.CURSORS`-wide test, treat both entries the same way part 3/3 treats the `left_ptr` vector entry: the corrupted-glyph variant, the shield-grid check and the differs-from-arrow check.
    - Add one test per cursor for the criteria below.
  - `tests/test_cursor_art_bindings.py`: the two `*_ART` constants pair with their `*_HOTSPOT` constants, under the rule part 3/3 added.
  - `docs/invariants.md`: update the cursor-set row and the hotspot row so they list `xterm` and `hand2` as vector-rendered.

**Files.** `tools/cursor_art_pointers.py`, `tools/cursor_art.py`, `tests/test_cursors_theme.py`, `tests/test_cursor_art_bindings.py`, `docs/invariants.md`, and the seven regenerated files `xterm`, `text`, `ibeam`, `hand2`, `hand1`, `pointer` and `pointing_hand` under `theme/icons/org.macos8.desktop/cursors/`.

**Acceptance criteria.** The values below are measured from the planned polygons with `tools/cursor_vector.py` on main. Tests derive their expectations from the design coordinates, not from the rendered output.
- **xterm.** The committed `xterm` parses to frames at 16, 24 and 32 with hotspots `(7,7)`, `(11,11)` and `(15,15)`. In each frame:
  - The hotspot pixel and the pixel containing design point `(15,15)` are `(0,0,0,255)`.
  - The pixel containing design point `(17,15)` is `(255,255,255,255)`: that is `(8,7)`, `(12,11)` and `(17,15)`.
  - All four corners are `(0,0,0,0)`.
  - At least one pixel has alpha strictly between 0 and 255.
  - The 24-pixel frame also has an opaque pixel with a channel strictly between 0 and 255, where the stem edge falls inside a pixel.
- **hand2.** The committed `hand2` parses to frames at 16, 24 and 32 with hotspots `(7,2)`, `(10,3)` and `(14,4)`. In each frame:
  - The hotspot pixel has alpha 255.
  - The pixel containing design point `(14,8)` (the finger) is `(0,0,0,255)`.
  - The pixel containing design point `(17,7)` (the outline beside the finger) is `(255,255,255,255)`.
  - All four corners are `(0,0,0,0)`.
  - At least one pixel has alpha strictly between 0 and 255, and at least one opaque pixel has a channel strictly between 0 and 255.
- **Freshness and aliases.** Each committed canonical file equals `make_cursors.cursor_bytes` for its entry, and each alias is byte-identical to its canonical file. A moved face vertex, a dropped size or a moved hotspot each change the bytes.
- **Scope.** `git diff --stat` touches no cursor file outside the seven listed above.
- `make check` passes after the final edit. This change does not close the BUGS.md cursor report. The remaining families are watch; help, progress and context-menu; resize, fleur and crosshair; and drag, grab and not-allowed. Each will get its own entry.

### Antialiased cursors, part 2/3: render VectorCursor art in the cursor generator and define the arrow design (planned 2026-11-12 by the plan role; split from part 2/2 2026-11-12 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-12 by the feature role

Nothing is bound or regenerated here: every committed cursor file keeps its bytes. Part 3/3 binds the arrow and regenerates `left_ptr`. **Approach.**
- **Arrow art.** In `tools/cursor_art_pointers.py`, add `ARROW_ART = VectorCursor(face=…, outline_width=2, design_size=32)` and `ARROW_HOTSPOT = (3, 3)` (design units), with a comment that this is this theme's own original outline. The face is this polygon, in order: tip `(3,3)`, down the vertical left edge to `(3,24)`, notch `(8,19.5)`, tail `(12,28)`, `(15,26.6)`, inner notch `(11.2,18.5)`, wing `(18,18.5)`, then back to the tip. - **Tests.** In `tests/test_make_cursors.py`, add a test class for the vector path. Parse output with the `support.xcursor` reader the file already imports. Expected values come from the design coordinates scaled by `size/32`, not from rendered output.

  - The top-right `(size-1,0)` and bottom-right `(size-1,size-1)` pixels are `(0,0,0,0)`.
  - At least one pixel has alpha strictly between 0 and 255, and at least one opaque pixel has a channel strictly between 0 and 255. This is the antialiasing evidence.

### Antialiased cursors, part 1/2: a stdlib polygon rasterizer for vector cursor art (planned 2026-11-12 by the plan role; independent of the waiting README chooser plan) — done 2026-11-12 by the feature role

**Goal.** On 2026-11-12 the user chose smoother original cursor artwork with antialiased contours (QUESTIONS.md, "What direction should replace the disliked cursor artwork?", Option 2). That answers the direction fork recorded in the BUGS.md report "Cursor artwork is still visually unacceptable to the user". Today `tools/make_cursors.py::render_rgba` can only enlarge a 16×16 cell grid with nearest-neighbour sampling, so it cannot draw a smooth contour. This part adds the renderer. Part 2/2 draws the arrow with it. Each later cursor family gets its own plan.

**Approach.** Add a new module `tools/cursor_vector.py`. Use the standard library only and the same `if __package__:` import pattern as `tools/cursor_art.py`. It defines:
- `VectorCursor`, a frozen (hashable) dataclass with these fields:
  - `face`: a tuple of at least three `(x, y)` vertices of one simple polygon, in design units.
  - `outline_width`: a non-negative number of design units.
  - `design_size`: a positive int, default 32.
  `VectorCursor.__post_init__` raises `ValueError` in these cases, naming the field: fewer than three vertices, a non-numeric coordinate, a coordinate outside `0..design_size`, a negative width, or a design size that is not a positive int (bool is refused, as `tools/ints.py::is_plain_int` does).
- `render_vector_rgba(art, size, samples=4)` returns `size*size*4` straight (non-premultiplied) RGBA bytes. `tools/xcursor.py::write_rgba_cursor` premultiplies them itself. Each pixel takes `samples×samples` sub-samples at the centres `(px + (i+0.5)/samples, py + (j+0.5)/samples)`, scaled by `design_size/size` into design units. Each sample is classified as follows:
  - Inside `face` under the even-odd rule: black face.
  - Otherwise, within `outline_width` (`<=`) of the nearest face edge segment: white outline.
  - Otherwise: empty.
  Let `B` and `W` be the black and white counts, `N = samples²` and `K = B + W`. A pixel with `K == 0` is `(0, 0, 0, 0)`. Otherwise it is `(g, g, g, a)` with `a = (510*K + N) // (2*N)` and `g = (510*W + K) // (2*K)`; both are integer round-half-up. The colours match the pinned `PIXELS` face `#000000` and outline `#FFFFFF` in `tools/cursor_art.py`. Validate `size` with the same rule and messages as `tools/make_cursors.py::_checked_size`. Move that helper into this module, or have both modules share it, so the limit `MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` stays the single bound.
- `vector_hotspot(hotspot, art, size)` returns `(min(floor(hx*size/design_size), size-1), …)` for a design-unit hotspot. It raises `ValueError` when the hotspot is not two numbers in `[0, design_size)`.

The module docstring records the provenance. No reference screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a pointer. The antialiased style comes from the user's 2026-11-12 answer, and the black face and white outline are the set's pinned palette. Each nominal size is rendered natively from vectors, so no shipped frame is resampled from another frame. Nothing calls this module yet, so no shipped cursor changes in this part.

**Files.** New `tools/cursor_vector.py` and `tests/test_cursor_vector.py` (unittest, matching the existing `tests/test_make_cursors.py` style). If `_checked_size` moves, edit `tools/make_cursors.py` only for the import. Add one row to `docs/invariants.md` for the rasterizer's coverage and rounding contract, anchored to the new tests.

**Acceptance criteria.** All expected values are worked out by hand from the geometry below, not taken from the code's output.
- Square face `(8,8),(24,8),(24,24),(8,24)`, `outline_width=0`, `design_size=32`, at size 32: every pixel with `8 <= x,y <= 23` is `(0,0,0,255)`, and every other pixel is `(0,0,0,0)`. At size 16 the opaque black block is exactly `4 <= x,y <= 11`.
- Face `(8,8),(24.5,8),(24.5,24),(8,24)`, width 0, size 32: pixel `(24,16)` is `(0,0,0,128)` because half its samples are inside.
- The same face with `outline_width=2`, size 32:
  - Pixel `(24,16)` is `(128,128,128,255)`: half face, half outline.
  - Pixels `(6,16)` and `(7,16)` are `(255,255,255,255)`.
  - Pixel `(5,16)` is `(0,0,0,0)`.
  - Corner pixel `(6,6)` is white with alpha strictly between 0 and 255.
- `vector_hotspot((3,3), art32, s)` gives `(1,1)`, `(2,2)` and `(3,3)` for `s` = 16, 24 and 32. `(31.9,31.9)` at 16 gives `(15,15)`.
- Each invalid `VectorCursor` field, size and hotspot named above raises `ValueError` whose message names the field. Two renders of the same input are byte-identical, and their length is `size*size*4`.
- No file under `theme/` changes, and `make check` passes after the final edit.

**Goal and grounding.** Give the file chooser's breadcrumb buttons the landed black keyboard-focus colour. - `filechooser #pathbarbox > stack > box > button:focus:focus-visible`
- `filechooser #pathbarbox > stack > box > box > button:focus:focus-visible`
- `filechooser #pathbarbox > stack > box > menubutton > button:focus:focus-visible`

Their ID-qualified specificity outranks the shipped `button:focus:focus-visible` colour. The corresponding `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css` resource in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-4.so.1` has no `pathbar` focus-visible arm. Searches of the shipped GTK 4 sheet, its tests, PLANS.md, PLANS-DONE.md and the invariant register found no `pathbarbox` treatment. The landed `pathbar > scrolledwindow > viewport` recipe targets a different node hierarchy. No collected reference shows GTK file-chooser breadcrumb focus; black is a platform adaptation reusing the landed generic button focus policy.

**Approach and files.** Append one grouped rule with exactly the three selectors above and only `outline-color: #000000` to `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`. Use a dated adaptation comment naming the missing reference surface and reused button focus colour; keep the library name out of CSS comments because `TestGtk4Theme::test_stands_alone` rejects it. For each exact selector, assert its complete parsed dictionary equals `{"outline-color": BLACK}`, its count in `self.selectors` is one, and its colour equals the generic button focus colour. Assert the set of parsed selectors containing `pathbarbox` equals these three spellings. Add a dated row under `## gtk` in `docs/invariants.md` linking this test, recording the full resource probe above, missing reference surface, chosen colour's source and user-import scope. Limit implementation to these three files; GTK 3, toolbar focus and breadcrumb face geometry are outside this plan.

**Acceptance criteria.** The shipped stylesheet declares opaque black once for each of the three exact breadcrumb keyboard-focus arms, with no width or offset declaration in those rules. The new test fails if a selector is omitted or renamed, an accent colour is substituted, an extra declaration is added, or another `pathbarbox` spelling appears. ### Fidelity CLI: offer a quiet verdict mode for scripted gates (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** Let shell callers compare screenshots for their exit status without printing a successful or failed comparison report. Source searches found no quiet option in the fidelity CLI and no planned or archived quiet-mode entry. This is independent of the waiting GTK suite split and the push-button retirement being handled on the pending plan branch.

**Approach and files.** In `tools/fidelity_cli_parser.py::build_parser`, make `--json` and a new `--quiet` boolean mutually exclusive output choices. In `tools/fidelity.py::main`, return the computed budget verdict before constructing/rendering the report when quiet is selected, after the existing image reads, comparison and option validation. Keep diagnostic flags legal with quiet: they retain their validation but produce no report. Do not introduce a separate comparison path or change budget calculations. Add `tests/test_fidelity_quiet.py` using `support.fidelity_cli_case.FidelityCliTestCase` and its PNG fixtures; update `tests/test_fidelity_cli_parser.py` for the parser's new default and help text; document the option in README.md's Fidelity checking section and append its guarantee to `docs/invariants.md`'s tooling table. The change touches these six files and stays within a few hundred lines including tests.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- Given identical 1x1 RGB PNGs, `--quiet` returns 0 with empty stdout and stderr. Given pixels (0,0,0) and (1,0,0), it returns 1 by default and 0 with `--tolerance 1`, with empty stdout and stderr in both cases. These fixtures distinguish quiet reporting from accidentally forcing success.
- Given a missing input or malformed PNG with `--quiet`, the CLI retains its normal error status and a nonempty stderr diagnostic, with empty stdout. Quiet does not hide usage errors: `--quiet --json` fails argument parsing before attempting to open missing input paths, in either flag order.
- Quiet with a valid diagnostic option such as `--difference-rows` still yields empty stdout and the correct comparison status; an invalid dependent-option combination still reports a usage error. Without quiet, existing text and JSON reports retain their tested behavior.
- A direct script invocation exercises the quiet option successfully; `make check` passes after the final edit. No GUI session or new dependency is needed.

### Platinum GTK 4 scrollbar: pin the rendered trough band, thumb face and raised thumb bevel with an offscreen pixel probe (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 4 push-button and GTK 4 slider probe entries — those entries add their own probes beside `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`'s landed rendered probes and append end-of-table `## gtk` rows to `docs/invariants.md`, while this entry adds its own probe beside the same probes and appends one end-of-table `## gtk` row to the same table — the three share no test method, no pinned widget and no README sentence, though all touch `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`'s rendered-probe region and `docs/invariants.md`'s `## gtk` table tail, so whichever merges later re-reads the file's probe region and the table tail before writing; at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** The GTK 4 sheet's plain scrollbar recipe — `scrollbar > range > trough` (the `#EEEEEE` band, 1px `#000000` border, `border-radius: 0`, `transition: none`) and `scrollbar > range > trough > slider` (the `#DDDDDD` thumb face, `background-image: none`, 1px `#000000` border, zero radius, `margin: 0`, 12px minima, the raised `inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #999999` bevel) — is pinned today only by declaration checks (`tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_scrollbar` and its neighbours `test_scrollbar_ordinary_trough_margins`, `test_scrollbar_overlay_*`, `test_scrollbar_disabled_thumb_opacity`, `test_scrollbar_fine_tune_thumb_face`). A GTK-side regression — a trough or slider rule that never matches the rendered node tree, a thumb that never paints or loses its bevel, stock's beige trough or rounded thumb leaking through — would ship green, unlike the GTK 4 progress meter whose rendered probe (`test_progressbar_faces_render`) already pins pixels. The suite's landed GTK 4 rendered probes (`test_mixed_indicators_draw_black_dashes`, `test_spin_field_renders_the_mirrored_etch_in_rtl`, `test_notebook_tab_faces_render`, `test_progressbar_faces_render`) prove the child-interpreter route works, and no rendered probe of a `Gtk.Scrollbar` exists (a grep over the file finds no scrollbar construction in any child program), and a grep of PLANS.md and PLANS-DONE.md finds no entry carrying one.

**Approach and files.**

1. `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`: add `TestGtk4Theme::test_scrollbar_faces_render` beside `test_progressbar_faces_render`, the landed meter probe's shape: `require_gui_opt_in()` first (`tests/support/gui_tests.py`), then a child interpreter subprocess with `GDK_BACKEND=x11` and `GSK_RENDERER=cairo` that imports `gi` with `Gtk` 4.0 (exit 77 when introspection or an X11 display is missing, mapped by the parent to a skip naming what is missing), loads the shipped sheet's bytes into a `Gtk.CssProvider` at priority 801 with the `'../assets/'` URL rewrite the landed probes use, sets the stock theme name to Adwaita the way the mixed-indicator probe does, then builds a `Gtk.Window` holding two vertical `Gtk.Scrollbar`s built from `Gtk.Adjustment.new(0, 0, 100, 1, 10, 50)` with `set_size_request(24, 120)` — one resting, the second wrapped in a `set_sensitive(False)` holder so the `:disabled` state propagates the way the meter probe's disabled bar does — pumps the main context until both are allocated, asserts the widget and node css names `scrollbar`/`range`/`trough`/`slider` and that the resting scrollbar carries no `overlay-indicator` style class (a standalone scrollbar built outside a scrolled window takes no overlay class, so the plain recipe is what the probe pins), snapshots each scrollbar with `Gtk.WidgetPaintable` at the widget's own allocation, renders it through `renderer.render_texture` into a pixbuf with the same deadline loop and failure reporting as the meter probe, and asserts each pinned pixel as a literal tuple at positions derived from the fresh trough and slider allocations (the child program reads their `get_allocated_width()/get_allocated_height()` plus `get_allocation()` origins and computes every coordinate from those, exactly as the meter probe derives its pins). The plan states no absolute coordinates. Pin, per resting scrollbar, each position clear of antialiasing edges: the thumb interior centre expecting the `#DDDDDD` face, the thumb's top border row expecting `#000000`, the thumb's top interior row expecting the `#FFFFFF` bevel arm, the thumb's bottom interior row expecting the `#999999` bevel arm, a trough interior row above the thumb and one below the thumb each expecting `#EEEEEE` (stock's beige trough fill or a leaked gradient fails either side), and the trough's left border column expecting `#000000`. The disabled scrollbar repeats the trough band, trough border and thumb face pins — the landed `scrollbar > range > trough > slider:disabled` group keeps `opacity: 1`, so the disabled thumb's interior must still read opaque `#DDDDDD`, and any state fade or repaint leaves a pinned pixel wrong and fails. Every expectation comes from the landed recipe and the palette constants already imported in `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` (`FACE`, `BLACK`, `WHITE`, `GREY`, `TROUGH` — re-grep the import list before writing and add only what is missing), never from a capture's own pixels. The pressed and fine-tune states stay out: the landed `slider:hover, slider:active` and `range.fine-tune` groups repaint the same `#DDDDDD` face and raised bevel as the resting thumb, so those pins would be byte-identical and add nothing discriminating — the declaration tests hold the spellings. Overlay scrollbars stay out: the probe builds no scrolled window and no overlay-indicator widget; the landed overlay groups restate the same faces, and `test_scrollbar_overlay_*` holds their margins, breadths and outline. The probe imports no GTK in the suite process (the `tests/test_no_gtk_introspection.py` guard pins that) and mentions no brand or toolkit name.
2. `docs/invariants.md`: append one dated (2026-11-11) end-of-table `## gtk` row naming the new probe: a plain vertical GTK 4 scrollbar paints the landed `#EEEEEE` trough band with its `#000000` border and the raised `#DDDDDD` thumb with its black rim and white/`#999999` bevel, the disabled thumb keeping the landed opaque face; recording the missing reference surface (no collected screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a GTK scrollbar — the GTK scope's standing adaptation premise), the value sources (the sheet's landed `scrollbar > range > trough` and `scrollbar > range > trough > slider` groups and the platinum palette constants), and that the probe runs under the opt-in guard through the child interpreter, establishing rendered pixels only where GTK 4 introspection and an X display are present, as the landed declaration rows never have.

**Files.** `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` (one probe beside the landed rendered probes), `docs/invariants.md` (one appended end-of-table `## gtk` row). No sheet change, no production tool change, no render-harness change, and no other GTK 4 widget is touched.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `make check` stays green where GTK 4 probes are not runnable: without `PLATINUM_RUN_GUI_TESTS=1` the new probe raises the same skip as the landed probes, and where GTK 4 introspection or a display is missing despite the opt-in, the child exits 77 and the probe skips with its own reason — the hosted job keeps today's behavior.
- Where GTK 4 introspection and an X display are present with `PLATINUM_RUN_GUI_TESTS=1`, the child completes and every pinned pixel reads its literal tuple: the resting scrollbar's `#DDDDDD` thumb face, `#000000` thumb rim, `#FFFFFF` and `#999999` thumb bevel arms, `#EEEEEE` trough band above and below the thumb and `#000000` trough rim; the disabled scrollbar's unchanged trough band and rim and its still-opaque `#DDDDDD` thumb face. Deleting or weakening any landed scrollbar rule — the trough band, the trough rim, the thumb face, the thumb rim, a raised bevel arm, or the disabled twin's `opacity: 1` — changes at least one pinned pixel and fails the probe.
- The landed neighbouring probes (`test_progressbar_faces_render`, `test_notebook_tab_faces_render`, `test_spin_field_renders_the_mirrored_etch_in_rtl`, `test_mixed_indicators_draw_black_dashes`) and the scrollbar declaration tests (`test_scrollbar`, `test_scrollbar_ordinary_trough_margins`, the overlay-family tests, `test_scrollbar_disabled_thumb_opacity`, `test_scrollbar_fine_tune_thumb_face`) pass unchanged, the no-GTK-in-suite guard passes, and `make check` passes after the final edit.

**Implementation deviations (2026-11-11 by the feature role).** Three anchors moved at
implementation, all recorded in the probe and the invariants row. The value rides to 25 on the
plan-named `Gtk.Adjustment.new(0, 0, 100, 1, 10, 50)` adjustment (`adjustment.set_value(25)`;
`Gtk.Scrollbar` has no `set_value`), because at the resting value 0 the thumb sits against the
trough's top border and no interior row exists above it — with the value moved, a trough band
exists above and below the thumb and the plan's two band pins are pinnable. The child reads
`get_allocation()` rather than the entry's `get_allocated_width()`/`get_allocated_height()`
anchors — the landed spin, button and scale probes record the getters as deprecated and
margin-box-excluding, and the trough and slider allocations (plus the range child's) are what
the pins derive from. The probe sits after the landed `test_scale_faces_render` (the
rendered-probe region's tail) rather than beside `test_progressbar_faces_render`, matching the
slider entry's own landing beside the then-newest probe. Measured 2026-11-11 on this host by
running the probe's child program under an isolated headless Wayland session (no Xvfb
executable, so the shipped probe skipped here): two clean runs settled with every pin at its
literal tuple, and the six sheet mutations each failed the probe on the corresponding pin.

### Platinum GTK 4 push button: pin the rendered raised face, bevel and inverted active bevel with an offscreen pixel probe (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 4 progress-meter entry — that entry adds its `test_progressbar_faces_render` probe beside `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`'s landed rendered probes and appends one end-of-table `## gtk` row to `docs/invariants.md`, while this entry adds its own probe beside the same landed probes and appends one end-of-table `## gtk` row to the same table — the two share no test method, no pinned widget and no README sentence, though both touch `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`'s rendered-probe region and `docs/invariants.md`'s `## gtk` table tail, so whichever merges later re-reads the file's probe region and the table tail before writing; at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

1. `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`: add `TestGtk4Theme::test_button_faces_render` beside `test_notebook_tab_faces_render`, the landed probes' shape: `require_gui_opt_in()` first (`tests/support/gui_tests.py`), then a child interpreter subprocess with `GDK_BACKEND=x11` and `GSK_RENDERER=cairo` that imports `gi` with `Gtk` 4.0 (exit 77 when introspection or an X11 display is missing, mapped by the parent to a skip naming what is missing), loads the shipped sheet's bytes into a `Gtk.CssProvider` at priority 801 with the `'../assets/'` URL rewrite the landed probes use, sets the stock theme name to Adwaita the way the mixed-indicator probe does, then builds a `Gtk.Window` holding two childless `Gtk.Button`s at `set_size_request(24, 24)` with `set_focusable(False)` — no label child, so no glyph row becomes a fixture — the second carrying the pressed state (`set_state_flags(Gtk.StateFlags.ACTIVE, True)`), pumps the main context until both are allocated, snapshots each button with `Gtk.WidgetPaintable` at the button's own allocation, renders it through `renderer.render_texture` into a pixbuf with the same deadline loop and failure reporting as the mixed-indicator probe, and asserts each pinned pixel as a literal tuple at positions derived from the fresh allocations (the child program reads `button.get_allocated_width()/get_allocated_height()` and computes every coordinate from `w`/`h`, exactly as the spin probe derives its pins). **Files.** `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` (one probe beside the landed rendered probes), `docs/invariants.md` (one appended end-of-table `## gtk` row). No sheet change, no production tool change, no render-harness change, and no other GTK 4 widget is touched.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `make check` stays green where GTK 4 probes are not runnable: without `PLATINUM_RUN_GUI_TESTS=1` the new probe raises the same skip as the landed probes, and where GTK 4 introspection or a display is missing despite the opt-in, the child exits 77 and the probe skips with its own reason — the hosted job keeps today's behavior.
- Where GTK 4 introspection and an X display are present with `PLATINUM_RUN_GUI_TESTS=1`, the child completes and every pinned pixel reads its literal tuple: the resting button's `#DDDDDD` face, `#000000` border, `#FFFFFF` top arm and `#AAAAAA` bottom-right arm, and the pressed button's swapped arms with the same face and border. Deleting or weakening any landed button rule — the face, the border, a raised bevel arm, or the inverted active twin — changes at least one pinned pixel and fails the probe.

**Implementation deviations (2026-11-11 by the feature role).** Three anchors moved
at implementation, all recorded in the probe and the invariants row. The child reads
`get_allocation()` instead of the entry's `get_allocated_width()`/`get_allocated_height()`
anchors — those getters are deprecated and exclude the margin box, so the landed spin and
progressbar probes snapshot at the allocation, which on a plain button is its painted border
box 1:1 (verified against a window-level capture; the 24px size request still holds). The
pinned tuples are formatted into the child program from the suite's own imported palette
constants (`FACE`, `BLACK`, `WHITE` and the newly imported `BUTTON_SHADOW`) instead of being
hand-copied literals, so a palette change cannot desynchronize them. One exposure was found
while running the mutation checks: the child-interpreter probes inherit the running
environment, and a host that applies the theme's own user CSS (`~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`
importing the installed sheet) restates the plain-button recipe under the probe — deleting
the resting group's bevel left the pins passing until the checks ran with a clean
`HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` child, after which every mutation failed on the corresponding pin.
This exposure is shared by the landed child probes and is recorded in the new
`## gtk` row in `docs/invariants.md`.

### Platinum GTK 4 progress meter: pin the rendered trough, fill and disabled fill with an offscreen pixel probe (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of the waiting file-dialog content-faces part 2/2 — that entry extends `tests/test_render_surface.py`'s `TestFileDialogRender` beside its landed tests and edits README's `--file-dialog` paragraph and `docs/invariants.md`'s `## tooling` table, while this entry adds one probe to `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` beside its landed rendered probes and appends one end-of-table `## gtk` row to `docs/invariants.md` — the two share no test, no file region and no README sentence, so either merge order holds; at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** The GTK 4 sheet's plain meter recipe — `progressbar > trough` (the `#EEEEEE` face, 1px `#000000` border, `inset 1px 1px #999999` shadow arm, 10px minimums), `progressbar > trough > progress` (the `#CCCCFF` fill, margin 0) and the `progressbar > trough > progress:disabled` group (the `#999999` disabled fill) — is pinned today only by declaration checks (`tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_progressbar`, `::test_progressbar_disabled_filter`, `::test_disabled_meter_trough_faces`), and the `## gtk` invariants rows for the disabled-filter restatements say so explicitly: declaration coverage, not rendered-pixel evidence. A GTK-side regression — a trough rule that never matches the rendered node tree, a fill colour that never paints, the stock disabled `filter: Opacity(...)` surviving at higher specificity than the landed `filter: none` arm — would ship green, unlike the GTK 3 meter whose offscreen probe (`tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py::TestGtkThemeControls::test_progressbar_fill_spans_the_trough`) already pins rendered pixels. The suite's three landed GTK 4 rendered probes (`test_mixed_indicators_draw_black_dashes`, `test_spin_field_renders_the_mirrored_etch_in_rtl`, `test_notebook_tab_faces_render` in `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`) prove the route works; no rendered probe of a `Gtk.ProgressBar` exists (a grep over the file finds no `Gtk.ProgressBar` construction anywhere), and a grep of PLANS.md and PLANS-DONE.md finds no entry carrying it.

**Approach and files.**

1. `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`: add `TestGtk4Theme::test_progressbar_faces_render` beside `test_notebook_tab_faces_render`, the same shape: `require_gui_opt_in()` first (`tests/support/gui_tests.py`), then a child interpreter subprocess with `GDK_BACKEND=x11` and `GSK_RENDERER=cairo` that imports `gi` with `Gtk` 4.0 (exit 77 when introspection or an X11 display is missing, mapped by the parent to a skip naming what is missing), loads the shipped sheet's bytes into a `Gtk.CssProvider` at priority 801 with the `'../assets/'` URL rewrite the landed probes use, sets the stock theme name to Adwaita the way the notebook probe does, then builds a `Gtk.Window` holding one horizontal `Gtk.ProgressBar` at `set_fraction(0.5)` with `set_show_text(False)` — every pinned region sits clear of any text, so no font metric or glyph row becomes a fixture — plus a second bar at the same fraction whose parent carries the disabled state (`set_sensitive(False)`), pumps the main context until both bars are allocated, snapshots each bar's `trough` node (guarded with `assert trough.get_css_name() == "trough"`, the `progress` child likewise guarded, walking the node tree the way the landed probe guards its `header`) with `Gtk.WidgetPaintable`, renders it through `renderer.render_texture` into a pixbuf with the same deadline loop and failure reporting as the landed probe, and asserts each pinned pixel as a literal tuple at positions derived from the fresh node allocations (the trough node's allocation and the progress child's allocation), exactly as the notebook probe derives its tab positions. The plan states no absolute coordinates. Pin five discriminating bands, each derived so antialiasing edges stay clear: (a) one pixel inside the enabled bar's filled half's interior, away from every border and shadow arm, expecting `#CCCCFF` — so a lost or recoloured fill fails; (b) one pixel on the trough's top border row over the filled half, expecting `#000000` — so a lost trough border fails; (c) one pixel in the unfilled half just inside the top border, expecting the `#999999` inset shadow arm, and one pixel in the unfilled half's interior clear of the arm and borders, expecting the `#EEEEEE` trough face — so a dropped shadow arm or a recoloured face fails; (d) on the disabled bar, one pixel in its filled half's interior expecting `#999999` and one pixel in its unfilled half's interior expecting `#EEEEEE`, plus one pixel on its trough's top border row expecting full-strength `#000000` — so a restored stock translucency filter or a recoloured disabled fill fails; and (e) the relative pixel immediately below the enabled trough's bottom border row, outside the window, expecting the window's `#DDDDDD` surface — so a bar painting outside its bounds fails. Every expectation comes from the landed recipe and the palette constants already imported in `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` (`TROUGH`, `BLACK`, `SELECTION` and the greys read from `support.platinum_palette` — re-grep the import list before writing and add only what is missing), never from a capture's own pixels. The probe imports no GTK in the suite process (the `tests/test_no_gtk_introspection.py` guard pins that) and mentions no brand or toolkit name.
2. `docs/invariants.md`: append one dated (2026-11-11) end-of-table `## gtk` row naming the new probe: a GTK 4 plain meter paints the landed trough, fill and disabled fill; recording the missing reference surface (no collected screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a GTK meter — the GTK scope's standing adaptation premise), the value sources (the sheet's landed `progressbar > trough`, `progressbar > trough > progress` and `:disabled` groups and the platinum palette constants), and that the probe runs under the opt-in guard through the child interpreter, establishing rendered pixels only where GTK 4 introspection and an X display are present, as the landed declaration rows never have.

**Files.** `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` (one probe beside the landed rendered probes), `docs/invariants.md` (one appended end-of-table `## gtk` row). No sheet change, no production tool change, no render-harness change, and no other GTK 4 widget is touched.

**Implementation deviations (2026-11-11).** The probe snapshots each bar's own node at the bar's allocation instead of the trough node: the trough widget's allocation is its CSS `min-height` floor (10px on the measured build), smaller than its painted 12px border box, so a trough-node capture is vertically resampled and reads blended inks (the border's `#000000` read `#252525`); the bar's painted box equals its allocation, the trough fills it 1:1, and fill positions still derive from the progress child's allocation. And the disabled bar's dropped `filter: none` arm is pixel-invisible in the plain child — the cascade's only competing meter filter arm lives in the integration library's base.css resource (line 1860, recorded in the sheet), which a plain toolkit child never loads — so that spelling stays held by `test_progressbar_disabled_filter`, while the disabled faces are pinned full-strength.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `make check` stays green where GTK 4 probes are not runnable: without `PLATINUM_RUN_GUI_TESTS=1` the new probe raises the same skip as the landed probes, and where GTK 4 introspection or a display is missing despite the opt-in, the child exits 77 and the probe skips with its own reason — the hosted job keeps today's behavior.
- Where GTK 4 introspection and an X display are present with `PLATINUM_RUN_GUI_TESTS=1`, the child completes and every pinned pixel reads its literal tuple: the enabled fill `#CCCCFF` and trough border `#000000`, the unfilled half's `#999999` shadow arm over the `#EEEEEE` face, the disabled bar's `#999999` fill with opaque faces and its border still `#000000`, and the window surface outside the bar `#DDDDDD`. Deleting or weakening any landed meter rule — the fill rule, the trough face, the inset shadow arm, or the disabled `filter: none` arm letting the stock translucency filter back in — changes at least one pinned pixel and fails the probe.
- The landed neighbouring probes (`test_notebook_tab_faces_render`, `test_spin_field_renders_the_mirrored_etch_in_rtl`, `test_mixed_indicators_draw_black_dashes`) and the meter declaration tests (`test_progressbar`, `test_progressbar_disabled_filter`, `test_disabled_meter_trough_faces`) pass unchanged, the no-GTK-in-suite guard passes, and `make check` passes after the final edit.

### Splash render mode, part 1/2: plumb a `--splash` ksplashqml capture through the render CLI, workflow and Makefile (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of both waiting render-gate entries — the file-dialog part 2/2 gate appends a `_DialogGate` subclass and its gate-count words in `tests/test_render_surface.py`'s dialog tail, `README.md`'s `--file-dialog` paragraph and `docs/invariants.md`'s skip-guard row, while the applet face gate extends `TestRender` beside its landed strips, adds one sentence to `README.md`'s fidelity-checking gates paragraph and appends its `## tooling` row at the table's end; this entry edits `tools/render_surface.py`'s parser blocks directly beside `--desktop` and its preflight branch, `tools/render_clients.py`'s new client, `tools/render_workflow.py`'s `_client_command` and `render()` mode branches, the `Makefile`'s `RENDER_MODE_VALUES`/case/help narration, `README.md`'s prerequisites row, capture-enumeration prose and one command-table row, `tests/test_render_surface_units.py` beside its desktop cases, `tests/test_render_make.py`'s mode pin, `tests/test_render_surface.py`'s `TestFailurePaths`, `tests/test_ci_workflow.py`'s render-tool loop and one appended `## tooling` row — so no test method, production function or README paragraph is shared, though this entry and the applet face gate both append a row at the `## tooling` table's end, so whichever merges later re-reads the table before appending; at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names; the splash's pixel gate is a later part a later plan writes) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** The global theme ships a startup splash — `theme/look-and-feel/org.macos8.desktop/contents/splash/Splash.qml` with its placeholder `macos-logo.svg`, authored on the 240x180 grid of `macos8.6-screenshots/boot2_betawiki.png` and pinned by `tests/test_splash_qml.py`, `tests/test_splash_logo.py` and `tests/test_splash_reference.py` — but the fidelity workflow cannot capture it: `tools/render_surface.py` renders the calculator applet, the fourteen dialogs and the desktop menu bar, and no QML-structure check establishes rendered splash pixels (a runtime-only break — a missing image reference, a `unit` computation that collapses, a LayerShellQt surface the compositor never maps — passes every landed splash test). This part plumbs a `--splash` render mode that starts the themed splash in the headless KWin session and publishes a 640x400 fullscreen capture; its pixel gate is the later part. The splash's own placeholder asset keeps its `PLACEHOLDER:` marker and `PLACEHOLDERS.md` row — a render is measurement evidence, not a shipped-artifact change.

**Grounding (verified fresh 2026-11-11 by the plan role).** `ksplashqml` is installed on this host (`/usr/bin/ksplashqml`, `--help`: `Usage: ksplashqml [options] theme`, options `--test` (test mode), `--window` (windowed), `--nofork` (don't fork), `--pid`, positional `theme` — "Path to the theme to test"); an offscreen `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ksplashqml --test --nofork <look-and-feel package dir>` run exits 0 quickly, so the binary starts and returns, but offscreen cannot confirm paint. The session plumbing already supports a shell-only client: `tools/render_workflow.py::_client_command`'s `args.desktop` branch returns `["plasmashell"]`, `render()` writes `write_desktop_selection(session)` for it, and `tools/render_session.py::session_script` applies the color scheme, waits the settle, fails the session when the backgrounded client is dead at the settle (`"$1 exited before the capture"`), captures fullscreen with `spectacle -b -n -f -o` and reaps the client afterwards — so the splash client must stay alive at the settle, which is why `--nofork` (no forking parent exit) is required and why the probe below measures which argument shape survives. `make install` copies the look-and-feel package to `{XDG_DATA_HOME}/look-and-feel/org.macos8.desktop` (`INSTALL_FAMILIES` includes `look-and-feel`; the render session runs `make install` with `XDG_DATA_HOME={session.data}`, `tools/render_setup.py::install_theme`), so the client argument is a session-local path, deterministic and outside the caller's data home. The splash paints fullscreen on the nested compositor's layer shell, and the probe's virtual framebuffer is the 640x400 the desktop capture already fixes (`_DESKTOP_CAPTURE = (640, 400)`, `tools/render_surface.py`), so the splash capture is the same fixed size. `Splash.qml`'s field colour is the literal `"#63639C"` (`root.fieldColor`), so a painted capture is recognizably non-black and the probe can demand it.

**Approach.**

1. First probe the client on this host, inside a nested session shaped like the render CLI's own (`dbus-run-session` with a scratch `XDG_DATA_HOME` holding a `make install`-ed tree, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland`, KWin running, capture with `spectacle -b -n -f` after a settle): try `ksplashqml --nofork <scratch-data>/look-and-feel/org.macos8.desktop` (the primary shape), then, only if it exits before the settle or paints nothing, `--test --nofork` and `--window --nofork` with the same path. Require the chosen shape to (a) still be running at an 8 s settle and (b) produce a capture containing the `#63639C` splash field in a measurable region; record the chosen shape, the measured first-paint settle and the argument form that worked (the package directory path, versus a package id resolved through the data dirs) in the test comments added below. If no shape paints the splash in a bare nested session, stop — record the finding as a plan-defect note on this entry for the plan role instead of plumbing a mode that cannot paint. If the first paint misses the 8 s default, raise the splash settle default to the measured minimum plus margin (the `--desktop` precedent: `_DESKTOP_SETTLE = 30.0`) and record the re-derivation beside the constant.
2. `tools/render_surface.py`: add `_SPLASH_CAPTURE = (640, 400)` beside `_DESKTOP_CAPTURE`, and a `--splash` `store_true` argument directly after the `--desktop` one with help text naming the themed startup-splash capture and the fixed 640x400 size. Extend the validation with the desktop-shaped checks: `--splash` refuses every `--*-dialog` flag and `--desktop` with the landed one-conflict wording shape (`--splash renders the look-and-feel's own splash: do not combine it with <flag>`), refuses a non-default `--applet` and refuses `--width`/`--height` (`--splash captures at 640x400, the probe framebuffer size the later splash gate crops: do not combine it with --width/--height`); a splash run fixes `args.width, args.height = _SPLASH_CAPTURE`. Defaults: the applet's 8 s settle and 90 s timeout (`args.settle`/`args.timeout`'s mode ternaries gain the splash arm) unless step 1's probe raised the settle; the `--timeout must be longer than --settle` guard runs unchanged. Preflight: when `args.splash`, `requirements = REQUIRED_TOOLS + ("ksplashqml",)` so the missing-tool diagnostic names `ksplashqml`; no applet-package preflight (the splash opens no applet).
3. `tools/render_clients.py`: add `splash_client(session: Session) -> tuple[str, ...]` returning `("ksplashqml", "--nofork", str(session.data / "look-and-feel" / "org.macos8.desktop"))` (the shape step 1 chose; adjust the arguments there and record the choice) with a docstring naming what the gate renders — the look-and-feel package's own `Splash.qml` painted from the session's installed tree, never the caller's data home. Keep the id alongside `tools/render_setup.py`'s package ids the way the file's existing style does (import or comment, decided when writing).
4. `tools/render_workflow.py`: `_client_command` gains the splash branch beside the desktop one (`if args.splash: return list(splash_client(session))`, checked before the applet fallback); `render()` gains `splash = args.splash` beside `desktop = args.desktop` — session configs stay `CONFIG_FILES` for a splash run (the splash reads no selection), no Kvantum or GTK selection, no desktop selection, and no window-rules write.
5. `Makefile`: append `splash` to `RENDER_MODE_VALUES` and a `splash) set -- --splash ;;` arm to the case beside `desktop`; the `RENDER_MODE=name` help line's list derives from `RENDER_MODE_LIST`, so it moves unchanged.
6. Tests: `tests/test_render_make.py`'s `RENDER_MODE_VALUES` pin set and the flag-pairing table gain the splash entry. `tests/test_render_surface_units.py` gains cases beside the landed desktop ones: `--splash` delegates at the fixed 640x400 capture, refuses each conflicting option (`--desktop`, one dialog flag each, a non-default `--applet`, `--width`/`--height`) with the landed diagnostics' shape, carries the settle/timeout defaults overridable by explicit flags, names `ksplashqml` in the missing-tool diagnostic, and `--help` names the mode. `tests/test_render_surface.py`'s `TestFailurePaths` gains, modeled on the landed desktop ones: the splash render launches the `ksplashqml` client with the scratch-data package path, writes only the `CONFIG_FILES` session configs, runs no applet preflight and installs no Kvantum or GTK selection; the landed unpainted-capture and size-mismatch refusals cover the splash unchanged. `tests/test_ci_workflow.py`'s by-name tool loop gains `ksplashqml`, with its comment's tool count moved (seven→eight tools; the "five Plasma tools" wording moves likewise) — the CI image installs `plasma-workspace`, so no workflow install line changes; verify that reading the workflow before editing.
7. `README.md`: the prerequisites' "Render headlessly" row gains the splash clause (the splash render also needs `ksplashqml`); the `### Capturing a candidate` enumeration sentence gains "or the startup splash" after "or the desktop menu bar", the fixed-size/tool sentence gains the splash clause (`the splash capture is fixed at 640x400 and requires ksplashqml`), and the command table gains one row (`python3 tools/render_surface.py --splash splash.png`, 640x400). No `--file-dialog`/`--desktop` paragraph and no fidelity-checking paragraph edit.
8. `docs/invariants.md`: append one `## tooling` row recording the new mode: the client shape and argument the probe chose, the measured first-paint settle, the fixed 640x400 fullscreen capture basis (the probe framebuffer, the desktop capture's own basis), that the splash reads no selection (the client argument is the session-local installed package path), and that this plumbing pins no pixel (the splash gate is a later part).

**Files.** `tools/render_surface.py`, `tools/render_clients.py`, `tools/render_workflow.py`, `Makefile`, `README.md`, `docs/invariants.md`, `tests/test_render_surface_units.py`, `tests/test_render_surface.py`, `tests/test_render_make.py`, `tests/test_ci_workflow.py`. `tools/render_session.py`, `tools/render_setup.py` and `tools/render_dialogs.py` stay untouched: the session script, the install and the dialog table need no change for a shell-only client.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- On this host `python3 tools/render_surface.py --splash <scratch>/splash.png` exits 0 and publishes a 640x400 PNG of the themed startup splash (the probe's shape and settle), and the fresh probe's findings (client shape, argument form, first-paint settle) are recorded in the new tests' comments and the appended `## tooling` row.
- `--splash` refuses each conflicting option with the landed wording shape, keeps the `--timeout must be longer than --settle` guard, and a host missing `ksplashqml` refuses with exit 2 naming `ksplashqml` before any session; the unit and failure-path tests pin each behavior, and the landed desktop and dialog tests read back unchanged.
- `tests/test_render_make.py`'s pin covers the splash entry, `make render RENDER_MODE=splash RENDER_OUTPUT=<scratch>/splash.png` renders it, and `make check` passes after the final edit.
**Revision (2026-11-11 by the feature role, recorded with the done stamp).** Implementation notes the anchors missed: `make install` places the look-and-feel package under `plasma/look-and-feel/`, not `look-and-feel/`, so the client argument is `<session-data>/plasma/look-and-feel/org.macos8.desktop`; the probe's surviving argument shape is `ksplashqml --test --nofork <that path>` (upstream 6.3.6 `ksplash/ksplashqml/splashapp.cpp` advances one 2 s stage at a time and exits 0 at stage 7, while a plain `--nofork` client was measured unstable in the bare session), so the settle/timeout defaults stayed at the applet's 8 s / 90 s; and README.md's `### Rendering a candidate` section also enumerates the render modes and surfaces, so it gained the splash surface beside the planned `### Capturing a candidate` edits.

### Applet face gate: pin the rendered calculator applet's display field and keypad in `TestRender` (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of both waiting render-gate entries — it adds tests inside the existing `TestRender` class that reads the landed applet capture, so `_Renders.KINDS`, the dialog-count words, `DIALOG_MODES` and the `--file-dialog`/`--desktop` prose stay untouched; the two waiting entries touch `README.md`'s `--file-dialog` and `--desktop` paragraphs and `docs/invariants.md`'s skip-guard and desktop rows, while this entry's README sentence lands in the fidelity-checking gates paragraph and its row appends at the `## tooling` table's end, so whichever merge order holds, the later re-reads the others before extending; at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed applet render publishes the 320x240 calculator capture whose title strip, title boxes, frame borders and first client rows `TestRender` byte-compares to the reference screenshots, and whose body keeps exactly one pinned pixel (300,200). The applet's own face — the desktop theme rendering the calculator display field and keypad buttons inside that window — is otherwise unpinned: a regression that drops a keypad button's bevel arm, recolours the display field's outline or paints art into the flat gaps between the cells would pass every landed test. This plan pins those face regions, keeping the font-dependent glyph ink out of the exact pins.

**Grounding (measured fresh 2026-11-11 by the plan role: two consecutive full `python3 tools/render_surface.py <scratch>/a.png` runs on this host, both exit 0, both 320x240 PNGs and byte-identical — 0 differing pixels — so every pixel is run-stable and no exclusion region is needed).** The client face spans rows 22..233; the chrome around it (title strip, first client rows 22..26, bottom border) is already byte-compared to the reference by `TestRender`'s landed strips, so this plan pins only rows 27..233. The measured face: the display field is a 1px `#000000` outline box x=10..309, y=27..78 (top row 27, bottom row 78, left column x=10, right column x=309) whose interior x=11..308, y=28..77 is flat `#dddddd` except the display digit's ink — every non-face interior pixel lies in x=292..305, y=45..63 (197 pixels, antialiased greys included). Below it the keypad draws five button-row bands with top outline rows y=83, 113, 143, 174 and 204 and bottom outline rows y=108, 138, 169, 199 and 229, each cell the raised arrangement: `#000000` outline rectangle, `#ffffff` left inner bevel column, `#aaaaaa` right inner shadow column, flat `#dddddd` interior; the flat `#dddddd` gap rows between the bands are y=109..112, 139..142, 170..173, 200..203 (flat only for x=6..208 — the rightmost column's cell spans across rows 200..203) and 230..233 (flat full width), and rows 23..26 are flat full width. The button columns' outline columns are x=10, 71, 76, 138, 143, 204, 209 and 309 with flat `#dddddd` gap columns x=72..75 and 139..142 — clean in the first four row bands, but in the fifth band (rows 206..227) the leftmost cell's glyph ink bleeds across x=72..76 (measured rows 209..210), so the fifth band's gap-column flatness stays unpinned. The rightmost column x=209..309 merges the fourth and fifth row bands into one tall cell y=174..229 (measured at x=250: outline row 174, bevel row 175, interior 176..227, shadow row 228, bottom outline row 229). Every measured cell carries dark glyph ink inside its interior (row-1 cells' dark cores x=34..47, 101..113, 168..178 and 243..274); the ink is font-dependent, so it is pinned only by live-ink checks. These are session-measured platform values (plasmawindowed's calculator applet rendering the selected desktop theme on this host, 2026-11-11) no reference screenshot shows.

**Implementation note (2026-11-11 by the feature role).** The planned pins were re-derived from three fresh full renders the same day (every pair byte-identical, all exit 0, all 320x240), and three measured corrections ride with them: the flat face rows span x=6..313 (x=0..5 and x=314..319 are the side-border art the landed strips byte-compare), rows 79..82 between the display and the keypad are flat too, and the fifth band draws two cells, x=10..138 and x=143..204 — no frame pixels sit at x=71/76 in rows 207..226, the black pixels around x=69..79 are the wide cell's label ink — so the cell pins use a three-pixel blended corner arc (a `corner_blend` keyword on the shared pixel helper; the dialog call sites pass no argument and keep the sharp-rectangle semantics) and the fifth band has no gap column to pin.

**Approach.**

1. First re-verify stability: run two consecutive full applet renders on this host and compare every pixel; measured 2026-11-11 they are byte-identical, so require the fresh pair to be byte-identical too — any differing pixel means an unstable value: stop and re-derive every region from the fresh capture, never pin an unstable one, and record the re-derivation in the test comments.
2. `tests/test_render_surface.py`: lift `_DialogGate`'s three pixel helpers (`assert_pixel`, `assert_band`, `assert_raised_frame`) into a module-level shared base (for example `class _PixelPins`) that both `_DialogGate` and `TestRender` inherit, a mechanical move that leaves every existing call site and `_DialogGate`'s behavior unchanged; then extend `TestRender` beside its landed strip tests with the tests below, each reading the capture through `candidate_image` and quoting the measured values in comments with the two-run provenance:
   - `test_the_display_field_pins_its_outline_and_flat_interior`: the outline box x=10..309, y=27..78 black on all four sides, the interior x=11..308, y=28..77 flat `#dddddd`, and every non-face interior pixel confined to the measured ink region x=292..305, y=45..63 — a recoloured outline, a lost face row or stray art in the display fails here.
   - `test_the_display_inks_its_digit`: at least one dark pixel inside x=292..305, y=45..63 — the digit must draw, glyphs unpinned (mirrors the dialog gates' live-ink checks).
   - `test_the_keypad_cells_pin_the_raised_frames`: each measured cell — the four row bands' cells over the column spans (10..71, 76..138, 143..204), the fifth band's left cells, and the tall right-column cell x=209..309, y=174..229 — pinned through the shared raised-frame helper (black outline rectangle, `#ffffff` bevel column, `#aaaaaa` shadow column, `#dddddd` interior at its clean edge columns) with the band's outline rows and columns asserted black; a dropped bevel arm, a shifted cell boundary or a resampled frame fails here.
   - `test_the_gaps_between_the_cells_stay_flat_face`: the flat gap rows (full width for y=109..112, 139..142, 170..173, 230..233 and rows 23..26; x=6..208 for y=200..203) and the flat gap columns x=72..75 and 139..142 for the first four row bands — the fifth band's gap columns stay unpinned per the measured ink bleed — so stray art or a bevel bleeding between the cells fails here.

### Platinum cursor set: ship the side-edge and corner resize roles as byte-identical aliases of the landed resize glyphs (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of the waiting desktop render part 1/2 — that entry edits the render plumbing (`tools/render_surface.py`, `tools/render_workflow.py`, `tools/render_setup.py`, the `Makefile`, the render test suites and README's render prose), while this entry edits only `tools/cursor_art.py`, the regenerated `theme/icons/org.macos8.desktop/cursors/` files, `tests/test_cursors_theme.py`, README's pointer-set paragraph and the `## icons` cursor row of `docs/invariants.md`, so the two share no file, test or anchor and either merge order leaves both working; at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Close the shipped pointer set's visible Xcursor leak: the package carries no file for the eight resize roles an Xcursor client names when a pointer drags or resizes a window edge or corner — `top_side`, `bottom_side`, `left_side`, `right_side`, `top_left_corner`, `top_right_corner`, `bottom_left_corner` and `bottom_right_corner` — so GTK CSD windows and X11 resize handles draw those eight pointers from the fallback theme (Breeze, here and on the hosted CI image; the Breeze set ships each name as its own art file, distinct from its `size_*` glyphs, byte-compare confirmed on this host 2026-11-11). README's pointer-set paragraph already records the limitation ("Xcursor roles the theme does not name still come from the fallback cursor theme"). No new art is needed: the set's alias policy (the `## icons` cursor row's provenance cell records alias grouping as "this theme's own choice") lets each new role ship as a byte-identical copy of the landed resize glyph whose axis it spans. A future set of single-direction arrows for these roles is a separate art candidate and stays out; so does `right_ptr` (no reference screenshot shows a right-pointing arrow and a mirrored glyph is a new-art decision; Breeze supplies it only in RTL locales today).

**Approach.**

1. `tools/cursor_art.py`: extend four `CURSORS` alias tuples with no change to any canonical name, grid or hotspot — `size_ver` gains `"top_side"` and `"bottom_side"`, `size_hor` gains `"left_side"` and `"right_side"`, `size_fdiag` gains `"top_left_corner"` and `"bottom_right_corner"`, and `size_bdiag` gains `"top_right_corner"` and `"bottom_left_corner"`. A throwaway probe on this host today (2026-11-11) verified the mechanism end to end: with the theme installed into a scratch data home, `[KDE] LookAndFeelPackage=org.macos8.desktop` written into the scratch `plasmarc` (and `kdeglobals`), and `plasmashell` as the client of the landed `dbus-run-session -- kwin_wayland --virtual --no-lockscreen --width 640 --height 400` harness, the 20px menu bar painted (white top row, `#DDDDDD` face rows, `#999999`/`#000000` bottom rules, clock digits and a shell label in the bar's right half), `spectacle -b -n -f` captured it and KWin exited cleanly when the client died; the desktop area below painted flat, so the wallpaper is not part of this series.
