### Inactive-window gate, part 2/2: pin the rendered unfocused window's decoration pixels in `TestInactiveDialogRender` (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; completes the two-part series whose part 1/2 landed 2026-11-11, so no allocator dependency clause remains — the landed part 1/2 plumbed the two-window `--inactive-dialog` capture and its `kwinrulesrc` rules and recorded the regions for this gate in `tests/test_render_window_rules.py` and the `## tooling` invariants row; independent of the waiting applet-preflight entry — that entry edits `tools/render_surface.py`'s preflight and `_applet`, `tools/render_applet.py` (new), `tests/test_render_applet.py` (new), `tests/test_render_surface_units.py`, README's prerequisites/`### Rendering a candidate`/troubleshooting rows and a `## tooling` table-tail row, while this entry edits `tests/test_render_surface.py`'s gate scaffolding (`_Renders.KINDS`, a new gate class, the count-bearing docstrings), `tests/test_dialog_gate_count_prose.py`'s number map, `tests/test_ci_workflow.py`'s count comment, README's dialog-gate enumeration and `docs/invariants.md`'s two count-bearing rows plus one new row appended directly after the landed 2026-11-11 part 1/2 row, deliberately not at the `## tooling` table tail so the two entries' table appends cannot collide — the two share no production file, no test module and no assertion and either merge order leaves all working; at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed two-window `--inactive-dialog` render has plumbing and a measured capture but no pixel gate: no assertion holds a running KWin to the shipped inactive decoration art — the flat buttonless `#DDDDDD` bar with its 1px `#555555` outline that `tests/test_aurorae_frame.py::TestDecorationSvg::test_inactive_frame_matches_reference` derives from `desktop_fandom.png`'s four unfocused windows and the `#777777` title ink `tests/test_aurorae_rc.py` pins against `org.macos8.desktoprc`'s `InactiveTextColor=119,119,119`. A regression that, say, resurrects flattened box art in the inactive bar, recolours the outline, resamples the field or paints the title in the active ink would pass every landed test. This part adds the gate the landed part 1/2 record promised.

**Grounding (measured fresh 2026-11-11 by the plan role, one full `python3 tools/render_surface.py <scratch>/dialog.png --inactive-dialog` run on this host, exit 0, 480x360 PNG).** The left (unfocused) window's frame occupies exactly `(4,8)`–`(227,351)` — position `(4,8)`, size `(224,344)`, matching `tests/test_render_window_rules.py::INACTIVE_GEOMETRY` — and its decoration structure on the capture is exactly: a 1px `#555555` outer ring around the whole rect (every border pixel measured `#555555`); a 1px `#555555` inner rectangle ring — the active frame's black client edge recoloured — with its top row y=29 and bottom row y=346 spanning x=9..222 and left column x=9 and right column x=222 spanning y=29..346; every pixel strictly between the two rings flat `#DDDDDD`; and the only non-`#DDDDDD` pixels in that between-rings region the centered title "Inactive window"'s glyph band, ink `#777777` spanning x=60..128 at y=14..23 (antialiasing bleeds one pixel around it; band x=58..130, y=13..24 contained all of it in the measured run), with the leftmost stem column x=60 fully `#777777` down y=14..23 — no box or button art anywhere in the bar. The right (focused) window's frame ring at `(252,8)`–`(475,351)` is 1px `#000000` with non-field pixels in its title bar, proving the capture really holds two states. These are session-measured platform values (KWin 6.3.6, Lato title font, kdialog 25.04.x) no reference screenshot shows; `tests/test_aurorae_frame.py` and `tests/test_aurorae_rc.py` are the art-side re-derivation the gate's constants point at.

**Approach.**

1. First re-verify the measurement: run two consecutive full `--inactive-dialog` renders on this host and `cmp` the two captures; only pin once they agree byte for byte (the landed color- and gtk-gate pattern). If the pair disagrees, or any region differs from the values above, stop and re-derive every region from the fresh capture — never pin an unstable value — and record the re-derivation in the test comments.
2. `tests/test_render_surface.py`: append `("inactive", ("--inactive-dialog",), "dialog.png")` to `_Renders.KINDS` after the `"gtk"` entry, and add `class TestInactiveDialogRender(_DialogGate, unittest.TestCase)` beside the landed gate classes with `KIND = "inactive"` and a docstring stating it pins the shipped inactive Aurorae decoration as KWin draws it on the unfocused left window, complements the landed art-side pins, and holds no client-widget pin (the message-box contents stay unpinned; the other dialog gates own widget pins). Its tests, reading the capture through the inherited `candidate_image`:

This kills flattened box art, a stray active bevel row and any resampling bleed in the bar; the glyph-band bounds sit in the test comments with the measured-run provenance.

Do not byte-compare the full antialiased glyph set; the stem column is the ink's deterministic core.

### Render CLI: refuse a missing applet package before the session starts (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of the waiting fidelity JPEG entry and the waiting inactive-window part 1/2 entry — the JPEG entry edits `tools/fidelity_sources.py::read_source`, `tests/test_fidelity_jpeg.py`, README's `## Fidelity checking` section and one `## tooling` row, while part 1/2 edits `tools/render_clients.py`, `tools/render_dialogs.py`, `tools/render_workflow.py`, the `Makefile` and README's render-mode enumeration; this entry edits only `tools/render_surface.py`'s preflight in `main` and the `_applet` validator beside it, a new standalone module with no render plumbing import, its own test module and `tests/test_render_surface_units.py`, and README's prerequisites row plus one troubleshooting-table row — so the three entries share no file region, no test module and no assertion and any merge order leaves all working; at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** The calculator render's client is `plasmawindowed <applet>` (`tools/render_workflow.py::_client_command`'s non-dialog branch), but the CLI's preflight (`tools/render_surface.py::main`) checks only command names through `tools/diagnostics.py::report_missing_tool`; an applet package is not a command, so a host without `org.kde.plasma.calculator` wastes a full scratch KWin session and reports only an indirect failure — README.md's prerequisites row and `### Rendering a candidate` paragraph both say "without it the window never paints and the capture times out instead of failing at a tool check". README's `### Troubleshooting a render` table then has to tell the reader a timeout does not diagnose the absence. A pre-flight existence check closes the wart the same way the landed missing-tool refusal closes the missing-command one: exit 2 before `Session.create()`, naming the applet id. Grep of PLANS.md `## Planned`, PLANS-DONE.md, BUGS.md and BUGS-FIXED.md found no entry carrying a missing-applet preflight (the archived render-triage plan explicitly left it as an unverified cause; the CI workflow's `has_calculator_applet` shell check provisions the runner image and stays untouched).

**Grounding (verified fresh 2026-11-11).** `plasmawindowed` opens a KPackage applet package from the XDG data directories' `plasma/plasmoids/<id>/` directory: on this host `/usr/share/plasma/plasmoids/org.kde.plasma.calculator/metadata.json` exists and `plasmawindowed --help` takes `applet` as its first positional. `tools/render_surface.py::main` runs `report_missing_tool(TOOL, requirements)` and then `output_problem`, all before `with exit_on_termination(): return render(args)` — the insertion point for the new refusal. `_applet` (same file) already refuses empty, option-like and NUL-carrying ids but accepts path separators (`"a/b"` parses), which a path-joining existence check must not accept. The dialog modes never open the applet (`main` computes `dialog_flags` before the preflight), so the check must be skipped when a dialog flag is set — a `--menu-dialog`-only host without the calculator applet must still render its dialogs.

**Approach.**

1. New `tools/render_applet.py`, no imports from the render plumbing: `applet_problem(applet_id, data_roots=None) -> str | None`. When `data_roots` is None, derive them as `XDG_DATA_HOME` (default `~/.local/share` when unset or empty) followed by the `XDG_DATA_DIRS` entries (default `/usr/local/share:/usr/share`), mirroring the XDG data locations KPackage searches. An id that is empty or contains `/`, `\` or NUL is itself a problem string. When every root misses `<root>/plasma/plasmoids/<id>/metadata.json` (a plain file, not a directory), return a problem string naming the applet id and the searched `plasma/plasmoids` locations; any root holding that file ends the search with None. The module docstring records the probed location rule and its 2026-11-11 host evidence.
2. `tools/render_surface.py`: extend `_applet` to also refuse path separators with the same diagnostic shape (a plasmoid id is a dotted KPlugin id; `"a/b"` must exit 2 at parse time). In `main`, directly after the `report_missing_tool` block, when `dialog_flags` is empty call `applet_problem(args.applet)` and on a problem `return report_error(TOOL, problem)` (exit 2, the same missing-external-dependency status the epilog already documents), before `output_problem` and the session.
3. `tests/test_render_applet.py` (new): the finder unit tests pass explicit `data_roots` lists — found via an `XDG_DATA_HOME`-style root, found via an `XDG_DATA_DIRS`-style root, directory without `metadata.json` still missing, first matching root wins, problem string names the id and both attempted shapes, path-separator and empty ids refused — plus one derivation test patching `XDG_DATA_HOME`/`XDG_DATA_DIRS` in `os.environ` (including the empty-string-falls-back-to-default cases).
4. `tests/test_render_surface_units.py`: beside the landed applet cases, pin that `"a/b"` as `--applet` exits 2 at parse time; and that `main(["out.png"])` with `XDG_DATA_HOME`/`XDG_DATA_DIRS` patched to empty scratch dirs exits 2 with a diagnostic naming `org.kde.plasma.calculator` and reaches no session (patch the render call seam to fail loudly on invocation), while the same patched environment with a scratch root holding `plasma/plasmoids/org.kde.plasma.calculator/metadata.json` passes the preflight and reaches the render seam; and that a `--menu-dialog` run under the empty patched environment refuses through the landed missing-client-tool path and never consults the applet check (assert the check seam was not called alongside the tool-report seam), all without starting a KWin session.
5. README.md: in the prerequisites row and the `### Rendering a candidate` paragraph, replace the "never paints and the capture times out" wart wording with the new behavior — a calculator capture needs the `org.kde.plasma.calculator` applet installed (Debian packages it in `plasma-widgets-addons`), and a render of a missing applet refuses with exit 2 before any session, naming the applet id and the searched locations. In the `### Troubleshooting a render` table, reword the timeout row's applet clause: the absence is now diagnosed by its own preflight refusal, so a bare timeout no longer lists it as an undiagnosed cause.
6. `docs/invariants.md` `## tooling` table: append one dated (2026-11-11) end-of-table row naming `tests/test_render_applet.py` and the new `tests/test_render_surface_units.py` cases, recording the probed KPackage applet location (XDG data dirs' `plasma/plasmoids/<id>/metadata.json`, verified against the installed `plasmawindowed` on 2026-11-11), that the refusal is a preflight diagnostic with no pixel pinned, and that dialog modes skip the check.

**Files.** `tools/render_applet.py` (new), `tools/render_surface.py`, `tests/test_render_applet.py` (new), `tests/test_render_surface_units.py`, `README.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `python3 tools/render_surface.py out.png` on a host whose XDG data locations hold no `org.kde.plasma.calculator` package (reproducible with the patched-environment unit cases) exits 2 with a diagnostic naming `org.kde.plasma.calculator` and the searched `plasma/plasmoids` locations, creating no scratch session directory; with the package present (this host) the render proceeds unchanged and the landed calculator gates and their unit tests pass unchanged.
- `--applet a/b` (and `a\\b`, and an empty id) exits 2 at parse time with the landed applet-validator diagnostic shape; a dialog flag with a non-installed default applet still refuses only through the landed dialog preflight, never on the applet check.
- Every `plasma/plasmoids/<id>/metadata.json` root match ends the search and produces no diagnostic; a directory without `metadata.json` does not match; the searched-location list appears in the missing-applet diagnostic.
- README's prerequisites row, `### Rendering a candidate` paragraph and `### Troubleshooting a render` timeout row state the preflight refusal instead of the timeout wart; `docs/invariants.md`'s `## tooling` table ends with the new row; `make check` passes after the final edit.

### Rendered inactive-window gate, part 1/2: plumb a two-window capture that renders one unfocused client through the render CLI, workflow, session and Makefile (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; part 1 of a two-part series — part 2/2 will add the `TestInactiveDialogRender` pixel gate to `tests/test_render_surface.py`, byte-comparing the captured unfocused window's flat buttonless bar, `#777777` title ink and frame rows against the shipped inactive Aurorae art `tests/test_aurorae_frame.py` pins, and will be planned once this part lands, its heading naming this part as its landed prerequisite in the allocator's clause form, so this part lands mergeable on its own; independent of the waiting fidelity JPEG entry — that entry edits `tools/fidelity_sources.py`, `tests/test_fidelity_jpeg.py`, README's `## Fidelity checking` section and one appended `## tooling` row, while this entry edits the render plumbing (`tools/render_clients.py`, `tools/render_dialogs.py`, `tools/render_workflow.py`, `tools/render_surface.py` only through the shared table, `Makefile`), two render test modules and README's render sections plus its own appended `## tooling` row, so the two share no production function, no test module and no assertion and either merge order leaves all working — at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** No render gate has ever rendered an unfocused window: every landed gate captures exactly one client, and KWin activates a session's only window, so the shipped inactive Aurorae art — the flat buttonless `#DDDDDD` bar whose centered title paints `org.macos8.desktoprc`'s `InactiveTextColor` `#777777` (`tests/test_aurorae_frame.py::TestDecorationSvg`'s static pins, the 2026-11-04 inactive-art direction) — has never been seen drawn by a running KWin. The landed kwin-decoration session proofs (docs/invariants.md `## kwin-decoration`) exercised only the active path. A two-window capture — the focused client beside an earlier one KWin leaves unfocused — closes that gap and gives part 2/2 its candidate. Grep of PLANS.md `## Planned`, PLANS-DONE.md, BUGS.md, BUGS-FIXED.md and the tree found no window-rule or two-window render coverage.

**Grounding (verified fresh 2026-11-11).** `tools/render_dialogs.py::DIALOG_MODES` declares one `DialogMode(attr, flag, help, client, client_tool)` per dialog surface; `tools/render_surface.py` builds one `--*-dialog` flag per entry from that table and refuses more than one, `tools/render_workflow.py::_client_command` maps the flag to the client factory and `_select_dialog_theme` writes the Kvantum selection (the GTK selection only for `zenity` modes), and `_dialog_config_files` adds `kdeglobals` for every dialog render. `tools/render_session.py::session_script` backgrounds one client argv (`"$@" & client=$!`), liveness-checks it after the settle and reaps it after the capture, and `session_command` wraps `dbus-run-session -- kwin_wayland --virtual --width/--height`; `tools/render_setup.py::write_session_configs` writes exactly the config files named by the `files` tuple from the look-and-feel `contents/defaults` via `tools/theme_defaults.py::defaults_groups`. The `Makefile` spells the mode list once in `RENDER_MODE_VALUES`, pinned against `DIALOG_MODES` by `tests/test_render_make.py`'s mode-table test.

**Approach.**

1. `tools/render_clients.py`: add `inactive_dialog_client(session)`, returning a `sh -c` wrapper command that backgrounds two `kdialog --title <TITLE> --msgbox <TEXT>` windows with two distinct fixed titles — the to-be-inactive window first, the focused one last, so KWin activates the newest and the earlier one draws the inactive frame — then `wait`s, so the wrapper is the single client PID the session script liveness-checks and reaps exactly as today. The factory's comment records that the wrapper's death leaves the two kdialogs to the private bus's teardown, the session lifecycle every client already relies on.
2. `tools/render_dialogs.py`: append the entry `DialogMode("inactive_dialog", "--inactive-dialog", <help in the landed help style naming the two kdialog windows and the 480x360 capture>, inactive_dialog_client, "kdialog")` at the table's end. Geometry: a new small `tools/render_window_rules.py` writes a `kwinrulesrc` into the scratch config home holding exactly two rules matched on the exact titles and forcing both position and size — the inactive window at the capture's left, the focused one at its right, both fully inside the 480x360 dialog capture. Probe the installed KWin 6.3.6's rule parser (the rule grammar and the rule-value integer meaning "force") the way the kwin-decoration records verified engine behavior, record the probed keys in the rules writer's test comments and the invariants row, and pin both windows' forced sizes in the writer's tests; sizes are chosen from a first measured render, never assumed. The `DialogMode` named tuple lives in `tools/render_dialogs.py`, so that module gained the optional trailing `extra_config_files: tuple[str, ...] = ()` field (empty for every landed mode). The plan expected `render()` to pass `files=_dialog_config_files() + mode.extra_config_files`: at implementation the theme-defaults writer refuses a config file no `[<file>][<group>]` section defines, so `kwinrulesrc` cannot ride the `files` tuple — instead `render()` writes the rules file beside the dialog defaults through `tools/render_window_rules.py::write_window_rules` exactly when the selected mode's `extra_config_files` names `kwinrulesrc`, so only this mode's session writes `kwinrulesrc`.

5. Unit tests beside the landed dialog-mode unit tests (the per-mode CLI parser unit tests actually live in `tests/test_render_surface_units.py`, not `tests/test_render_surface.py` as this plan assumed; the workflow-level tests sit beside the landed ones in `tests/test_render_surface.py`'s `TestFailurePaths`, and the shared-table pins in `tests/test_render_dialogs.py` grew the new entry): the parser accepts `--inactive-dialog` alone and refuses it beside any other `--*-dialog` flag with the landed "open one dialog client each" wording; `_client_command` maps the flag to the two-window wrapper; the mode's session configs include `kwinrulesrc` beside `kwinrc`, `plasmarc` and `kdeglobals`; the Kvantum selection is written and no GTK selection installs; a new `tests/test_render_window_rules.py` pins the written `kwinrulesrc` bytes (both exact titles, both forced geometries, nothing else in the file). ### Fidelity CLI: read JPEG candidate and reference screenshots through the landed sampler convert bridge (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of the waiting fidelity min/max-refusal entry — that entry edits `tools/fidelity.py::main`'s validation block, the four existing fidelity fixture-window modules and the new `tests/test_fidelity_option_validation.py`, while this entry edits `tools/fidelity_sources.py::read_source`, adds `tests/test_fidelity_jpeg.py`, and touches only README's `## Fidelity checking` section and one appended `docs/invariants.md` `## tooling` row, so the two share no production function, no test module and no assertion and either merge order leaves all working — at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role
**Goal.** The fidelity CLI is the tool an operator points at the reference set to measure a rendered surface, but it still refuses every non-PNG reference: `python3 tools/fidelity.py render.png macos8.6-screenshots/opendialog_macrumors86.jpg` exits 2 with `fidelity: error: cannot decode macos8.6-screenshots/opendialog_macrumors86.jpg: not a PNG file: the input is a JPEG image, not a PNG; convert it to PNG first` (verified fresh 2026-11-11). The reference set carries JPEG screenshots (`opendialog_macrumors86.jpg`, `apps_macrumors8.6.jpg`, `boot_powerbookphoto_macrumors.jpg`, `desktop_archiveorg.jpg`) whose widget recipes the GTK plans cite, so measuring against them needs a manual `convert` round-trip whose output path and cleanup the operator nurses by hand — exactly the friction the landed sampler JPEG plan (PLANS-DONE.md, "Sample JPEG screenshots directly", 2026-11-10) removed for `tools/sample.py` and explicitly scoped out of the fidelity CLI ("No change to `tools/fidelity.py`; this plan covers the sampler only"). Grep of PLANS.md, PLANS-DONE.md, BUGS.md and BUGS-FIXED.md for fidelity-and-JPEG coverage finds no other entry carrying it.

**Grounding (verified fresh 2026-11-11).** `tools/fidelity_sources.py::read_source` is the single source loader for both comparison sides (`tools/fidelity.py` imports it as `_read_source`, package and direct-script branches; the pre-read validation spies in `tests/test_fidelity_column_runs_limit.py` and siblings patch `fidelity._read_source` at that boundary). It calls `tools.containment.require_within_repo` then `read_png(path, alpha=True)` with a `max_rows` bound from the crop and a sideways-overflow retry — PNG only. The landed bridge is reusable as-is: `tools/jpeg_convert.py::is_jpeg`/`convert_jpeg` (supervised `convert jpeg:- PNG24:<temp>` through `tools.process_group.py::run_logged_split`, `shutil.which` for the tool, diagnostic returned as a problem string), and `tests/support/jpeg_sampler_fixture.py` ships `QUILT_JPEG` (a 32x24 JPEG) with `QUILT_WIDTH`/`QUILT_HEIGHT`. `read_png(alpha=True)` on an RGB-only PNG derives an all-`255` alpha plane (run against a generated 4x4 PNG), and `tools/fidelity_pixels.py` treats a missing alpha plane as opaque `255`, so a JPEG converted to PNG24 compares coherently against an RGBA render with no alpha refusal — fidelity has no alpha flag to refuse. `tools/fidelity.py::main` catches `(PngError, FidelityError, ValueError)` and routes them through `report_error`, so a loader-side failure needs no `main` change; `FidelityError` lives in `tools/fidelity_geometry.py`.

**Approach.**

1. `tools/fidelity_sources.py::read_source`: after `require_within_repo`, open the path once and read its first three bytes; when `is_jpeg` holds, read the file whole, `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="fidelity-jpeg-")` a private directory, and `convert_jpeg(bytes, temp_png)` into it — never the input's directory. A `convert_jpeg` problem string raises `FidelityError(f"cannot decode {path}: {problem}")`, the same user-facing-path shape every other loader failure uses. On success, run today's decode against the temp PNG exactly as against the original: `read_png(temp, alpha=True, max_rows=…)`, the same sideways-overflow retry re-reading the same temp file unbounded, any `PngError` message having the temp path rewritten to `path` (the sampler's scrub pattern), and `shutil.rmtree(directory, ignore_errors=True)` in a `finally` before returning. A sniff `open` that raises `OSError` falls through to the PNG path so absent and unreadable paths keep `read_png`'s own diagnostics; PNG inputs keep the entire current code path with no conversion attempt; a non-PNG non-JPEG head (WebP, GIF, arbitrary bytes) keeps today's exact `not a PNG file` decode refusal. Import `is_jpeg`, `convert_jpeg` and `FidelityError` in both the package and direct-script import branches; `tests/test_no_unused_imports.py` keeps the imports honest.
2. Add `tests/test_fidelity_jpeg.py`, built on `support.fidelity_cli_case.FidelityCliTestCase` and using `tests/support/jpeg_sampler_fixture.py`'s `QUILT_JPEG`, mirroring `tests/test_sample_jpeg.py`'s class shapes: (a) the self-comparison `quilt.jpg quilt.jpg` exits 0 with the zero-difference report (all-zero metrics, `passed` true) — identical inputs decode identically on any `convert` build, so no lossy pixel value is pinned, and stdout names the given `.jpg` paths and no temporary path; (b) a crop run (`--crop 0,0,64,64`) fails naming the decoded JPEG's own 32x24 dimensions, pinning the converted decode's geometry without pinning lossy pixels; a within-bounds crop with `--difference-run-count` reports count 0; (c) a PNG pair with `mock.patch.object` turning the loader's `convert_jpeg` into an `AssertionError` runs the comparison unchanged — the PNG path never converts; (d) with `mock.patch.object(jpeg_convert.shutil, "which", return_value=None)` a JPEG pair exits 2 with empty stdout and a diagnostic naming the user path and `convert`, reaching no decode; (e) a truncated JPEG (`QUILT_JPEG` head plus a garbage tail) exits 2 naming the user-facing `.jpg` path and never a temporary path; (f) a WebP-headed file (`RIFF`…`WEBP` bytes) keeps the exact `not a PNG file` decode refusal; (g) a repo-symlink escape is still refused before any sniff or decode, and a path outside the repository is converted and read as before; (h) direct-script and package invocations agree.
3. README's `## Fidelity checking` opening paragraph: add one sentence after the crop-options sentence stating that a JPEG candidate or reference is decoded once through ImageMagick into a private temporary PNG before the comparison, other non-PNG formats keep the decode refusal, and the reference set's JPEG screenshots are therefore comparable directly.
4. `docs/invariants.md` `## tooling` table: append one end-of-table row naming `tests/test_fidelity_jpeg.py`, recording the bridge reuse, the opaque-alpha reading, the user-facing-path diagnostics, and the provenance sentence modeled on the sampler's JPEG row (row: "The reference-pixel sampler reads JPEG screenshots directly … (added 2026-11-10 by the feature role)") — ImageMagick's `convert` performs the JPEG decode, no reference screenshot pins the decoder itself, and the shipped fixture's recorded constants mean no test runs ImageMagick at check time.

**Files.** `tools/fidelity_sources.py`, `tests/test_fidelity_jpeg.py` (new), `README.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `python3 tools/fidelity.py a.jpg a.jpg` (the fixture JPEG written to a scratch path) exits 0 and prints the zero-difference report naming both given paths; `--crop 0,0,64,64` on a JPEG pair exits 2 naming the decoded 32x24 dimensions; within-bounds cropped runs report the same empty-difference results the same PNG pair reports.
- A JPEG with `convert` absent from `PATH` exits 2 before any decode, naming the user path and `convert`; a truncated JPEG exits 2 naming the user path with no temporary path anywhere in the diagnostic; a WebP-headed file keeps today's exact `not a PNG file` refusal; a repository-symlink escape is refused before any read of the file's bytes.
- Every existing PNG-path fidelity test passes unchanged, including the pre-read validation spies at the `_read_source` boundary; the loader's `tests/test_fidelity_sources.py` rows pass unchanged; a PNG pair never enters the conversion path (the mocked converter is not called); `make check` passes after the final edit.

### Fidelity CLI: refuse contradictory min/max mismatch-run filter windows and rewrite the empty-result fixtures (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 3 menu scroll-arrow entry — that entry touches the GTK 3 sheet, `tests/test_gtk_theme_views.py` and an appended `## gtk` row of `docs/invariants.md`, while this entry touches `tools/fidelity.py`, five fidelity test modules and the `## tooling` rows of `docs/invariants.md`, so no file, test or invariants row is shared and either merge order leaves all working — at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** The sampler refuses a minimum above its paired maximum before any image read — the user answered the 2026-11-11 QUESTIONS.md fork with "option 2, refuse", and the landed sampler change gave all five sampler pairs the diagnostic — but the fidelity CLI's two length-filter pairs still accept a contradictory window and exit 0 with an empty list: `--min-difference-run-length 3 --max-difference-run-length 2 --difference-runs --json` prints `"difference_runs": []` beside a full `difference_run_count` and the full comparison's metrics, indistinguishable from a genuine no-mismatch measurement. A typo'd window looks like a real measurement, exactly the shape the sampler's refusal exists to kill. The fidelity validation block already refuses misleading combinations before image reads (`--min-difference-run-length requires --difference-runs` and its siblings); the cross-check is the one missing member of that family. No queued or archived entry covers it (grepped PLANS.md, PLANS-DONE.md, BUGS.md for `must not exceed`, `contradict` and the fidelity pair names).

**Grounding (verified fresh 2026-11-11).** `tools/fidelity.py::main`'s validation block (the nine `parser.error` checks before `_read_source`, ~lines 96–105) carries only per-flag `requires`/`requires-cap` checks; `grep -rn "must not exceed" tools/fidelity.py tools/fidelity_cli_parser.py tools/fidelity_arguments.py` found nothing before this change; after the landed checks below it matches twice (tools/fidelity.py:104 and :118). The landed sampler shape is `tools/sample_arguments.py::option_error` (the `must not exceed` arms at the color-count, color-fraction, run-length, match-run-length and match-column-run-length pairs), wording `--min-run-length must not exceed --max-run-length (3 > 2)`, placed after that pair's own `requires` checks. Four test sites use the contradictory window as their empty fixture: `tests/test_fidelity_difference_runs_max_length.py` (min 3 / max 2 on the 9x2 `difference_pair(9, 2, ({0,2,3,5,6,7}, {0,1,2,3,8}), vertical=False)` fixture whose runs are lengths 1,2,3,4,1 — longest 4), `tests/test_fidelity_difference_runs_limit.py` (min 3 / max 2 / cap 1, same fixture), `tests/test_fidelity_column_runs_max_length.py` (min 3 / max 2 on the `difference_pair(2, 9, ({0,2,3,5,6,7}, {0,1,2,3,8}), vertical=True)` fixture whose longest column run is 3) and `tests/test_fidelity_run_count.py` (min 4 / max 1 on its 4x3 fixture whose runs are lengths 2,1,4). `tests/test_fidelity_column_runs_limit.py` already uses the legal empty window (min 9, above every run), the rewrite's shape.

### Platinum GTK 3 menu scroll arrows: restate the stock arrow face family with the landed flat-button recipe and square the landed scroll-arrow glyph groups (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 3 notebook-arrow entry — that entry appends ten `notebook > header > tabs > arrow` groups at the GTK 3 sheet tail, adds one test beside `test_notebook_tab_close_button_arms` in `tests/test_gtk_theme.py` and appends an end-of-table `docs/invariants.md` row while amending the flat-family row's stay-stock clause, while this entry adds four `menu > arrow` face groups at the sheet tail, extends the two landed glyph groups mid-sheet, adds one test beside `test_menu_scroll_arrows` in `tests/test_gtk_theme_views.py` and appends its own end-of-table row without touching any landed row — the two share no selector, no test file and no assertion, and whichever entry lands second re-reads the sheet tail and sits after the first's block; at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** When a GTK 3 menu is too short to show all its items, its ends show scroll arrows whose CSS nodes spell `menu > arrow`, `.menu > arrow` and `.context-menu > arrow`. The landed glyph series redirected only `-gtk-icon-source` on the two top/bottom arms; every face and state claim stock makes on these nodes is still live. Probed fresh this run 2026-11-11 with `gresource extract /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0 /org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` (libgtk-3 3.24.49, the 2055-line extract): resource line 808 `menu > arrow, .menu > arrow, .context-menu > arrow` clears border, background-image, box-shadow, text-shadow and `-gtk-icon-shadow`, sets 16px minimums and 4px padding — and then closes with `background-color: #ffffff` after its own transparent face declaration, so the effective rest face is white; line 814 hovers to `background-color: #eaebeb`; line 816 backdrops to `background-color: #fcfcfc`; line 818 disables with `color: transparent` and transparent face and border; and the top/bottom arms (lines 810/812) add scroll-geometry margins, a 1px `#eaebeb` edge hairline and 5px top or bottom radii. A scrolling menu over the landed `#DDDDDD` paper therefore shows a white 5px-rounded tile per arrow, a grey hover wash and a near-white backdrop tile. The landed glyph groups cannot fix this (they declare only `-gtk-icon-source`), no archived record restates the arrow faces (the landed CSD-corners record names the `.context-menu > arrow` spellings only as a sweep exclusion), and no queued entry touches them. No collected reference screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a GTK scrolling menu — the standing GTK-scope adaptation premise — so the arrows take the landed flat-button recipe, introducing no new palette value; the GTK 4 sheet needs nothing (its header comment already records that GTK 4 scrolls menus inside a popover through no arrow node).

### Platinum GTK 4 spin field in RTL: mirror the etch's inset arm to the field's exposed edge in the plain and .osd state groups, pinned by declaration tests and the landed child-interpreter probe shape (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 4 disabled-view ink entry — that entry amends only the landed disabled-view field block at the sheet tail, extends `test_disabled_view_face` and adds `test_disabled_view_family_ink` in `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, and appends its own end-of-table `docs/invariants.md` row, while this entry adds rules directly after the landed `entry, spinbutton:not(.vertical), spinbutton.vertical > text` field rule and the three landed `.osd` field groups, adds two new tests beside `test_osd_entry_fields` in `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` and appends its own row, so no entry shares a sheet region, test name or assertion and either merge order leaves all working — at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names, since the waiting entry also edits the same two files) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed 2026-10-29 entry recipe paints every GTK 4 field with `box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999` — the `entry, spinbutton:not(.vertical), spinbutton.vertical > text` rule and, inside an OSD overlay, the landed 2026-11-03 `.osd` restate's three state groups (`.osd spinbutton.vertical > text, .osd spinbutton:not(.vertical), .osd entry` and its `:focus-within` and `:disabled` twins). GTK 4, like GTK 3, does not mirror `box-shadow` for text direction, so in a right-to-left horizontal spin button the steppers sit at the field's left edge — the landed sheet's own `:dir(rtl)` stepper arms (`spinbutton:not(.vertical) > button.image-button.up:not(.flat):dir(rtl)` and its `:dir(rtl):first-child` corner twins, plus the `row.spin` twins) move both buttons there — covering the etch's vertical arm at that edge, so the exposed right edge keeps only the horizontal top arm: a half-etched field where the LTR field shows the full L. The landed GTK 3 sheet already carries the fix for its own sheet (the `spinbutton:dir(rtl):not(.vertical)` mirror and the four `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl)` state twins, measured 2026-11-11 in a GTK 3 offscreen child and recorded beside the plain field rule); a fresh grep this run finds no `spinbutton:dir(rtl)` `box-shadow` arm anywhere in `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, so the GTK 4 field keeps the half-etched defect. No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK spin field in either direction (the standing GTK-scope adaptation premise), so the fix restates the landed recipe's own grey, introducing no palette value.

**Approach.**

1. `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`: before writing, re-read the landed field rule and the three `.osd` groups and measure first — run the probe below's child program before the edit and record in the dated comment that the shipped sheet's RTL field exposed right edge lacks the etch arm on this host and date. Then, directly after the landed `entry, spinbutton:not(.vertical), spinbutton.vertical > text` rule, add one dated (2026-11-11) comment-and-rule `spinbutton:dir(rtl):not(.vertical) { box-shadow: inset -1px 1px #999999; }`, and directly after each of the three landed `.osd` state groups its twin — `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl):not(.vertical)`, `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl):focus-within:not(.vertical)` and `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl):disabled:not(.vertical)` — each declaring exactly `box-shadow: inset -1px 1px #999999`. Each mirror out-ranks its base group by one class (`:dir(rtl)`), so the win does not depend on source position. The dated comment records the mechanism (GTK does not mirror box-shadow for direction; the steppers cover the etch's vertical arm at the RTL field's left edge, measured before the edit), the landed GTK 3 mirror it follows, and the exclusions with their reasons: vertical `spinbutton.vertical > text` fields (no horizontal stepper covers the arm — the landed GTK 3 exclusion's reason stands), plain `entry` fields (no steppers, the landed GTK 3 plain-entry exclusion), and the treeview-embedded entry group (an `entry`, not a spin field). No background, border, radius, colour or other declaration is added, and the `.osd` record declares no `:backdrop` field twin, so none is mirrored.

2. `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`: first re-grep `test_flat_entry_fields` and `test_osd_entry_fields` for any count or token-sweep pin the four new selectors would break, then add `test_spin_field_mirrors_the_etch_in_rtl` beside `test_osd_entry_fields`: for each of the four mirror selectors assert `self.rules[selector] == {"box-shadow": "inset -1px 1px #999999"}` exactly and `self.selectors.count(selector) == 1`; an order pin that each mirror's index is greater than its base group's index (`spinbutton:dir(rtl):not(.vertical)` after the landed `spinbutton:not(.vertical),`-carrying plain field key, each `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl)` after its `.osd` state group); and token sweeps keyed on substrings no other landed selector carries (`spinbutton:dir(rtl):not(.vertical)`, `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl):focus-within:not(.vertical)`, `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl):disabled:not(.vertical)`), mapping to exactly the expected spelling, so a dropped mirror, a lost twin, a stray extra declaration or a changed value fails.

3. `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, probe: add `test_spin_field_renders_the_mirrored_etch_in_rtl` beside the landed probes, the same shape as `test_mixed_indicators_draw_black_dashes`: `require_gui_opt_in()` first, then a child interpreter subprocess with `GDK_BACKEND=x11` and `GSK_RENDERER=cairo`, exit 77 mapped to a skip naming what is missing; the child loads the shipped sheet bytes with the same `../assets/` URL rewrite at provider priority 801, builds a `Gtk.SpinButton` with an adjustment in a `Gtk.Window` (wide enough that no digit glyph reaches the pinned pixels), calls `set_direction(Gtk.TextDirection.RTL)` on the spin button, presents, finds the spin field node (guarded by `get_css_name() == "spinbutton"`), settles by frame and snapshots it with `Gtk.WidgetPaintable.new(...)` through `renderer.render_texture` into a pixbuf with the landed deadline loop, then asserts each pinned pixel as a literal tuple. A second window in the same child wraps an identical RTL spin button in an ancestor box carrying the `osd` class so the landed `.osd spinbutton …` descendant groups match, and captures it the same way. The pinned positions are measured at implementation on this host from a fresh child render, the plan states no coordinates, and every position is clear of glyph rows, the field border's edge ratio and the stepper buttons' interior: on the plain capture, one interior pixel at the field's exposed right edge expecting the mirrored `#999999` vertical arm (dropping the mirror turns it field-white), one pixel on the top border row expecting `#000000`, and one interior pixel at the covered left edge under a stepper expecting the stepper button's `#FFFFFF` bevel arm rather than the etch grey; on the `.osd` capture, the same exposed-edge pixel expecting `#999999` — so any of a dropped mirror, a foreign value, a mirror that loses its specificity race or an unmirrored `.osd` state changes at least one pinned pixel.

4. `docs/invariants.md`: append one dated (2026-11-11) end-of-table `## gtk` row naming both tests, re-grepping the tail first since landed rows are appended there, and recording: the missing reference surface (no collected screenshot shows a GTK spin field in either direction); the value source (the landed entry recipe's own etch grey, mirrored from the landed GTK 3 `spinbutton:dir(rtl)` record); the specificity shape (each mirror out-ranks its base group by one class); the exclusions and reasons; and that the probe establishes rendered pixels only under the opt-in guard where GTK 4 introspection and an X display are present, as declaration checks never have.

**Files.** `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- The GTK 4 sheet declares exactly the four mirror rules, each with exactly `box-shadow: inset -1px 1px #999999`, each placed directly after its base group with its dated comment; the landed field rule, the three `.osd` groups, the stepper arms and every other sheet rule are unchanged.
- `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_spin_field_mirrors_the_etch_in_rtl` passes and fails on a dropped mirror, a foreign value, a lost placement or a stray extra declaration; `test_flat_entry_fields` and `test_osd_entry_fields` pass unchanged.
- Without `PLATINUM_RUN_GUI_TESTS=1` the probe raises the landed opt-in skip, and where GTK 4 introspection or a display is missing despite the opt-in it skips with its own reason; where both are present the child completes and its pinned pixels read the literal tuples, so deleting any one of the four mirrors — or spelling one with the LTR arm `inset 1px 1px #999999` — changes at least one pinned pixel and fails.
- `docs/invariants.md` carries the appended row, and `make check` passes after the final edit.

**At implementation (2026-11-11 by the feature role).** The probe grew two
captures beside the two the plan names — a focused `.osd` capture and an
insensitive `.osd` capture with their own state guards (`FOCUS_WITHIN`,
`INSENSITIVE`) — because the criterion that deleting any one of the four
mirrors changes a pinned pixel only holds for the state twins once their

### Platinum GTK 3 disabled view: restate the insensitive view family's white field and grey ink over the toolkit's stock disabled arms and pin both with an offscreen pixel probe (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of every other entry — it adds one dated block directly after the GTK 3 sheet's landed disabled-selected groups, two tests to `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, one render probe to `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` and one appended end-of-table `## gtk` row of `docs/invariants.md`; the waiting OSD RTL entry touches only that sheet's four OSD entry-field state groups and the landed RTL-mirror comment, its own OSD test module and one probe method of its own in the same controls file, so the entries share no sheet region, test name or assertion and either merge order leaves both working — at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names, since the two spin entries also extended these files) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** An insensitive list, icon view, text view or tree view in a GTK 3 app still paints the toolkit's own foreign disabled faces. Measured 2026-11-11 with `gresource extract` of `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0` (libgtk-3 3.24.49, the 2055-line resource; paths recorded in `docs/invariants.md`): the resource declares exactly three disabled view arms — line 28 `.view:disabled, iconview:disabled, .view text:disabled, iconview text:disabled, textview text:disabled { color: #929595; background-color: #faf9f8; }`, line 699 `treeview.view:disabled { color: #929595; }` and line 705 `treeview.view:disabled:backdrop { color: #d4cfca; }` — and the toolkit's dark twin `gtk-contained-dark.css` carries the same-shaped family (probe it at implementation and quote it in the invariants row). Every member of the first arm out-specifies the landed base view group `.view, textview text, list` (which declares `background-color: #FFFFFF` and `color: #000000`), and the landed disabled-selected groups own only the `:disabled:selected` combinations, so today an insensitive view paints the warm near-white stock field `#faf9f8` under stock grey `#929595` ink, and in an unfocused window the tree ink pales to stock's `#d4cfca`, instead of the landed white field, the landed insensitive grey and the landed disabled-selected backdrop policy. No collected reference screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a disabled GTK view (the standing GTK-scope adaptation premise), so the values are platform-adapted: the fill reuses the landed white view field the base group states, the ink reuses the landed insensitive grey `#888888` (the same grey the landed disabled label, entry and disabled-selected arms paint, re-derived from the colour scheme's `[Colors:Button] ForegroundInactive`), and the backdrop twin keeps that grey in unfocused windows exactly as the landed `row:backdrop:disabled:selected` and `treeview.view:disabled:selected:backdrop` restatements do.

**Implementation correction (2026-11-11, feature role — measured, not planned).** Render-probing the landed sheet in the offscreen child disproves the Goal's stock-face premise: the user sheet installs above the toolkit resource (the probes load it at `GTK_STYLE_PROVIDER_PRIORITY_USER` (800) over the theme resource) and GTK's cascade decides per property by provider priority before specificity, so the landed `.view, textview text, list` base group already wins — pre-change an insensitive text view or icon view painted the landed white field under the base group's unconditional black ink, and neither stock literal ever rendered (both measured; the icon view field read pure `#FFFFFF`). The observable defect these rules fix is that ink: insensitive view text painted the base group's black, unlike every other landed insensitive text, and the restated comma group and tree arms change it to the landed insensitive grey (mutation-verified: dropping the comma group's `color: #888888` declaration renders the black ink and fails the probe's grey-run assertion). The white-field restatement is a coherence restate whose removal stays unobservable through the base group. The probe's stroke: the default-font underscore stroke is a sub-pixel hairline whose pixels never reach full ink coverage (measured about 0.815 coverage), so the buffer's underscores are scaled 3x with a `TextTag`, which yields full-coverage `#888888` runs; the sheet comment, this entry and the invariants row record the measured story, and the criterion below is reworded to the measured mutation behavior. One file beyond the plan's list also changes: `tests/test_gtk_theme_views.py`'s landed icon-view family sweep gains the two new `iconview` disabled spellings, the same extension that sweep took when the 2026-11-04 corner record landed its icon-view arms.

**Approach.**

1. `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`: one dated (2026-11-11) comment block plus three rules appended directly after the landed `label:backdrop selection:disabled, …` disabled-selected group and before the tab-close comment block that follows it (re-grep the anchor before writing): a comma group spelling stock's line-28 members byte-equal — `.view:disabled, iconview:disabled, .view text:disabled, iconview text:disabled, textview text:disabled` — restating exactly `color: #888888` and `background-color: #FFFFFF`, so the byte-equal spelling wins both per-property ties by later user-sheet source order; and the two byte-equal tree arms `treeview.view:disabled { color: #888888; }` and `treeview.view:disabled:backdrop { color: #888888; }`, restated separately because their spellings out-specify the comma group and would otherwise keep the stock values. The comment records: the three stock arms with their resource lines and the foreign literals elided per the palette convention (the verbatim values live in the invariants row), the missing reference surface, the value sources named in the Goal, and the exclusions — the `:disabled:selected` combinations (the landed disabled-selected groups own their ink, including `treeview.view:disabled:selected` and its backdrop twin), the toolkit's remaining insensitive arms outside the view family (label, entry and button fields are the landed disabled-text records' own), and the GTK 4 sibling: the integration library's per-family disabled view ink arms and the landed 2026-11-09 GTK 4 disabled-view group's deliberately excluded `color` co-declaration are a separate candidate entry, not this one. No geometry, margin, transition or other-state declaration is added.

2. `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`: add `test_disabled_view_face_and_ink` beside the landed disabled-selected block in `TestGtkTheme`, shaped like `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_disabled_view_face`: count-one pins (each of the three rules appears exactly once) and exact-declaration pins (the comma group to exactly `color: #888888` and `background-color: #FFFFFF` via `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`'s `DISABLED_TEXT` recipe plus the white field, the two tree arms to exactly `color: #888888`), plus token sweeps keyed on substrings no other landed selector carries (e.g. `treeview.view:disabled:backdrop`), so a dropped rule, a stray extra declaration or a changed value fails.

3. `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`: add `test_disabled_view_renders_the_white_field_and_grey_ink` to `TestGtkThemeControls`, built from `support.gtk_child_probe`'s `_GTK3_CHILD_HEAD` and `_run_gtk_child` like the landed render probes: strip `url(...)` from the shipped sheet, install the provider, and render, in a fresh `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`, a `Gtk.TextView` with `set_sensitive(False)` and `set_can_focus(False)` whose buffer holds one long line of underscore characters (a solid ink stroke), packed in a 5px-border `Gtk.Box`. Read the text view's allocation and assert: the four allocation-interior corner pixels each read exactly `#FFFFFF` (the restated field fill); no pixel anywhere in the allocation equals the stock literal `#929595` or `#faf9f8` (both are non-grey, and the restated sheet paints only pure white and pure grey there, so antialiasing can never synthesize them); and at least one allocation row carries eight or more consecutive pixels equal to exactly `#888888` (the underscore stroke's full-coverage core under the restated ink). With the ink twin removed the cores read `#929595` and the test fails; with the fill twin removed the field reads `#faf9f8` and the test fails. It skips with the child's own reason where GTK 3 introspection or a display is missing.

4. `docs/invariants.md`: one appended end-of-table `## gtk` row naming both new tests and recording: the missing reference surface (no collected screenshot shows a disabled GTK view), the provenance (the three stock arms probed 2026-11-11 with `gresource extract` as in the Goal, lines 28, 699 and 705, their verbatim foreign values quoted in the row — `#929595`, `#faf9f8`, `#d4cfca` — plus the dark twin's same-shaped family probed at implementation), the value sources (the landed white field and the landed insensitive grey, with the backdrop policy and its landed disabled-selected backdrop precedents), the `:disabled:selected` exclusion, and the GTK 4 sibling left to its own candidate.

**Files.** `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- The GTK 3 sheet contains exactly one rule for the five-member disabled view comma group (declaring exactly `color: #888888` and `background-color: #FFFFFF`), exactly one `treeview.view:disabled` and exactly one `treeview.view:disabled:backdrop` (each declaring exactly `color: #888888`), each placed directly after the landed disabled-selected groups; the landed disabled-selected groups, the base `.view, textview text, list` group and every other sheet rule are unchanged.
- `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_disabled_view_face_and_ink` passes and fails on a dropped rule, a comma member lost, a stray extra declaration, or a changed value.
- When GTK 3 introspection and a display are present, `test_disabled_view_renders_the_white_field_and_grey_ink` renders the insensitive text view reading `#FFFFFF` at its four interior corners, no allocation pixel equal to `#929595` or `#faf9f8`, and an eight-pixel `#888888` underscore run; with the comma group's `color: #888888` declaration removed the cores read the base group's black ink and the probe fails (measured), with the ink spelled with a stock value the probe fails both the stock-literal and the grey-run assertions, with the white-field declaration removed the probe still passes through the landed base group (measured — see the correction above), and it skips with the child's own reason where GTK 3 or a display is missing.
- `docs/invariants.md` carries the appended row, and `make check` passes.

### Platinum GTK 3 OSD spin field in RTL: mirror the etch's inset arm to the field's exposed edge in the four OSD state twins (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of every other entry — it touches only the GTK 3 sheet's four OSD entry-field state groups and the landed RTL-mirror comment beside the plain spin rules, `tests/test_gtk_theme_osd.py`, one new probe in `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` and one new `docs/invariants.md` row; the waiting child-probe harness entry touches only that probe file's harness block, the `_GTK3_*` constants and `_run_gtk_child`, whose call surface this entry's new probe keeps, so either merge order leaves both working) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed RTL mirror `spinbutton:dir(rtl):not(.vertical) { box-shadow: inset -1px 1px #999999; }` in `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` deliberately excluded the four `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical)` state groups, whose record that entry named "a future candidate". Those groups restate `box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999` at equal-or-higher specificity — `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical)` ties the (0,2,1) mirror and wins by later source position, and the `:focus`/`:backdrop`/`:disabled` arms out-rank it — so an RTL OSD spin field still draws the half-etched field the mirror fixed everywhere else. Measured 2026-11-11 on this host with a GTK 3 offscreen child rendering a `Gtk.SpinButton` under an `.osd`-classed `Gtk.Box` (columns L+1 and R−1 of the spin button's allocation, rows T+1, T+2, T+3 and B−1): LTR reads `#999999` at all four rows at L+1 and `#000000` at all four at R−1; RTL reads `#000000` at all four at L+1 and `#999999`, `#FFFFFF`, `#FFFFFF`, `#FFFFFF` at R−1 — the top arm only, no vertical arm, with the plain mirror rule already active. A scratch copy of the sheet with `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl):not(.vertical) { box-shadow: inset -1px 1px #999999; }` appended rendered RTL R−1 as `#999999` at all four rows and left LTR unchanged.

**Approach.**

1. `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`: directly after each of the four groups at the `/* No collected reference screenshot shows a field inside a GTK OSD overlay … */` record — `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical), .osd entry`, `.osd spinbutton:focus:not(.vertical), .osd entry:focus`, `.osd spinbutton:backdrop:not(.vertical), .osd entry:backdrop`, `.osd spinbutton:disabled:not(.vertical), .osd entry:disabled` (re-grep each selector for count-one before writing) — append one twin rule carrying exactly one declaration, `box-shadow: inset -1px 1px #999999`, spelled `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl):not(.vertical)`, `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl):focus:not(.vertical)`, `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl):backdrop:not(.vertical)` and `.osd spinbutton:dir(rtl):disabled:not(.vertical)`. Each twin out-ranks its base group by one class, so the win does not depend on source position; placing each beside its group keeps the record together. Change nothing in the four base groups, in the grouped `.osd entry` arms, or in the landed plain mirror rule. Replace the mirror comment's last sentence ("The four .osd spinbutton state groups … the OSD family stays a future candidate.") with a pointer naming the landed twins. Above the twins, one dated (2026-11-11) adaptation comment recording: no collected reference screenshot shows a field inside a GTK OSD overlay (the standing premise the base groups' comment already records), so the etch is the landed field recipe and the mirror is this theme's adaptation because GTK 3 does not mirror `box-shadow` for direction; the four groups restate the etch at equal-or-higher specificity, so the landed plain mirror never reached an OSD RTL field (measured as in the Goal, this host, the date, a GTK 3 offscreen child); plain `entry` fields stay untouched because they have no steppers to cover the arm — the landed exclusion's reason stands for them.

2. `tests/test_gtk_theme_osd.py`: extend `test_osd_entry_fields` — its `expected` dict gains the four twin selectors each mapping to exactly `{"box-shadow": "inset -1px 1px #999999"}` and its family sweep over `self.rules` (every selector containing `.osd entry` or `.osd spinbutton` and no `" button"`) grows to include them, keeping the sweep's dropped-or-stray kill. Docstring gains one sentence naming the twins' reason. Add `test_osd_spin_field_mirrors_the_etch_in_rtl`, shaped like `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_rtl_spin_field_mirrors_the_etch`: count-one and exact-declaration pins for the four twins (the `expected` extension already pins the declarations; this test pins each twin's source position directly after its base group's selector in the comment-stripped sheet, killing a misplaced twin).

3. `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`: add `test_osd_spin_field_renders_the_mirrored_etch_in_rtl` directly after `test_horizontal_spinbutton_steppers_render_one_pixel_seams`, built from `_GTK3_CHILD_HEAD` and `_run_gtk_child` like that test: strip `url(...)` from the shipped sheet, install the provider, and render, in fresh `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`s, a `Gtk.SpinButton.new_with_range(0, 100, 1)` with `set_can_focus(False)` packed into a `Gtk.Box` with 5px border width whose style context carries `.osd`, once LTR and once with `set_direction(Gtk.TextDirection.RTL)`. Read the spin button's allocation and assert the Goal's measured edge columns — LTR `L+1` `#999999` ×4 and `R−1` `#000000` ×4; RTL `L+1` `#000000` ×4 and `R−1` `#999999` ×4.

4. `docs/invariants.md`: one new `## gtk` row beside the landed RTL-spin-field row (the row naming `test_rtl_spin_field_mirrors_the_etch`), naming both new tests and recording: the missing reference surface (no collected screenshot shows a GTK OSD overlay field), the provenance (the etch is the landed field recipe, the mirror is the theme's adaptation because GTK 3 does not mirror `box-shadow` for direction, and the four OSD groups restated it at higher specificity so the plain mirror never reached an OSD RTL field — measured, this host, 2026-11-11, a GTK 3 offscreen child, the shipped sheet reading `#999999`, `#FFFFFF`, `#FFFFFF`, `#FFFFFF` at RTL R−1), the entry-field exclusion with its reason, and that this resolves the landed entry's recorded OSD-family exclusion.

**Files.** `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme_osd.py`, `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- The GTK 3 sheet contains exactly one rule for each of the four twin selectors, each declaring exactly `box-shadow: inset -1px 1px #999999`, each placed directly after its base state group; the four base groups' declarations are unchanged, as are the landed plain mirror rule and every other `.osd` rule.
- `tests/test_gtk_theme_osd.py::test_osd_entry_fields` pins the four twins in its `expected` dict and family sweep and passes; `test_osd_spin_field_mirrors_the_etch_in_rtl` fails on a dropped twin, a stray extra spelling in the family, or a twin moved away from its base group.
- When GTK 3 introspection and a display are present, `test_osd_spin_field_renders_the_mirrored_etch_in_rtl` renders the OSD spin button reading LTR `L+1` `#999999` ×4 and `R−1` `#000000` ×4, and RTL `L+1` `#000000` ×4 and `R−1` `#999999` ×4; it fails with the base twin removed or spelled `inset 1px 1px #999999` (RTL `R−1` then reads `#FFFFFF` below the top arm) and it skips with the child's own reason where GTK 3 or a display is missing. (Criterion corrected 2026-11-11 by the feature role while implementing: the render exercises the base state only — an offscreen window cannot take focus and GTK cannot force the backdrop state in the probe — so a twin removed, misspelled or misplaced in any state fails the declaration tests instead; the render spec itself is unchanged.)
- `docs/invariants.md` carries the new row, and `make check` passes.

### GTK 3 child-probe harness: move the shared child-interpreter program heads and runner into tests/support/gtk_child_probe.py (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of every other entry — it touches only `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`'s harness block, the three `_GTK3_*` program-string constants and the `_run_gtk_child` method, and adds `tests/support/gtk_child_probe.py` plus one contract test, sharing no sheet rule, widget, probe assertion or invariants row with the waiting RTL spin-field entry or the in-flight vertical-spin-button branch, whose probes keep working unchanged whichever lands first because the imported names and the `_run_gtk_child` call surface stay; at implementation re-grep every anchor this entry names, since the two spin entries also extend this test file) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` (2,503 lines) carries, besides its probes and shipped-glyph tests, the GTK 3 child-probe harness: the three program-string constants `_GTK3_CHILD_HEAD`, `_GTK3_SHEET_AND_WINDOW` and `_GTK3_PIXEL_HEAD` and the `TestGtkThemeControls._run_gtk_child` runner that seven probes call through. The project's one-responsibility principle puts shared helpers in `tests/support` beside `snippet_child.py`, `gtk_css.py` and the rest; the waiting RTL spin-field entry and the in-flight vertical-spin-button branch each add more probes to this same file, and every landed GTK 3 probe plan (progress-bar fill, notebook faces, seam and frame probes) already describes its probe as built from these in-file pieces. Moving the harness gives the growing probe family a stable import surface and trims the test file without touching a single probe.

**Approach.**

1. New `tests/support/gtk_child_probe.py`: the module docstring carries the harness comment above the constants (the child interpreter's gi imports with their exit-77 skip guards, the sheet provider the `Gtk.OffscreenWindow` paints with, the pixel reader the assertions sample through, and why the GTK work runs in a child — an in-process `import gi` leaves GLib's C worker threads in the suite process, which `tests/test_no_gtk_introspection.py` pins) and the `_run_gtk_child` docstring's rationale. The three constants move byte-for-byte. Add `def run_gtk_child(test, program, *paths)` with the moved method body: `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", program, *paths], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)`, `returncode == 77` calls `test.skipTest(result.stdout.strip() or "GTK 3 is not available")`, otherwise `test.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout + result.stderr)`. The module imports only `subprocess` and `sys`; `gi` appears only inside string constants, which the AST scanner never sees as imports.

2. `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`: delete the constants block and the `_run_gtk_child` body. Import the three constants from `support.gtk_child_probe` and shrink the method to a one-line delegate — `return run_gtk_child(self, program, *paths)` — keeping its name, signature and a short docstring pointing at the support module. Every one of the seven call sites, every probe program and every prose mention of `_run_gtk_child` stays untouched.

3. New `tests/test_gtk_child_probe_support.py` (no GTK in the suite process, no introspection needed):
   - Pin `_GTK3_CHILD_HEAD`'s contract strings as substrings: `gi.require_version("Gtk", "3.0")` and `gi.require_version("Gdk", "3.0")`, the two skip reasons "GTK 3 introspection is not installed" and "no display for GTK 3" (the parent judges the child's printed reason, so the wording is the contract), and both `sys.exit(77)` guards.
   - Pin `_GTK3_PIXEL_HEAD`'s pixel reader: it defines `def at(x, y)` over the offscreen pixbuf's pixels, stride and channel count.
   - Pin `run_gtk_child` against a recorder object (methods `skipTest(reason)` and `assertEqual(a, b, msg=None)` that record instead of skipping): a child printing a reason and exiting 77 records a skip with that reason; a child exiting 1 with output records the failure assertion with the child's output attached; a child printing "ok" and exiting 0 records neither. This fails on the plausible swapped-branch bug — treating 77 as a failure or 0 as a skip.

No sheet, artwork or invariants change: the no-gi invariant row in `docs/invariants.md` pins `tests/test_no_gtk_introspection.py`, which scans `tests/` tree-wide and keeps passing over the new module unchanged; the GTK 4 counterpart head in `tests/test_gtk_view_census.py` stays where it is (its probes use the `GDK_BACKEND`/`GSK_RENDERER` pattern and are out of scope).

**Files.** `tests/support/gtk_child_probe.py` (new), `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`, `tests/test_gtk_child_probe_support.py` (new).

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `tests/support/gtk_child_probe.py` holds the three program-string constants byte-equal to the deleted block and defines `run_gtk_child`; `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` defines none of the four harness members itself beyond the one-line `_run_gtk_child` delegate and imports the three constants from `support.gtk_child_probe`; all seven call sites still read `self._run_gtk_child(...)` unchanged.
- A GTK 3 pixel probe renders the same pixels after the move as before it: the child programs are byte-identical concatenations, so every probe that passed before the move passes after it where GTK 3 introspection and a display are present, and skips with the child's own reason where they are missing — the probe set's behavior is unchanged.
- `tests/test_no_gtk_introspection.py` passes unchanged over the new support module, and `tests/test_no_unused_imports.py` reports no finding in the touched files.
- The new contract test pins the head's guard strings, the pixel reader's presence and `run_gtk_child`'s three exit-status behaviors (77 → skip with the child's reason, nonzero → failure with the child's output attached, 0 → pass), and fails when the 77 and 0 branches are swapped.
- `make check` passes.

### Platinum GTK 3 spin field in RTL: mirror the etch's inset arm to the field's exposed edge and pin it in the seam probe (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of every other entry — it adds one rule to the GTK 3 sheet directly after the landed `entry, spinbutton:not(.vertical)` rule, one declaration test to `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, extends the landed probe `test_horizontal_spinbutton_steppers_render_one_pixel_seams` in `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` and adds one `## gtk` row to `docs/invariants.md`, sharing no sheet region, test or invariants row with the waiting flat-`Gtk.Frame` entry or the queued vertical-spin-button entry; at implementation re-read the landed field rule and the horizontal-seam record and its probe, and re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed field rule `entry, spinbutton:not(.vertical)` etches the spin field with `box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999`, and GTK 3 does not mirror `box-shadow` for right-to-left text direction. In a horizontal RTL spin button the steppers therefore overlay the entry node's left edge and cover the etch's vertical arm, so the exposed field draws only the horizontal top arm — a half-etched field, where the LTR field shows the full L. Measured 2026-11-11 on this host with the shipped `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` (`url(...)` stripped) in a child-interpreter `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`: a `Gtk.SpinButton.new_with_range(0, 100, 1)` with focus disabled, packed in a `Gtk.Box` with a 5px border width, allocation L,T,R,B = 5,5,110,36, its four black columns at L, 52, 81, R in LTR and at L, 34, 63, R in RTL (the steppers sit left of the field in RTL). The column at L+1 read `#999999` at T+1, T+2, T+3 and B−1 in LTR; in RTL the same column read `#FFFFFF` at T+1…T+3 and `#AAAAAA` at B−1 (the steppers' face over the arm), and the exposed field's other edge read `#999999` at T+1 only, then `#FFFFFF` — no vertical arm at either exposed edge. That GTK 3 keeps the arm at the covered left column rather than mirroring it is itself measured: if the toolkit mirrored `box-shadow`, the RTL column at R−1 would read `#999999` below T+1 and it reads `#FFFFFF` in the shipped sheet. No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK spin button in any direction (the standing GTK-scope adaptation premise); the etch is the theme's own landed recipe, and mirroring it keeps the RTL field's sunken L at its exposed outer edge, the same corner the LTR field's L sits at.

**Approach.** In the GTK 3 sheet, directly after the `entry, spinbutton:not(.vertical)` rule, add this rule with a short dated comment naming the landed etch it mirrors, the measured covered-arm defect above, GTK 3's non-mirrored `box-shadow`, and the mirrored result:
- `spinbutton:dir(rtl):not(.vertical) { box-shadow: inset -1px 1px #999999; }`

The mirror out-specifies the base rule per-property (two pseudo-classes against one), so it wins the plain RTL field's `box-shadow` at any source position; placing it beside the base rule keeps the record together. Change nothing else. A scratch copy of the sheet with exactly this rule at exactly that position, rendered as above, gave:
- **LTR:** unchanged — the column at L+1 read `#999999` at T+1, T+2, T+3, B−1 and the column at R−1 `#AAAAAA` at those rows; the four black columns stayed at L, 52, 81, R.
- **RTL:** the column at R−1 read `#999999` at T+1, T+2, T+3 and B−1 (was `#999999` at T+1 only); the column at L+1 kept the steppers' `#FFFFFF`, `#FFFFFF`, `#FFFFFF`, `#AAAAAA`; the four black columns stayed at L, 34, 63, R.

Exclusions with reasons, recorded in the comment and the invariants row: the four `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical)` state groups restate the etch at equal-or-higher specificity, so their RTL fields keep the covered arm; giving them `:dir(rtl)` twins would multiply the overlay-scoped OSD record across its four states, so the OSD family is this entry's own future candidate, not part of it. Plain `entry` fields are untouched — the plan measures only the spin field, whose overlay is the defect. The rule carries `:not(.vertical)`, so vertical spin fields cannot match it. GTK 4 is out of scope: its spin button uses a different node tree and its probe cannot run on a host without Xvfb.

**Tests.**
1. `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_rtl_spin_field_mirrors_the_etch`, shaped like `test_rtl_collapsed_expander_arrows`: `assert_rule` pins the mirror's single declaration exactly, and `self.selectors.count("spinbutton:dir(rtl):not(.vertical)")` equals exactly 1.
2. Extend `test_horizontal_spinbutton_steppers_render_one_pixel_seams` in `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`: inside its LTR/RTL loop, after the seam assertions, read the columns at L+1 and R−1 at rows T+1, T+2, T+3 and B−1 and assert the two measured column results above — this fails on the shipped sheet (RTL R−1 reads `#FFFFFF` at T+2 and B−1) and on a mirror added to the wrong side (RTL L+1 would then read `#999999`).

### Platinum GTK 3 vertical spin button: draw each field/stepper join as one 1px black line and pin it with an offscreen pixel probe (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of every other entry — it extends the two landed `spinbutton.vertical button.up`/`button.down` rules in the GTK 3 sheet, extends one test in `tests/test_gtk_theme_views.py` and adds one probe to `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` and one `## gtk` row to `docs/invariants.md`, sharing no sheet region, test or invariants row with the waiting flat-`Gtk.Frame` entry; at implementation re-read the landed radius record and its comment, `test_vertical_stepper_and_content_view_check_corners`, `test_horizontal_spinbutton_steppers_render_one_pixel_seams` and the horizontal-seam invariants row, and re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** A vertical GTK 3 spin button stacks its up stepper on top, the field in the middle and the down stepper below, and each member paints its own full 1px black border, so both field/stepper joins draw adjacent 2px black lines. Measured 2026-11-11 on this host with the shipped `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` (`url(...)` stripped) in a child-interpreter `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`: a `Gtk.SpinButton.new_with_range(0, 100, 1)` with `set_orientation(Gtk.Orientation.VERTICAL)` and `set_can_focus(False)`, packed in a `Gtk.Box` with a 5px border width, allocation L,T,R,B = 5,5,36,88. The column at L+3 read `#000000` at both rows T+27 and T+28 (the up stepper's bottom border beside the field's top border) and at both rows T+55 and T+56 (the field's bottom border beside the down stepper's top border); the top and bottom edges were single. Rendered with the stock resource extracted the same day, the same widget draws exactly one 1px separator line at each join and no adjacent doubles.

The stock resource GTK 3 ships avoids the doubling by splitting the steppers' border-style: re-extracted with `gresource` on 2026-11-11, `gtk-contained.css` inside `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0` declares `spinbutton.vertical button.up { … border-style: solid solid none solid; }` (resource line 532) and `spinbutton.vertical button.down { … border-style: none solid solid solid; }` (resource line 534). Selecting this theme replaces that resource, so neither half reaches the steppers — the landed radius record's comment claims these halves "stay inherited per-property", which the doubling measurement disproves on the selecting path. The landed record already restates both rules' `border-radius: 0`, and this plan extends those same two rules rather than adding new ones, because `test_vertical_stepper_and_content_view_check_corners` pins that exactly one rule in the sheet carries each of the two spellings. No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK spin button.

**Approach.** In the GTK 3 sheet, change the two landed radius rules to:
- `spinbutton.vertical button.up { border-radius: 0; border-style: solid solid none solid; }`
- `spinbutton.vertical button.down { border-radius: 0; border-style: none solid solid solid; }`

and extend the comment above them with a dated note naming the stock border-style halves being restated, their resource lines and extraction date, the doubling measurement that corrects the comment's per-property-inheritance claim, and the result: the up stepper keeps its solid head and the down keeps its solid tail, so the field's own 1px borders supply each join's single line. Change nothing else. Under the lower-sheet reading the extended declarations stay per-property ties with stock that later source order wins; under the replacing reading they now carry the halves. A scratch copy of the sheet with exactly these two extended rules rendered as above gave, in LTR and RTL alike, allocation height 82 (was 84) and:
- exactly four fully-black rows — T, T+27, T+54 and B — each a single 1px line, no adjacent pair;
- the column at L+3 read `#000000` at T, `#FFFFFF` at T+1, `#DDDDDD` at T+2, `#AAAAAA` at the row before the first join, `#000000` at the first join, `#999999` at the row after it, `#FFFFFF` at the row after that (the field's etched face), `#000000` at the second join, `#FFFFFF` at the row after it, `#DDDDDD` from the next row to two rows above B, `#AAAAAA` at B−1 and `#000000` at B.

The `.osd spinbutton.vertical button:first-child` groups declare no border-style, so the restated halves shape the OSD's stacked steppers the same way stock's own halves shape them; no OSD test pins border-style there. The landed horizontal-seam rules and the `.osd` groups are untouched. GTK 4 is out of scope: its vertical steppers use a different node tree (`spinbutton.vertical > button`) with its own landed geometry arms, and its probe cannot run on a host without Xvfb.

Tests:
1. `tests/test_gtk_theme_views.py::test_vertical_stepper_and_content_view_check_corners` — extend the two stepper dictionaries in its `assert_rule_group` call with the border-style declarations and update its docstring, which today says the two groups rest stock's end halves at zero radius only.
2. A pixel probe in `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`, directly after `test_horizontal_spinbutton_steppers_render_one_pixel_seams`: `test_vertical_spinbutton_renders_one_pixel_joins`, built like that test from `_GTK3_CHILD_HEAD`, the url-stripped sheet and `_run_gtk_child`, rendering the vertical spin button above once LTR and once with `set_direction(Gtk.TextDirection.RTL)`, each in a fresh `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`. It finds the fully-black rows from the allocation and asserts the two measured results above.

Add one `## gtk` row to `docs/invariants.md` directly after the landed horizontal-spin-button seam row, naming both tests and recording: no reference screenshot shows a GTK spin button; the stock resource path, the two resource lines and the 2026-11-11 extraction date the selector spelling comes from; the doubled-join measurement that corrects the radius record's inheritance claim; and the measured render (this host, the date, a GTK 3 offscreen child). In the same change, reword the horizontal-seam row's trailing clause "the vertical spin button is unchanged" to point at the new row instead.
