Each spelling still names exactly one rule in the sheet, and no `.osd spinbutton` rule changes.
- When GTK 3 introspection and a display are present, a vertical spin button rendered with the shipped sheet paints exactly four fully-black single-row lines across its allocation — its top edge, the field/stepper join, the two-steppers' join and its bottom edge — with no adjacent black pair, in LTR and in RTL.
- The up stepper's column keeps the raised button pattern `#000000`, `#FFFFFF`, `#DDDDDD` at its head rows and `#AAAAAA` above its removed bottom border; the field column keeps `#000000`, `#999999`, `#FFFFFF` after its top border; the down stepper keeps `#FFFFFF`, `#DDDDDD` at its head rows after its removed top border and `#AAAAAA`, `#000000` at its bottom edge. All hold in LTR and RTL.

### Platinum GTK 3 flat frame: draw no border or inset shadow on a `Gtk.Frame` whose shadow type is NONE (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of every other entry. It adds one rule to the GTK 3 sheet, two tests to `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` and one `## gtk` row to `docs/invariants.md`. When implementing, re-read the sheet's `frame > border, .frame` rule and any `scrolledwindow viewport.frame` rule that has landed beside it, and re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** A GTK 3 `Gtk.Frame` set to `Gtk.ShadowType.NONE` asks for no frame: GTK gives its `border` node the `flat` style class. The sheet's `frame > border, .frame` rule (`border: 1px solid #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999`) still matches that node, so a flat frame draws exactly the same sunken frame as a shadow-IN one. Measured 2026-11-11 on this host with the shipped `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` (`url(...)` stripped), in a child-interpreter `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`: a label-less `Gtk.Frame()` with `set_size_request(40, 30)`, packed in a `Gtk.Box` with a 5px border width, allocation L,T,R,B = 5,5,44,34. With shadow NONE, the middle column read `#000000`, `#999999`, `#DDDDDD` at T, T+1, T+2 and `#DDDDDD`, `#DDDDDD`, `#000000` at B−2, B−1, B, and the middle row read the same at L…L+2 and R−2…R — identical to shadow IN — in LTR and with `set_direction(Gtk.TextDirection.RTL)`.

The stock resource GTK 3 ships avoids this: `gtk-contained.css` inside `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0`, re-extracted with `gresource` 2026-11-11, declares `frame > border.flat, .frame.flat { border-style: none; }`. Selecting this theme replaces that resource, and the sheet does not restate the reset (`grep -n 'border\.flat\|frame\.flat'` over `theme/` finds nothing). The stock reset alone is not enough, because the sheet adds an inset `box-shadow` stock frames lack: a scratch copy with only `border-style: none` still read `#999999` at T and at L for shadow NONE. No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK frame.

**Approach.** Directly after the `frame > border, .frame` rule in the GTK 3 sheet (after the `scrolledwindow viewport.frame` rule if that waiting entry has landed there), add this rule with a short provenance comment naming the stock spelling, its extraction date, why `box-shadow` is reset too, and the measurement above:
- `frame > border.flat, .frame.flat { border-style: none; box-shadow: none; }`

Change nothing else. A scratch copy of the sheet with exactly this rule, rendered as above, gave:
- **IN:** unchanged — the middle column read `#000000`, `#999999`, `#DDDDDD` at T…T+2 and `#DDDDDD`, `#DDDDDD`, `#000000` at B−2…B; the middle row the same at L…L+2 and R−2…R; in LTR and RTL.
- **NONE:** all twelve of those pixels read `#DDDDDD`, in LTR and RTL.

GTK 4 is out of scope: `Gtk.Frame` there has no shadow type, and its probe cannot run on a host without Xvfb. The labelled frame's label gap is a separate question.

Tests go in `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`, after `test_progressbar_fill_spans_the_trough` (after the scrolled-viewport tests if those have landed):
1. **Declaration test.** `test_flat_frame_draws_no_border` uses `assert_rule` to pin the rule's two declarations exactly.
2. **Pixel probe.** `test_flat_frame_renders_no_frame` is built from `_GTK3_CHILD_HEAD` and runs through `_run_gtk_child`. Like `test_progressbar_fill_spans_the_trough`, it strips `url(...)`, installs the provider once and renders each case in a fresh `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`: the frame above with shadow IN and with shadow NONE, each in LTR and RTL. It reads L, T, R and B from `frame.get_allocation()` and samples the middle column and middle row.

Add a `## gtk` row to `docs/invariants.md` beside the other GTK 3 pixel-probe rows. It names both tests and records the provenance: no reference screenshot shows a GTK frame; the stock resource path and extraction date the selector spelling comes from; why `box-shadow` is reset too; the measured render (this host, the date, a GTK 3 offscreen child).

### Platinum GTK 3 scrolled window: stop a wrapped viewport from drawing a second frame inside the scrolled window's own (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of every other entry. It adds one rule to the GTK 3 sheet, two tests to `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` and one `## gtk` row to `docs/invariants.md`. When implementing, re-read the sheet's `frame > border, .frame` rule and its `placessidebar > viewport.frame` rule, and re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** A GTK 3 scrolled window whose child cannot scroll itself (a `Gtk.Box`, a grid, a preferences page) wraps that child in a `Gtk.Viewport`. That viewport carries the `frame` style class, so the sheet's `frame > border, .frame` rule (`border: 1px solid #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999`) gives it a sunken frame of its own. The viewport draws that frame inside whatever the scrolled window draws. Measured 2026-11-11 on this host with the shipped `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`: a child-interpreter `Gtk.OffscreenWindow` held a `Gtk.ScrolledWindow` (size request 30×30, both scrollbar policies `NEVER`, `add(Gtk.Box())`) packed in a `Gtk.Box` with a 5px border width. The viewport's class list was `['frame']`.
- **`set_shadow_type(Gtk.ShadowType.IN)`:** the column through the middle read `#000000`, `#000000`, `#999999` at T, T+1, T+2 and `#000000`, `#000000` at B−1, B. The row through the middle read the same at L…L+2 and R−1, R. That is a 2px black frame, where an ordinary sunken scrolled window (one holding a `Gtk.TextView`) draws 1px.
- **`set_shadow_type(Gtk.ShadowType.NONE)`:** the window asks for no frame, yet the viewport still drew a 1px black frame with a `#999999` inset (`#000000`, `#999999`, `#DDDDDD` at T…T+2; `#000000` at B).

The stock resource GTK 3 ships avoids the doubled frame: `gtk-contained.css` inside `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0`, re-extracted with `gresource` 2026-11-11, declares `scrolledwindow viewport.frame { border-style: none; }`. Selecting this theme replaces that resource. The sheet restates the reset only for `placessidebar > viewport.frame`. The stock reset is not enough by itself, because the sheet adds an inset `box-shadow` that stock frames do not have. A scratch copy with only `border-style: none` fixed the IN case, but the NONE case still read `#999999` at T and L. No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK scrolled window.

**Approach.** Directly after the `frame > border, .frame` rule in the GTK 3 sheet, add this rule with a short provenance comment. The comment names the stock spelling, its extraction date, why `box-shadow` is reset as well, and the doubled-frame measurement:
- `scrolledwindow viewport.frame { border-style: none; box-shadow: none; }`

Change nothing else. The scrolled window keeps drawing its own frame. The existing `placessidebar > viewport.frame` rule stays: the new rule also clears that viewport's inset shadow, which is the intended result. A scratch copy of the sheet with exactly this rule, rendered as above, gave the following, in LTR and with `set_direction(Gtk.TextDirection.RTL)` alike:
- **IN:** the middle column read `#000000`, `#999999`, `#DDDDDD` at T…T+2 and `#DDDDDD`, `#DDDDDD`, `#000000` at B−2…B. The middle row read the same at L…L+2 and R−2…R.
- **NONE:** all six of those pixels read `#DDDDDD` in both the column and the row.

GTK 4 is out of scope: its viewports carry no `frame` class, and its probe cannot run on a host without Xvfb. The flat `Gtk.Frame` (`set_shadow_type(NONE)`, which the sheet also still draws as a full sunken frame because stock's `frame > border.flat, .frame.flat { border-style: none; }` is not restated) is a separate fix.

Tests go in `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`, after `test_progressbar_fill_spans_the_trough`:
1. **Declaration test.** `test_scrolled_viewport_draws_no_frame` uses `assert_rule` to pin the rule's two declarations exactly.
2. **Pixel probe.** `test_scrolled_viewport_renders_one_frame` is built from `_GTK3_CHILD_HEAD` and runs through `_run_gtk_child`. Like `test_progressbar_fill_spans_the_trough`, it strips `url(...)`, installs the provider once and renders each case in a fresh `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`. The cases are the scrolled window above with shadow IN and with shadow NONE, each in LTR and RTL. The probe reads L, T, R and B from `scrolled.get_allocation()` and samples the middle column and middle row.

### Platinum GTK 3 horizontal spin button: draw each stepper seam as one 1px black line and pin it with an offscreen pixel probe (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of every other entry — it adds two rules to the GTK 3 sheet, two tests to `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` and one `## gtk` row to `docs/invariants.md`; at implementation re-read the sheet's `button` rule and the linked-group seam rules, and re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** In a horizontal GTK 3 spin button, the − and + stepper buttons paint the sheet's full `button` border (`1px solid #000000`) inside the spin button's own 1px black field border. Every place where a stepper meets the frame or another stepper therefore draws a 2px black line, but Platinum draws all of these edges 1px wide. Measured 2026-11-11 on this host with the shipped `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` (child-interpreter `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`, a `Gtk.SpinButton.new_with_range(0, 100, 1)` with focus disabled, packed in a `Gtk.Box` with a 5px border width so the frame is not clipped):
- Every stepper column is `#000000` at both the spin button's top row and the row below it, and at both its bottom row and the row above it.
- The trailing edge is two black columns.
- The seam between the two steppers is two black columns.
- An RTL spin button mirrors all of this; its black columns at the row 4px below the top were x 5, 6, 35, 36, 65 and 112.

The sheet has no `spinbutton … button` rule outside `.osd` and the vertical radius pair (`grep -n 'spinbutton[^{]*button'`). The stock resource GTK 3 ships, `gtk-contained.css` inside `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0`, avoids the problem by restyling these buttons: re-extracted with `gresource` 2026-11-11, it declares `spinbutton:not(.vertical) button { … border-style: none none none solid; … }` and `spinbutton:not(.vertical) button:dir(rtl) { border-style: none solid none none; }`. Selecting this theme replaces that resource, so neither rule reaches the steppers. No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK spin button. The one-seam result follows the landed linked-group scheme (`.linked:not(.vertical) > …` strips each member's trailing border so a group paints one 1px seam).

**Approach.** Add these two rules to the GTK 3 sheet directly after the vertical-stepper radius pair (`spinbutton.vertical button.up` / `spinbutton.vertical button.down`), with a short provenance comment naming the stock spelling, its extraction date and the doubled-seam measurement:
- `spinbutton:not(.vertical) button { border-style: none none none solid; }`
- `spinbutton:not(.vertical) button:dir(rtl) { border-style: none solid none none; }`

Change nothing else. The width and colour stay `1px #000000` from `button`, and the steppers keep the plain push-button face and bevel. A scratch render with exactly these two rules gave the following (spin-button allocation L,T,R,B = 5,5,110,36):
- In LTR, the row at T+4 had black columns at exactly x 5, 52, 81 and 110, and no two were adjacent.
- In RTL, the black columns were at x 5, 34, 63 and 110.
- Three columns inside each stepper, away from its seam, each stepper read `#000000` at T, `#FFFFFF` at T+1, `#DDDDDD` at T+2, `#AAAAAA` at B−1 and `#000000` at B.
- A field column still read `#000000` / `#999999` / `#FFFFFF` at T, T+1, T+2.

These rules do not reach the `.osd` stepper groups. Those groups use a full border on purpose, and their higher-specificity rules keep it. The vertical spin button is out of scope; it doubles at its field/stepper joins too, but that is a separate fix. So is GTK 4, whose probe cannot run on a host without Xvfb.

Tests go in `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`, after `test_vertical_spinbutton_focus_outline`:
1. A declaration test, `test_horizontal_spinbutton_steppers_share_one_seam`, uses `assert_rule` to pin the two rules.
2. A pixel probe, `test_horizontal_spinbutton_steppers_render_one_pixel_seams`, is built from `_GTK3_CHILD_HEAD`, `_GTK3_SHEET_AND_WINDOW` and `_GTK3_PIXEL_HEAD`, runs through `_run_gtk_child`, and strips `url(...)` as `test_entry_progress_draws_a_two_pixel_strip` does. It renders the spin button above once LTR and once with `set_direction(Gtk.TextDirection.RTL)`, each in a fresh `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`. It reads the edges from `spin.get_allocation()` and finds the seams by scanning row T+4, so it does not hard-code the stepper widths.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- The GTK 3 sheet contains `spinbutton:not(.vertical) button` declaring exactly `border-style: none none none solid`, and `spinbutton:not(.vertical) button:dir(rtl)` declaring exactly `border-style: none solid none none`. No `.osd spinbutton` rule changes.

No two of them are adjacent, and the two seams lie in the trailing part of the widget, right of the field.

- A field column of the same LTR render still reads `#000000`, `#999999`, `#FFFFFF` at T, T+1, T+2 and `#000000` at B.
- An RTL render shows the mirror image: four non-adjacent black columns at T+4, with the two seams left of the field, and each stepper column reads the same five colours.
- With the two new rules removed, the probe fails. The shipped sheet before this change has adjacent black columns at row T+4 and reads `#000000` at T+1 of a stepper column.
- Where GTK 3 introspection or a display is missing, the probe skips with the child's own reason, as the other GTK 3 pixel probes do. The suite process never imports `gi` (`tests/test_no_gtk_introspection.py` still passes). `make check` passes.

### Platinum GTK 3 progress bar: span the fill across the trough interior and pin it with an offscreen pixel probe (planned 2026-11-11 by the plan role; independent of every other entry — it touches only the GTK 3 sheet's two oriented fill rules, `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py` and `docs/invariants.md`'s GTK 3 meter rows; at implementation re-read the landed meter rules and their comment block and re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-11 by the feature role

**Goal.** A GTK 3 progress bar draws its fill as a thin strip centred in the trough, not as the full-height bar the reference meter shows. Measured 2026-11-11 on this host with the shipped `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` (child-interpreter `Gtk.OffscreenWindow`, a 100×10 default-size window holding a horizontal `Gtk.ProgressBar` at fraction 0.5): the trough renders 12px tall (1px `#000000` border rows 0 and 11, `#999999` inset arm at row 1 and column 1, `#EEEEEE` face), but the `#CCCCFF` fill covers only rows 4–7 — 4px of the trough's 10px interior — leaving `#EEEEEE` above and below it. The disabled `#999999` fill shows the same 4px strip. The reference meter fills every interior row: `tests/test_desktoptheme_progressbar.py`'s `FILL_ROWS` samples ten 1px fill rows from `desktop_fandom.png`'s memory meter. The sheet's own comment above `progressbar.horizontal trough` asserts that the fill's "natural allocation already spans the trough", and that is the reason it gives for declaring no fill minimum; the render shows the claim is false. GTK 3 gives the fill its own preferred cross-axis size and centres it in the trough.

**Approach.** In the GTK 3 sheet, add `min-height: 10px` to the existing `progressbar.horizontal progress` rule and `min-width: 10px` to the existing `progressbar.vertical progress` rule. Both rules already hold `margin: 0`, and 10px is the trough's existing interior minimum. Do not add new selectors: `test_meter_geometry`'s family sweep allows only the existing spellings. A scratch render with exactly these two declarations filled the horizontal bar's interior rows 1–10 at the filled columns, and the vertical bar's (12×100) interior columns 1–10 at the filled rows from the top. The fill paints over the trough's inset arm where it covers it, and the unfilled part keeps the `#999999` arm and `#EEEEEE` face. Rewrite the incorrect sentence in the comment block so it records the measured centring and the new minimum instead. `progressbar.osd progress` declares no minimum of its own and its trough is also 10px, so the oriented rules span it the same way. The `entry progress` strip and the `treeview.view.progressbar` cell use different selectors and are unaffected. GTK 4 is out of scope because its probe cannot run on a host without Xvfb. Add `test_progressbar_fill_spans_the_trough` to `TestGtkThemeControls` next to `test_entry_progress_draws_a_two_pixel_strip`. Build it from the same `_GTK3_CHILD_HEAD` / `_GTK3_SHEET_AND_WINDOW` / `_GTK3_PIXEL_HEAD` pieces, run it through `_run_gtk_child`, and strip `url(...)` as that test does. The child should render three bars in turn (a fresh `Gtk.OffscreenWindow` each): horizontal enabled, horizontal insensitive (`set_sensitive(False)`) and vertical enabled, all at fraction 0.5. Sample columns or rows well clear of the fill's end (for example x 25 and x 75 on the 100px bar) so the pin does not transcribe GTK's rounding of the fill length. Update `test_meter_geometry`'s whole-rule dicts for the two fill spellings. Add the minimum to `docs/invariants.md`'s GTK 3 meter-geometry row (the `test_meter_geometry` row), and append a `## gtk` row for the rendered probe that records the measured-render provenance (host, date, GTK 3 offscreen child) and the `FILL_ROWS` reference for the full-height fill, following the landed GTK 3 notebook render row's form.

**Files.** `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme_controls.py`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- When GTK 3 introspection and a display are present, a horizontal 0.5-fraction bar rendered with the shipped sheet reads `#CCCCFF` at every interior row (trough rows 1 through 10) of a column inside the filled half, including row 1 where the inset arm would otherwise show. A column inside the unfilled half reads `#999999` at row 1, `#EEEEEE` at rows 2–10, and `#000000` at rows 0 and 11.
- The insensitive horizontal bar reads `#999999` at every interior row of a filled-half column. Its unfilled half matches the enabled bar's.
- The vertical 0.5-fraction bar reads `#CCCCFF` at every interior column (1 through 10) of a row inside the filled top half. A row inside the unfilled bottom half reads `#999999` at column 1 and `#EEEEEE` at columns 2–10.
- With the sheet's two new declarations removed, the probe fails: the shipped sheet before this change renders `#EEEEEE` at rows 2–3 and 8–10 of a filled column.
- Where GTK 3 introspection or a display is missing, the probe skips with the child's own reason, as the other GTK 3 pixel probes do. The suite process never imports `gi` (`tests/test_no_gtk_introspection.py` still passes).
- `test_meter_geometry` pins `progressbar.horizontal progress` as exactly `{margin: 0, min-height: 10px}` and `progressbar.vertical progress` as exactly `{margin: 0, min-width: 10px}`. Its family sweeps admit no new spelling. The sheet comment no longer claims that the fill's natural allocation spans the trough. `make check` passes.

### Reusable deterministic fixtures for recurring no-fake validation gaps (planned 2026-11-10 by the steward role; promote the recurring `no-fake` tag and scope the first deliverable to process-start races and bounded filesystem reads) — retired 2026-11-11 by the plan role

**Retired 2026-11-11 by plan: the shared fixtures already exist on main (236483302 is an ancestor) — `tests/support/popen_signal.py` is used by `tests/test_process_group.py` for the Popen-return signal races, and `tests/support/fifo_fixtures.py` with the bounded `tests/support/snippet_child.py::run` (timeout parameter) is used by the Firefox FIFO tests in `tests/test_firefox_profile.py`.**

**Goal.** The archive records repeated missing-fake gaps for the same validation patterns: SIGINT and SIGTERM arriving as `Popen` returns (BUGS-FIXED.md, “A SIGINT while a child starts can leave the caller without cleanup” and “A SIGTERM that arrives while a child starts leaves the command running”), and FIFO paths requiring bounded child checks (BUGS-FIXED.md, “A FIFO at either Firefox profile-discovery INI file blocks the install” and “A FIFO at a Firefox profile file blocks the install forever”). Each fix added its own fixture after the absence of one made confirmation harder. Reduce that repeated setup cost without introducing a dependency or obscuring each test's behavior.

**Approach and files.** Inspect the cited tests and `tests/support/` first. Identify the smallest reusable standard-library helpers for (1) injecting a signal at a controlled `Popen` return boundary and (2) running a child with a bounded timeout against a FIFO fixture. Add a helper only if it removes duplicated setup across the cited cases while keeping assertions and cleanup visible at the call site; otherwise document why the existing tests are already the appropriate reusable pattern and close the plan with that finding. Update the relevant test modules and any focused helper documentation, then run `make check`. Keep this effort limited to these two recurring fixture patterns; do not generalize every historical `no-fake` case into a fixture framework.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- The cited signal-race and FIFO tests use shared, narrowly named helpers where setup is genuinely duplicated, and retain explicit assertions for signal outcome, child termination, timeout, and cleanup.
- Helpers use only the standard library, have focused tests if they introduce behavior, and do not leave child processes or temporary files behind on failure.
- If inspection finds no meaningful shared setup, record the evidence in the plan's Done epitaph instead of adding abstraction. `make check` passes after the final edit.

**Goal.** The sampler is PNG-only: `python3 tools/sample.py` pointed at one of the reference set's JPEG screenshots (verified 2026-11-10 against `macos8.6-screenshots/opendialog_macrumors86.jpg`) exits 2 with `error: cannot decode <path>: not a PNG file: the input is a JPEG image, not a PNG; convert it to PNG first` — a refusal whose own text promises a conversion. Measuring a JPEG-distributed reference surface (e.g. the Open dialog's push-button recipes cite `opendialog_macrumors86.jpg`) currently needs a manual `convert` round-trip whose output path, naming and cleanup the operator nurses by hand. Let the sampler do that decoding itself: a JPEG input is sniffed at open, converted once through ImageMagick into a private temporary PNG, and then sampled exactly like a PNG today. The PNG decode pipeline in `tools/png/` stays stdlib-only PNG; this plan adds the conversion bridge beside the disk layer, not inside the package.

**Approach and files.** Add `tools/jpeg_convert.py`, a small module beside the PNG package holding everything the sampler's JPEG branch shares: `JPEG_MAGIC = bytes((0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF))`; `is_jpeg(head: bytes) -> bool`; and `convert_jpeg(input_bytes: bytes, temp_png: Path) -> str | None` that resolves `convert` with `shutil.which` and, when it is absent, returns a diagnostic naming `convert` (the same message shape the sampler's other refusals print), otherwise runs `convert jpeg:- PNG24:<temp_png>` with the bytes piped on stdin, supervised through `tools/process_group.py::run_logged_split` (its new optional `stdin_bytes` parameter, default None, carries the piped bytes, so every existing caller that passes nothing is untouched; returning the failure text through its non-zero-status path), and returns None on success — the output is written into a caller-provided path inside a private `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`, never the input's directory, so the user's tree is untouched and no planted path is followed. In `tools/sample.py::main`, after the existing fd open, containment and regular-file checks, `os.pread` the fd's first three bytes — a read on the already-open stable procfs handle, so a concurrent symlink swap cannot change what is sniffed — and route through a JPEG branch when `is_jpeg` holds: (1) a `--alpha` or `--match-alpha` refusal fires before any conversion, naming that flag, exiting 2, because a JPEG carries no alpha channel to sample or match; (2) the fd is read whole with `os.pread`, the private temp directory is created, and a `convert_jpeg` problem returns through `report_error` naming the user-facing path like every other failure while a success continues with `read_png_size` and `read_png` on the temp PNG, the same `region_error` bounds check as today running against the JPEG's own decoded size, and any `PngError` message carrying the temp path rewritten to `args.image` by the landed `/proc/self/fd` rewrite's pattern; (3) the `image:` header line still names `args.image`, now with the decoded JPEG's width x height. The non-JPEG path keeps the entire current code path byte for byte: same `read_png_size`/`read_png` calls, same refusal texts, no subprocess, so the `--alpha` and `--match-alpha` PNG behaviors are unchanged. No change to `tools/fidelity.py`; this plan covers the sampler only. README's `## Sampling reference pixels` opening paragraph gains one sentence: JPEG inputs are converted with ImageMagick before sampling, `--alpha` and `--match-alpha` need a PNG because JPEG carries no alpha, and the reference set's JPEG screenshots are readable directly. docs/invariants.md's `## tooling` table gains one dated (2026-11-10) end-of-table row naming the new tests, the JPEG flag rejection, ImageMagick's input-format decode, and that the PNG decoder itself is unchanged.

**Fixtures.** `tests/support/jpeg_sampler_fixture.py` ships a deterministic tiny JPEG as a base64 constant: the feature run generates it once with `convert` from a deterministic small RGB quilt (e.g. 32x24 colored blocks with distinct RGB values) and, alongside the base64, records the exact post-conversion decoded RGB triples measured once through the completed sampler, written as literal constants (the JPEG artifact, like the reference set's own JPEGs, is measured evidence, not a computed value). The test thus never runs ImageMagick at check time: it base64-decodes the shipped bytes and exercises `is_jpeg` and the sampler end to end against the recorded constants; give the fixture file a one-line provenance comment naming the generation date and command.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `python3 tools/sample.py <fixture>.jpg <x> <y> --width 3 --height 2` prints the pinned RGB triples and hex literals for that pinned region, identical to the recorded constants; `--histogram` and `--runs` over pinned regions report exactly the recorded counts; `--find-color` with a recorded hex literal yields the recorded match coordinates. The `image:` header line names the user-facing `.jpg` path with the decoded JPEG's own width x height.
- JPEG with `--alpha` or `--match-alpha` exits 2 with a message naming that flag before any conversion runs; the same flags on a PNG still work exactly as today.
- With `convert` absent from PATH (test by monkeypatching `shutil.which` in `tools.jpeg_convert` or by an empty-PATH subprocess environment), a JPEG input exits 2 with a diagnostic naming `convert` and reaches no other read. A truncated JPEG whose bytes decode to no valid image exits 2 with a diagnostic naming the user-facing `.jpg` path, never the temp one.
- Every existing PNG-path sampler test passes unchanged and the fixture test asserts the JPEG branch is not entered for a PNG input (no conversion attempt, no subprocess); non-PNG non-JPEG bytes keep today's exact `not a PNG file` refusal. `make check` passes after the final edit.

### Kvantum icon dialog render gate: pin a captured kdialog icon chooser's sunken list field, top-row search field and push buttons on the landed art recipe (planned 2026-11-10 by the plan role; the same CLI-plumbing files as the waiting color-dialog entry ahead of it, a further widget surface — the two entries share no assertion region and may merge in any order, so at implementation re-read the landed mode lists and re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-10 by the feature role

**Goal.** No render gate captures the icon chooser dialog: kdialog's `--geticon` opens KDE's icon chooser, whose search row, sunken icon-list field and push buttons are drawn by the widget engine with the theme's palette and art, so a change to the landed color scheme ([Colors:Window] `BackgroundNormal=221,221,221`, [Colors:View] `BackgroundNormal=255,255,255` in `theme/color-schemes/MacOS8.colors`) or to the engine's line-edit, item-view or push-button painting would ship green. Verified today (2026-11-10) on this host: a probe full-lifecycle render sequenced through `tools/render_workflow.py`'s setup (Session.create, install_theme, link_kvantum_themes, write_session_configs with `_dialog_config_files()`, write_kvantum_selection, session_command settle 8, 480x360 virtual desktop, timeout 90, run_logged; client `kdialog --title Test --geticon application ""` — no default, format or date pin needed) returned a themed capture: the Aurorae title-bar strip over a flat #DDDDDD window face; a top row carrying a flat #DDDDDD combo/field region and a sunken white search field on the right; a large white #FFFFFF icon-grid field below (roughly y≈58..323 at x≈14..473 on the probe) whose cells carry the fallback icon theme's colorful art in large white cells with black outline rules along the field's top and bottom edges; and a bottom row of raised push buttons (#DDDDDD face, #AAAAAA shadow arm, black border) in the lower right above the window's bottom black outline. Two consecutive full captures agreed byte for byte under `cmp`, so every band is deterministic without any pin. The grid's icon art is the fallback icon theme's, not theme-owned: every band must avoid icon-art cells and glyph rows, and no band may pin any icon's pixels. No collected reference screenshot shows an icon chooser, so the comparison values are the shipped art recipe and the palette's own entries, recorded in the invariants row with this provenance.

**Approach and files.** In `tools/render_clients.py` add `icon_dialog_client(_session)` beside `menu_dialog_client`, returning `kdialog --title Test --geticon application ""` with its docstring recording the determinism rationale and the not-theme-owned icon-art warning above. In `tests/test_render_surface.py` add unit cases beside the landed dialog-mode cases (mutually exclusive with the other dialog flags and the calculator surface, missing-tool naming names kdialog, `--help` names the mode, `test_only_dialog_renders_add_kdeglobals_to_the_session_configs` reads unchanged) and extend `TestDialogGateSkipGuards`' gate tuple in `test_all_dialog_gates_skip_only_when_a_tool_is_absent` with the new class, aligning its docstring. Model the gate class `TestIconDialogRender` on `TestMenuDialogRender` (same `_DialogGate` base, prerequisite and software-renderer-guard skips): measure the window origin and crops from two consecutive full `--icon-dialog` captures on the implementation host that agree byte for byte under `cmp`, and record both measured-crop dates in the class comment the way the landed crops' comments do; this plan's probe numbers are not the gate's anchors — the gate re-derives every crop and expected hex from fresh same-render double captures, choosing bands clear of the icon-grid's icon-art cells and every glyph row wherever a flat band exists. Pin four bands: (a) one window-face interior crop chosen in the flat #DDDDDD face clear of the search row, the icon-grid field, the buttons and all four window borders, expecting the flat #DDDDDD palette window face with no other ink inside; (b) one band over the icon-grid field's top edge expecting the measured black outline rule with the white #FFFFFF field face below it, so a lost outline, a shifted field or a recoloured view face fails; (c) one band over the top-row search field expecting the white #FFFFFF face inside the black outline with the #999999 top-left shadow arm as freshly measured per the landed line-edit recipe, so a shifted outline, a lost shadow or a full-strength text ink fails; (d) one band over one push button's full-height label-free cell expecting the landed raised push-button recipe re-derived from the shipped button art (the 1px black border, the white bevel arm, the flat #DDDDDD face and the #AAAAAA shadow arm), so a stock-rounded, recoloured or duplicated-face button fails. **Acceptance criteria.**

No pinned band contains icon-art pixels, so the gate fails on a theme change but never on a fallback-icon-set change. The gate skips cleanly when its tools are missing or the software-renderer guard triggers, so `make check` passes with today's skip behavior on the hosted job.

### Kvantum scrollbar dialog render gate: pin a captured kdialog text box's scrollbar handle and trough on the shipped art recipe (planned 2026-11-10 by the plan role; the same CLI-plumbing files as the waiting progressbar-dialog entry ahead of it, a further widget surface — the two entries share no assertion region and may merge in either order, so at implementation re-read the landed mode lists and re-grep every anchor this entry names) — done 2026-11-10 by the feature role

**Goal.** No render gate captures the Kvantum engine's rendered `QScrollBar`: a change to the shipped `scrollbarslider` frame tiles, the `[Scrollbar]`/`[ScrollbarSlider]`/`[ScrollbarGroove]` sections of `theme/kvantum/org.macos8.desktop/org.macos8.desktop.kvconfig` (`scroll_width=16`, `scroll_arrows=true`, `frame.element=scrollbarslider` with 2px margins, `indicator.element=grip` at size 13, a `slider`-element groove) or Kvantum's scrollbar drawing would ship green. A `kdialog --textbox <file>` dialog (the flag exists; verified on this host, and a probe capture in this session's scratch shows the scrollbar rendering) opens a real themed text view with a vertical `QScrollBar` in the isolated headless session, giving the missing surface. No collected reference screenshot shows a dialog with a scrollbar, so the comparison surfaces are the shipped art recipe: the raised 16x16 `scrollbarslider` arrangement `tests/test_kvantum_svg.py` pins by element id (flat #DDDDDD face, #FFFFFF top/left arms, #999999 bottom/right arms, 1px #000000 outline), the `slider` element interior `[ScrollbarGroove]` draws as the trough (flat #EEEEEE face with its 1px #000000 outline), the `grip` element's three #000000 bars the handle's 13px indicator paints, and the `arrow` element faces the `scroll_arrows=true` buttons paint. The dialog is byte-deterministic at rest: the client reads a plain scratch text file, the scrollbar rests at value zero, so value zero disables the up arrow (its triangle paints the disabled #999999 `arrow` state, the same disabled tint the pinned `comboarrow-*` families use) while the bottom arrow stays enabled in the normal #000000 state, and no hover, press or focus byte enters any crop. The reference screenshots stay out of the gate code, exactly as the landed menu-dialog gate does.

### Reference validation: reject a truncated image body (planned 2026-11-09 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-09 by the feature role

**Goal.** A reference download cut short can end in valid image bytes: today `tools/reference_validation.py::_check_entries` sniffs only the leading bytes through `tools/image_format.py::is_image`, so a truncated PNG (signature and IHDR present, IEND missing) passes `make check-references` and is found later only when a sampler decode of that image fails. The checker should report an incomplete stream at validation time, complementing the unrelated README diagnostics guide under `## Planned`. New diagnostic text is the contract, so it is pinned in tests.

**Approach and files.** In `tools/image_format.py` add `TERMINAL_PNG = bytes((0, 0, 0, 0)) + b"IEND" + b"\xae\x42\x60\x82"` (the zero-length IEND chunk with its constant CRC) and `TERMINAL_JPEG = b"\xff\xd9"`, `TERMINAL_GIF = b";"`, plus a pure function `is_complete(head: bytes, tail: bytes, size: int) -> bool` that identifies the format from `head` alone (PNG, JPEG, GIF 87a/89a, or RIFF+WEBP per the existing constants: never the extension, so `sherlock_fandom.jpg` routes by its WebP container) and returns True only when: PNG's last bytes equal `TERMINAL_PNG`; JPEG's last two bytes equal `TERMINAL_JPEG`; GIF's last byte is `TERMINAL_GIF`; or WebP's declared RIFF size (`int.from_bytes(head[4:8], "little") + 8`) equals `size`. Return False when the format is not an image. In `tools/reference_validation.py`, have the declared-entry reader take head and last 12 bytes in the single existing `open_regular_binary` call (padding `tail` with the head's own bytes when the file is shorter keeps both reads atomic in one open), and after the signature check passes append a problem naming the format's missing terminator: a PNG "ends without the PNG IEND trailer", a JPEG "ends without the JPEG EOI marker", a GIF "ends without the GIF trailer byte", a WebP "declares N RIFF bytes but holds M" (N from `head[4:8]`, M from `size`), each with the existing `"{sources}:{lineno}: {filename!r} ...; it may be a truncated download"` suffix and prefix shape. `_check_undeclared` still sniffs heads only. An unrecognized-payload diagnostic (HTML error page under an image name) always outranks the truncation diagnostic. Update `tools/check_references_selftest.py`'s clean-set fixtures from their current `PNG_MAGIC`-only contents to complete minimal images (a helper prefix plus `TERMINAL_PNG` suffices, as for JPEG `JPEG_MAGIC + TERMINAL_JPEG`, GIF `b"GIF89a" + TERMINAL_GIF`, WebP `b"RIFF" + (4).to_bytes(4, "little") + b"WEBP"`) and add four truncated cases, each one expecting the new diagnostic text. In `tests/test_check_references_validation.py` unit-test `is_complete` direction by direction (each complete form passing, each cut form failing, a RIFF/WAVE payload failing the image test before any terminator check) and pin the CLI diagnostics with `reference_set`/`assert_problem`; the existing `test_declared_image_prefix_is_read_with_one_open` must pass unchanged. README's `## Validating the reference set` failure list gains one clause naming the missing-stream-terminator diagnostic and stating it is a bounded structural check, not a full decode; add and date a `## tooling` row in docs/invariants.md pinning the ending rules with this entry's measurement below as provenance.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- For each of the four formats, a declared file missing its terminator exits 1 from `python3 tools/check_references.py` on a fixture set, prints the `sources.txt:<line>` problem naming the file and the format's terminator (WebP naming its declared and held sizes), and no sampler is ever reached; a complete `JPEG_MAGIC + TERMINAL_JPEG` fixture and the set's intact files still pass. A RIFF/WAVE payload keeps the existing "not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP" diagnostic, never a truncation one.
- Against the materialized repository set, `make check-references` passes with today's output unchanged; `python3 tools/check_references.py --self-test` exits 0 with the rewritten fixtures and the `test_declared_image_prefix_is_read_with_one_open` open count stays exactly one per declared file.
- README's new clause and the dated invariant row name these tests; the row records that every currently materialized reference file satisfies the ending rules (verified 2026-11-09 for all 28 image files in `macos8.6-screenshots/`) so no shipped reference regresses the gate. No runtime path other than `check-references` changes behavior; `make check` passes after the final edit.

Implemented 2026-11-09 by the feature role: the tail comes from reading the file's last bytes (up to 12) within the same `open_regular_binary` call rather than from padding the head, and the second acceptance criterion's `test_declared_image_prefix_is_read_with_one_open` keeps its assertion structure unchanged — only its fixture (and the shared `good_reference` fixture in `tests/support/check_references_fixtures.py`, plus the truncated accepted-format fixtures in `tests/test_check_references_validation.py`) was completed to a minimal full stream, because every clean fixture now has to satisfy the ending rules too.

### README reference validation: map diagnostics to corrective actions (planned 2026-11-09 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-09 by the feature role

**Goal.** Help contributors repair a failed `make check-references` without confusing missing LFS images with broken provenance. The existing validation section lists rejected inputs but gives no diagnostic-to-action guide. This is independent of the waiting render-failure guide and the pending vertical-storage change.

**Approach and files.** Edit README.md only: append a compact troubleshooting table within `## Validating the reference set`, before Sampling reference pixels. Ground the rows in `tools/reference_validation.py::_check_entries`, `_check_undeclared` and `check_references`, `tools/reference_sources.py::parse_sources`, and `tools/check_references.py::main`; these are evidence anchors, not implementation targets. Cover an unmaterialized LFS pointer, a declared file missing on disk, an image without an entry, malformed/duplicate entries or source URLs, and unrecognized image bytes. Explain the three-field `filename | source URL | version label` record, including bare filenames and evidence-based labels; link to Reference screenshots rather than duplicating its retail/beta policy. Distinguish the checker's signature inspection from full image decoding or provenance verification, and the fixture-only self-test from validation of the working reference directory. Keep existing commands and CI guidance.

**Acceptance criteria.**

### Fidelity horizontal reports: bound capped interval storage (planned 2026-11-09 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-09 by the feature role

**Goal.** Make `--difference-runs --max-difference-runs N` retain a bounded page of horizontal intervals, including with a large offset. `tools/fidelity_spatial.py::difference_runs` currently materializes the iterator before `tools/fidelity.py::main` applies `_filter_run_report`. The finished horizontal cap and paging plans explicitly limited output rather than segmentation storage. This improvement is independent of README navigation; vertical collection is a separate future task.

**Approach and files.** Add a focused `tools/fidelity_run_page.py` module whose collector consumes an interval iterable once, counts unfiltered intervals, selects the first longest interval before filtering, counts eligible intervals after inclusive minimum/maximum lengths, and retains only the offset/cap page. Return the page, eligible-minus-emitted omitted count, unfiltered count and longest record. Expose a horizontal iterator wrapper in `tools/fidelity_spatial.py` over `_iter_difference_axis_runs`; preserve the existing list-returning API. In `tools/fidelity.py::main`, use the collector on the capped horizontal path and take requested count/longest summaries from its full-stream results. Keep `_filter_run_report` for uncapped horizontal and existing vertical reports. Support direct-script and package imports. Add `tests/test_fidelity_run_page.py` and extend `tests/test_fidelity_difference_runs_limit.py`; revise the horizontal storage statements in README.md and docs/invariants.md (including the count/longest sharing wording). No flags or dependencies are added. This bounds retained interval records, not decoded images, channel deltas or mismatch flags.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- For horizontal intervals `(0,0,1)`, `(2,0,2)`, `(5,0,3)`, `(0,1,4)`, `(8,1,1)`, minimum length 2, maximum length 3, offset 1 and cap 1 emit only `(5,0,3)`, omit 1 eligible interval, report unfiltered count 5 and longest `(0,1,4)`. Offset beyond the eligible end emits an empty page with omitted count 2. Conflicting cutoffs yield an empty page with omitted count 0 while count and longest remain 5 and `(0,1,4)`. Empty input gives count 0 and longest null; equal longest lengths choose the earliest interval.
- A one-shot generated iterable containing many intervals, with an offset near its end and cap 2, is exhausted for accurate totals while at most the two page records plus a constant number of working/longest records remain live. Use deterministic live-record tracking in the collector test rather than timing or a machine-dependent memory threshold; eager materialization or retention of skipped records must fail it.
- CLI JSON and text retain existing fields, ordering, crop-relative coordinates, omitted counts, tolerance/alpha semantics and verdicts for capped reports. Requested count and longest still describe unfiltered input even when the longest is outside the page. Cover an uncapped comparison and simultaneous vertical diagnostics to guard the branch boundary; existing cap/offset tests remain green. Documentation states the horizontal interval-storage limit without extending it to vertical intervals or image buffers. Run `make check` after the final edit.

SUMMARY: Bound storage for capped horizontal fidelity interval reports
WHY: Capped reports now collect only the requested page while preserving full-stream totals. The backlog placeholder also falsely claimed that the planned section was empty.
RISK: Horizontal capped report paging could omit or miscount intervals; inspect `tools/fidelity_run_page.py` and its tests. Backlog placeholder detection lives in `tests/test_backlog_placeholders.py`.

### CI workflow: drop the forced llvmpipe driver override the KWin render sessions cannot survive on a GPU host (planned 2026-11-09 by the plan role; independent of the waiting desktop-theme legacy-art registration — that entry adds `tests/test_desktoptheme_legacy.py` and edits the `## desktoptheme` table row of `docs/invariants.md` and README's desktop-theme paragraph, while this entry edits one workflow env line, `tests/test_ci_workflow.py::test_workflow_runs_the_suite_on_the_headless_qt_platform` and the two `## tooling` render-gate rows of `docs/invariants.md`, so the two entries share the invariants file only in disjoint sections and one entry names no test module the other owns, letting either merge first; this entry settles the work the open BUGS.md entry "the render tests' KWin session cannot allocate its capture buffers under the workflow's llvmpipe env" (found by the ci role 2026-11-09) files, which routes to "the bugfix or plan role" — route it here: the fix is one env line plus its pinned assertions and rows, not recovery machinery) — done 2026-11-09 by the feature role

Corrected 2026-11-09 by the feature role: the acceptance criterion's whole-file llvmpipe grep cannot return nothing — the pre-existing install-step comment naming libgl1-mesa-dri's llvmpipe driver (workflow line 81, untouched by this entry's file list and present on main before it) and this entry's own dictated bug-comment keep matching it. The criterion is met in intent and in the assignment-scoped grep `grep -En '^[[:space:]]+(MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE|GALLIUM_DRIVER):' .github/workflows/ci.yml`, which returns nothing; whole-file grep still finds only prose comments.


**Goal and grounding.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s check job pins both `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE: '1'` and `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE: llvmpipe` (lines 20–23 today, re-read before editing) so the GPU-less runner's nested KWin virtual compositor gets a software EGL driver. The pairing is one variable too heavy: on this host (a real GPU is present, finding verified 2026-11-09 in the cited BUGS entry) `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` alone leaves the `kwin_wayland --virtual` session clean, but adding `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=llvmpipe` drives Mesa's KMS/GBM dumb-buffer path and KWin's virtual backend fails with `KMS: DRM_IOCTL_MODE_CREATE_DUMB failed: Permission denied` on `/dev/dri/renderD128` (the primary node admits the ioctl, the render node refuses it), so the session captures nothing and 32 errors plus 5 failures land in `tests/test_render_surface.py` under the workflow's env. The override's runner-side value was never observed: the hosted run `18ded7fe` failed at the install step before the suite, so nothing pins that the runner needs the second variable — and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` already forces a software driver (llvmpipe being Mesa's software GL path), which is why the session was clean locally without the override. The pin is documented nowhere as required: grep of tools, tests, docs and the Makefile finds the override string only in the workflow, the workflow-pinning test and the skip-guard tables (`tests/test_render_surface.py` keeps treating a *user-set* `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE`/`GALLIUM_DRIVER` as a software-forcing signal — that reader stays). The guard still fires on the runner without the override, because `tests/test_render_surface.py`'s skip condition covers `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` directly, so the render gates keep skipping with the software-renderer reason that `docs/invariants.md`'s `## tooling` rows record; the gate-skip semantics change nothing.

**Approach and files.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, delete the `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE: llvmpipe` env line and in the comment above it replace the two-value explanation with one dated (2026-11-09) statement: the entry sets only `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` because the runner has no GPU and Mesa otherwise tries Zink and cannot create an EGL screen, while a pinned `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=llvmpipe` breaks KWin's virtual session on a real-GPU host with a KMS dumb-buffer permission denial (BUGS entry named above); with no driver-name pinning under defaults, the gates' skip guard fires on `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` alone. Keep the two retained lines byte-equal in value (`QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen`, `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE: '1'`). In `tests/test_ci_workflow.py::test_workflow_runs_the_suite_on_the_headless_qt_platform`, replace the override-pinning `assertRegex` with `assertNotRegex` assertions for both `(?m)^\s+MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE:` and `(?m)^\s+GALLIUM_DRIVER:`, keep the offscreen and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE: '1'` assertions unchanged, and update the test's comment to the same one-variable reason (the runner-side Zink failure was reproduced before this pairing existed — commit `a005ece42` set both variables together, so the override never carried its own evidence). In `docs/invariants.md`, reword the two `## tooling` rows: row 646's "the job forces Mesa's llvmpipe" clause becomes "the job forces software GL (`LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`) so KWin's virtual backend has an EGL driver without a GPU", and row 647's trailing "the CI job's forced llvmpipe skips them with that reason" becomes "the CI job's software-GL forcing (`LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`) skips them with that reason"; row 646's provenance cell gains the dated deletion evidence — the hosted `18ded7fe` run failed at the install step before any test, so the override's runner-side value was never observed, and the local GPU-host finding (override set → `KMS: DRM_IOCTL_MODE_CREATE_DUMB failed: Permission denied` on the render node, session captures nothing; `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` alone → clean session) was verified 2026-11-09 per the BUGS entry the workflow comment names. No other production file, no Python tool change (the skip-guard readers in `tests/test_render_surface.py` keep covering user-set overrides), and no new dependency.

**Acceptance criteria.** (corrected 2026-11-09 by the feature role) the env-assignment grep `grep -En "^\s+(MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE|GALLIUM_DRIVER):" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns nothing, while `grep -n "QT_QPA_PLATFORM\|LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE" .github/workflows/ci.yml` finds both retained lines; the original whole-file `grep -n "MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE\|GALLIUM_DRIVER\|llvmpipe"` cannot return nothing — the pre-existing install-step comment naming `libgl1-mesa-dri`'s llvmpipe driver (untouched by this entry's file list and present on main before it) and this entry's own dictated bug-comment keep matching it, so whole-file grep is prose-only and the assignment-anchored grep is the pinned check; a revert of either deletion (`LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE` line or its comment intact but the override line restored) fails the new `assertNotRegex` assertions, proving the test actually pins the absence and not merely the file's length. Re-running the cited BUGS entry's reproduce command with the override stripped — `env QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 make check CHECK_TESTS=test_render_surface` on this host — completes the module without any KMS dumb-buffer error, missing capture PNG or `CaptureScreen` non-reply, and every render gate that would capture under it skips with the software-renderer skip reason rather than erroring as they do in the BUGS entry's worked output. The existing guard tests (`tests/test_render_surface.py::TestDialogGateSkipGuards::test_the_skip_guard_also_covers_a_software_renderer`, which covers the `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE` signal) pass unchanged, and the two reworded invariants rows still name the same test identifiers they name today. README's CI sentence ("runs `make check` and `make check-references`") needs no edit. Honesty bound, stated in the row: the change does not and cannot yet verify the runner-side virtual session, whose env value stays unobserved until the next hosted run with a GPU-less environment that reaches the suite — the plan commits only the documented, locally reproduced contrast above, not a claim that the runner has been observed clean. `make check` passes after the final edit.

### Reference-pixel sampler: bound retained vertical match intervals while paging (planned 2026-11-09 by the plan role; independent of the waiting uninstall split — that entry owns the uninstall diagnostics modules and their tests, while this entry touches only `tools/sample_match_runs.py`, `tools/sample_report_search.py`, `tools/sample_report_pixels.py`, one new test module, the match-column-runs passages of README.md and the vertical match-filter row of docs/invariants.md; the horizontal storage-bound entry carried by the merging `feature e63725e` change edits the horizontal statements of the same two sampler files, README and invariants, so this entry merges after it, mirrors its pattern and touches none of its horizontal code or tests) — done 2026-11-09 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** When `--match-column-runs` is combined with `--max-match-column-runs`, `--match-column-run-offset` and the vertical length filters, the requested page should bound retained vertical interval storage the way the horizontal bound does. Today `tools/sample_match_runs.py::_MatchRuns._record_column_run` appends every vertical interval during the row-major scan and `tools/sample_report_search.py::_search_match` filters and slices the completed column-major list, so a cap bounds only output, not segmentation memory; the vertical cap and offset records explicitly left collector memory unbounded, and the horizontal entry keeps vertical collection out because vertical intervals complete in row-major order while the page is defined column-major.

**Approach and files.** Keep the row-major scan's vertical bookkeeping unchanged for uncapped output and the full-region summaries; `_MatchRuns` itself stays untouched. Add `tools/sample_match_runs.py::_ColumnRuns`, a vertical interval collector mirroring `_MatchRuns`'s horizontal eligibility pattern: it takes the two inclusive length cutoffs, cap and offset, closes each column's active interval at every column boundary and at the bottom edge, counts eligible and unfiltered intervals at completion, and retains only the requested page. Add `tools/sample_report_pixels.py::_positioned_region_column_pixels`, a column-major twin of `_positioned_region_pixels` over the same decoded buffers. ### Remove the theme-id directories `make uninstall` empties under `themes/` (planned 2026-11-04 by the plan role; independent of the waiting kdedefaults series — part 1/2 and part 2/2 append their diagnostic blocks at the `_uninstall` recipe tail after the last aurorae check's `fi`, while this entry edits the `rmdir` line in the removal section above those blocks, adds no diagnostic line, no README uninstall-warning sentence and no new test module, so the two touch disjoint recipe regions, different README sections and disjoint test modules and can merge in either order; greps of PLANS.md `## Planned`, PLANS-DONE.md, BUGS.md, BUGS-FIXED.md and the tree found no entry, test or prose that removes or plans to remove the emptied shared theme directory or its `Kvantum/` parent — `docs/invariants.md`'s `## gtk` row pins the opposite covenant for the shared directory — it states the uninstall leaves `Kvantum/` and the theme directory itself — and `tests/test_gtk_install.py::TestUninstall`'s two landed cases rely on it, so this entry revises exactly that row's `removes` clause, with every other uninstall guarantee untouched) — done 2026-11-04 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** The Kvantum style and the GTK package share one theme directory: `KVANTUM_INSTALL_DIR` is `$(DESTDIR)$(XDG_DATA_HOME)/themes/$(KVANTUM_ID)/Kvantum` and `GTK_INSTALL_DIR` is `$(DESTDIR)$(XDG_DATA_HOME)/themes/$(GTK_ID)` — both ids `org.macos8.desktop` (Makefile's lines around 262-269) — so a full install creates `themes/org.macos8.desktop/`, `themes/org.macos8.desktop/Kvantum/` and the six sub-directories beneath them. `Makefile::_uninstall` removes every file the two families install — the two `rm -f` Kvantum lines and `gtk_remove_loop` — but its trailing cleanup runs only `rmdir "$(GTK_INSTALL_DIR)/assets" "$(GTK_INSTALL_DIR)/gtk-3.0" "$(GTK_INSTALL_DIR)/gtk-4.0" 2>/dev/null || true`, so after an ordinary (not SIGKILL-interrupted) uninstall the data home keeps three unreachable theme-id directories: the emptied `Kvantum/` parent under them, emptied `themes/org.macos8.desktop/` itself, and the `themes/` root the theme's own install created when that root did not exist before. The three empties are this theme's residue — verified on this host 2026-11-04 by running `make install` with a scratch `DESTDIR`/`XDG_DATA_HOME` and then `make uninstall`, whose exit-0 finishes leaving exactly `themes/`, `themes/org.macos8.desktop/` and `themes/org.macos8.desktop/Kvantum/` on disk. GTK and Qt theme discovery enumerate `themes/*/index.theme`, so an empty id-named directory cannot resolve to a theme and the residue is dead weight, but the removal table's promise is that `make uninstall` deletes the theme's installed packages; values installed to a directory the install itself created should leave nothing of their own there. `rmdir` is the right tool: it removes a directory only when it is empty, so a `Kvantum/` or shared directory holding a foreign file the theme did not install (the shape `test_make_uninstall_removes_the_installed_files` and `test_make_uninstall_leaves_foreign_files_in_the_gtk_directories` already stage) survives untouched, and `rmdir` on an absent or symlinked path fails, which the line's existing `2>/dev/null || true` swallows like it already does for the three sub-directories. The SIGKILL partial-publication limitation is unchanged and accepted: the plan covers only the ordinary-failure path the file removals already guarantee.

**Approach and files.** Three files plus the GTK invariant row, no tool module and no diagnostic wording. In `Makefile::_uninstall`, append two `rmdir` terms to the existing trailing cleanup's same command line, directly after the three landed ones, in parent-before-child order: `rmdir "$(KVANTUM_INSTALL_DIR)" 2>/dev/null || true` and then `rmdir "$(GTK_INSTALL_DIR)" 2>/dev/null || true` (or fold both into the one `rmdir` command with the same `2>/dev/null || true`; quoting stays double-quoted exactly like the existing terms so the space and apostrophe destination cases keep working). The following `#` comment block the landed diagnostics anchor on is below this line in the recipe and needs no edit. In `tests/test_gtk_install.py`, extend `TestUninstall::test_make_uninstall_removes_the_installed_files`'s planted-sentinel case and add one emptied-tree case: with no foreign file planted anywhere under the shared directory, after `uninstall(tmp)` (a full install via the module's `installed_destdir`) the shared directory `installed` itself, its `Kvantum/` sub-directory, and the parent `themes/` root's remaining `org.macos8.desktop` entries are all absent, while a foreign sibling directory under `themes/` (stage one, as the landed case already stages `second-theme`) and the `themes/` root itself survive. Its planted-sentinel case keeps its foreign file read-back and now also asserts the foreign file's directory still exists, pinning that only fully emptied directories go. In `tests/test_kvantum_install.py::TestKvantumInstall::test_make_uninstall_removes_the_installed_files`, add the same two absence assertions for the emptied `_installed_dir(tmp)` Kvantum directory and the shared parent above it, and add an idempotence note: a second `uninstall` still exits 0 when nothing of ours exists. README.md's 'Removing the theme' table `make uninstall` row — 'Deletes installed theme packages and leaves user configuration in place. Run after clearing selections; it does not remove the cursor link or change keyboard mappings.' — gains one clause stating that the uninstall also rmdir-removes the theme-id directories it emptied under `themes/`, that a directory still holding a file the theme did not install survives, and that this removes directories the install created, not user configuration. `docs/invariants.md`'s `## gtk` row (`make uninstall` ... clause, currently ending `removes only the thirteen files, their .staging siblings and the emptied assets/gtk-3.0/gtk-4.0 directories, leaving Kvantum/ and the theme directory itself`) is the row whose covenant this entry revises: restate that clause to say the uninstall also removes the emptied `Kvantum/` directory and the emptied shared theme directory `themes/org.macos8.desktop` itself, while a directory still holding any foreign file survives, and add `tests/test_kvantum_install.py::TestKvantumInstall::test_make_uninstall_removes_the_installed_files` to that row's test list. No `## tooling` row and no README uninstall-warning paragraph change; nothing under make prints anything new.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- With a full `make install` into a scratch `DESTDIR`/data home, `make uninstall` exits 0, and afterwards the shared `themes/org.macos8.desktop/` directory, its `Kvantum/` sub-directory, its `assets`/`gtk-3.0`/`gtk-4.0` subdirectories and the `org.macos8.desktop` entry under `themes/` are all absent from disk, while the `themes/` root itself and any foreign sibling directory under it still exist. A second `make uninstall` on that tree still exits 0 with no diagnostic.
- With a foreign file planted in `themes/org.macos8.desktop/Kvantum/`, or in `themes/org.macos8.desktop/` itself (neither of ours left behind), `make uninstall` exits 0, every file the two families shipped is gone, the foreign file reads back byte-identical, and the directory holding it still exists — the foreign sibling and everything else above it survive. Both these foreign-file shapes ride the same existing `installed_destdir` support the landed cases use; no new fixture is added.
- `make _uninstall` on a tree where neither family was ever installed stays a silent success, and on a scratch data home for a `make install INSTALL_PACKAGES=kvantum`-only tree followed by `make install INSTALL_PACKAGES=gtk`, uninstall then leaves no `themes/org.macos8.desktop` trace at all. The uninstall diagnostics' landed test modules read back byte-identical — this recipe change adds no stderr output and removes no diagnostic — install-uninstall under a destination path containing a space or an apostrophe still both succeed, symlink planted at the shared directory keeps the landed refusal (`require_uninstall_parents` runs before the recipe), and README's revised table row plus the revised `## gtk` row pass their register checks; `make check` is green after the final edit.

### kdedefaults series, part 2/2: Diagnose the kdedefaults ini mirrors the apply leaves behind (planned 2026-11-04 by the plan role; requires part 1/2 landed, so its block can anchor directly after part 1's block at the `_uninstall` recipe tail without ever sharing that region with another waiting entry; covers the three `kdedefaults` ini mirrors the isolated apply run recorded — `kdedefaults/kdeglobals` holding `[Icons] Theme=org.macos8.desktop` and `[KDE] widgetStyle=kvantum`, `kdedefaults/kwinrc` holding `[org.kde.kdecoration2] NoPlugin=false` plus the `library=org.kde.kwin.aurorae` / `theme=__aurorae__svg__org.macos8.desktop` pair, and `kdedefaults/plasmarc` holding `[Theme] name=org.macos8.desktop` — while part 1/2 covers the splash and flat `package` checks) — done 2026-11-04 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** The same look-and-feel apply that writes the live-config selections (the one isolated and recorded on part 1/2's heading-run evidence) also left defaults-layer mirrors of the `kdeglobals`, `kwinrc` and `plasmarc` selections under `$config_home/kdedefaults` (verified on this host on 2026-11-04 with the isolated scratch-home lookandfeeltool run recorded in part 1/2; file contents quoted in this heading's parenthetical). The landed uninstall diagnostics cover the live-config counterparts only, so after `make uninstall` — and, decisively, after the landed `kwriteconfig6 --delete` resets remove the live keys — a start still resolves the widget style, icon theme, window decoration and desktop theme from this untouched defaults layer, naming removed ids silently. The wording of each diagnostic mirrors its live-config counterpart's landed wording, with the path naming the `kdedefaults` mirror and the prose saying the defaults layer re-selects the removed id when the live key is absent or reset away; the reset names `kwriteconfig6 --delete` against the mirror's literal path, whose behavior on a `kdedefaults` path is the provenance ground verified in part 1/2.

**Approach and files.** Three files plus the invariant register, mirroring the landed widget-style/icon-theme and aurorae diagnostics (`Makefile`'s `_uninstall` kdeglobals two-key awk and kwinrc pair blocks and their tests). In the `Makefile` `_uninstall` recipe, insert directly after part 1/2's block's closing `fi` and before the `install-gtk:` target a block of three checks over the same resolved config home prefixed with `kdedefaults/`, each an awk with the landed ini scanner semantics and each independent: (a) one two-key awk over `kdedefaults/kdeglobals` printing the `[KDE] widgetStyle=kvantum` line only when that key's last value in `[KDE]` trims to `kvantum` and the `[Icons] Theme` line only when it trims to `org.macos8.desktop`, each followed by its reset `kwriteconfig6 --file <the mirror path> --group KDE --key widgetStyle --delete` and `kwriteconfig6 --file <the mirror path> --group Icons --key Theme --delete`; (b) one two-key awk over `kdedefaults/kwinrc` printing a line only when `[org.kde.kdecoration2]` holds the landed `library=org.kde.kwin.aurorae` and `theme=__aurorae__svg__org.macos8.desktop` pair (the `NoPlugin=false` key the isolated run wrote is not a match condition and stays silent), followed by the two-key `--delete` reset for the literal mirror path; and (c) one awk over `kdedefaults/plasmarc` printing only when `[Theme]`'s last `name` trims to `org.macos8.desktop`, followed by `kwriteconfig6 --file <the mirror path> --group Theme --key name --delete` (wording is the contract; each line mirrors its live-config counterpart's landed wording with the mirror path and the defaults-layer prose). Four diagnostic lines, each independent as in the landed entries. The provenance grounds are prose, never test-asserted: what draws when the defaults layer names a removed widget style, icon theme, aurorae package and desktop theme is grounded in the upstream sources the landed counterparts' README sentences already record, and the defaults-layer fallback claim (a deleted live key re-resolves from the mirror) is grounded once against the KDE config-cascade sources and recorded in the README sentence. The diagnostics edit nothing. Add `tests/test_kdedefaults_mirror_uninstall_diagnostic.py` modeled on `tests/test_kwinrc_uninstall_diagnostic.py` and `tests/test_colorscheme_install.py`'s uninstall-warning section, driving `make _uninstall` through `support.theme_install.uninstall_recipe` with staged `kdedefaults/` mirrors, pinning the four lines above, asserting byte-identical readback after each run, and covering both the warn and silent shapes of the acceptance criteria; note that `make _uninstall`'s full recipe needs `install` to have run in the make test support, which the like-named landed modules already handle. README.md's uninstall-warning paragraph gains one sentence directly after part 1/2's sentence and before the paragraph's closing `No such warning edits the user's configuration.` sentence. `docs/invariants.md` gains one `## tooling` row naming `tests/test_kdedefaults_mirror_uninstall_diagnostic.py`, and `tests/support/invariants.py` gets its register entry. No tool module changes and no existing test's wording changes.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- With a staged `kdedefaults` mirror holding any one of the four match positions at its published value, `make _uninstall` succeeds, stderr carries exactly that line with the real mirror path and no other new line, and every staged file reads back byte-identical. With all four staged, the four lines appear in the order `widgetStyle`, `Icons Theme`, kwinrc pair, plasmarc `name`. Warned variants include the landed counterparts' warn shapes: BOM-prefixed files with comments and indented keys, values that only trim to the expected ones, and an earlier foreign value followed by the expected one later in the same group (last value wins).
- Silent shapes, each exiting 0 with no mirror diagnostic on stderr while files read back byte-identical: absent paths; non-regular files; missing groups; missing keys; foreign or empty last values; later foreign duplicates; foreign `[Icons] Theme` leaving a matching `[KDE] widgetStyle` warning alone and vice versa; each key of the kwinrc pair alone failing while the other matches; the `NoPlugin` key matching while neither pair key does; and the selections living in differently named groups. Independence is two-sided for all four lines. With no usable config home nothing is checked, and the `$HOME/.config` fallback applies as in part 1/2.
- Part 1/2's two lines, the landed live-config diagnostics and this entry's four lines can all appear in one run in recipe order, each wording unchanged; the existing uninstall diagnostics' tests read back unchanged; README sentences and the new invariant row pass their register checks; `make check` is green after the final edit.

### kdedefaults series, part 1/2: Diagnose the splash theme and look-and-feel package defaults the apply leaves under `kdedefaults` (planned 2026-11-04 by the plan role; part 2/2 depends on this part and states that dependency on its own heading, so the two can never anchor on the same `_uninstall` recipe region; independent of the waiting Lato entry, whose block anchors between the kcminputrc pointer block's `fi` and the `kwinrc` assignment earlier in the recipe while this entry appends at the recipe tail after the last landed aurorae block's closing `fi`, and whose README sentences sit between the pointer and desktop-theme sentences while this entry's sit at the paragraph's end, so the two touch disjoint regions of the recipe and can merge in either order; searches of PLANS.md `## Planned`, PLANS-DONE.md, BUGS.md and BUGS-FIXED.md found no kdedefaults reader and no splash or `package` diagnostic, and the landed uninstall diagnostics cover the live-config selections only — `$kdeglobals`, `kvantum.kvconfig`, GTK, `plasmarc`, `kcminputrc` and `kwinrc` — never `$config_home/kdedefaults`) — done 2026-11-04 by the feature role

**Approach and files.** Three files plus the invariant register, mirroring the landed uninstall-pointer diagnostic (`Makefile`'s `_uninstall` kcminputrc block and `tests/test_cursor_uninstall_diagnostic.py`). In the `Makefile` `_uninstall` recipe, between the Kvantum kvconfig check's closing `fi` and the `kcminputrc="$$config_home/kcminputrc"` assignment, add a plasmarc block with the same shape: resolve the config home exactly as the other four blocks do (an absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, else `$HOME/.config`, else check nothing), read `$config_home/plasmarc` only when it is a regular file, scan with the shared `_uninstall` semantics the existing blocks' comments pin (first-line UTF-8 BOM stripped, each line trimmed before parsing, a trimmed `[`…`]` line switches the section to its bracketed name, `#`/`;` first-character lines are comments and never keys, key/value split at the first `=` with both sides trimmed, a later duplicate's value wins), match the key `name` inside the group `[Theme]`, and print once, to stderr, only when the last value trims to exactly `$(DTHEME_ID)` — the value `tools/apply_theme.py::DTHEME_ID` selects, with a comment over the Makefile literal keeping it in step with that constant — followed by the reset command:

    uninstall: the desktop theme selection still names org.macos8.desktop after removal in <path>; Plasma cannot load the removed desktop theme and keeps the default style. Reset it with: plasma-apply-desktoptheme breeze

The diagnostic edits nothing: the file must read back byte-identical, like the other four. Add `tests/test_plasmarc_uninstall_diagnostic.py` modeled on `tests/test_cursor_uninstall_diagnostic.py`, driving `make _uninstall` through `support.theme_install.uninstall_recipe` with only a staged `plasmarc`, pinning the exact diagnostic line above (the wording is the contract), asserting the staged file is byte-identical after each run, and covering both the warn and silent shapes of the acceptance criteria. README.md gains one sentence in the `make uninstall` warning paragraph that lists the four existing warnings: if the desktop theme selection `plasma-apply-desktoptheme` wrote (`[Theme] name=` in `plasmarc`) still names `org.macos8.desktop` after the uninstall, it prints a warning naming `plasma-apply-desktoptheme breeze` as the reset, with the default-style fallback recorded as a platform-required value grounded per the principle above. `docs/invariants.md` gains one `## tooling` row stating the diagnostic and silent shapes and naming `tests/test_plasmarc_uninstall_diagnostic.py`, and `tests/support/invariants.py` gets its register entry. No tool module changes and no existing test's wording changes.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- With a staged `plasmarc` holding `[Theme]` and `name=org.macos8.desktop`, `make _uninstall` succeeds, stderr carries exactly the diagnostic line with the real resolved path, and every byte of the file reads back unchanged. Warned variants also include: a BOM-prefixed file with comments, CRLF endings and indented keys; a value that only trims to ours; and a later duplicate `name` in the same group re-naming ours (last value wins), while an earlier foreign value followed by ours in the same group also warns.
- Silent shapes, each exiting 0 with no plasmarc diagnostic on stderr while the file reads back byte-identical: no `plasmarc` at all; a file at the path that is other than a regular file; a file without a `[Theme]` group; a group holding only a foreign value; an empty `name=` value; a later foreign duplicate overriding ours (last value wins); and the key sitting inside a differently named group. With no usable config home (no absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and no absolute `HOME`) nothing is checked, and with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` unset or relative the `$HOME/.config` fallback is read.
- When the pointer diagnostic's kcminputrc selection is staged alongside, both diagnostics can appear in one run and each keeps its landed wording; the four landed uninstall diagnostics' suites read back unchanged. README sentence and the new invariant row pass their register checks; `make check` is green after the final edit.
