### Warn when the Kvantum selection can only resolve from the default data home (planned 2026-11-04 by the plan role; independent of the waiting uninstall pointer-diagnostic entry — that entry edits the Makefile `_uninstall` awk block, a new uninstall test module and the README uninstall prose, while this entry edits `tools/theme_apply_optional.py::select_kvantum_theme`, `tools/xdg_homes.py`, the apply-test module and the README Installing/apply-plasma prose, so the two touch disjoint files and regions and can merge in either order) — done 2026-11-04 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** `make install` copies the Kvantum widget style into `$XDG_DATA_HOME/themes/org.macos8.desktop/Kvantum/`, and `tools/theme_apply_optional.py::select_kvantum_theme` selects it with `kvantummanager --set` — but Kvantum resolves its theme directory only through the literal `$HOME/.local/share/themes/<name>/Kvantum/` path (README's Installing section states this: "Kvantum searches `$HOME/.local/share/themes/<name>/Kvantum/` with that literal path, so it finds the theme only when `${XDG_DATA_HOME}` is the default"), and the make render scratch-session plumbing works around the same fact with a literal themes link. With a non-default absolute `XDG_DATA_HOME`, both the selection write and the apply succeed yet the engine silently draws its built-in default theme: a documented limitation with no warning at the moment the user makes the choice. The right remedy is a note at selection time, mirroring the missing-`kvantummanager` note the same function prints; grep of PLANS.md, PLANS-DONE.md, BUGS.md and BUGS-FIXED.md found no entry covering an apply-time data-home warning (the archived apply-plasma plan only repeats the limitation in prose), and the rollback/lock plans own other behaviors.

**Approach and files.** Two source files plus tests and prose. In `tools/xdg_homes.py`, add a pure `default_data_home(env) -> Path | None` beside `data_home`: the `$HOME/.local/share` child resolved the same way `data_home` falls back (None when `HOME` is unset or not absolute); no existing function or behavior changes. In `tools/theme_apply_optional.py::select_kvantum_theme`, after the `kvantummanager` presence check succeeds and before the selection runs, resolve `data_home(env)` and `default_data_home(env)` and, when both are not None and the resolved home differs from the default, print via the existing `_note` exactly: `the Kvantum engine reads its theme directory only under the default data home <default>, not the resolved <resolved>; widgets draw Kvantum's built-in default theme until themes/org.macos8.desktop/Kvantum exists there` with the two real absolute paths substituted — the selection itself runs unchanged either way, and the note never changes the exit status, keeping every note in this module best-effort. A None resolved home (no usable `HOME` in the apply's env) or a None default skips the check silently. `make apply-plasma`, which runs the same `tools/apply_theme.py`, inherits the note unchanged. README.md updates the two "existing default-data-home limitation" sentences (the apply-plasma paragraphs at the Installing and aggregate-apply spots) to name the apply-time note, and the Installing Kvantum paragraph gains a sentence stating that running `make apply` with a non-default `XDG_DATA_HOME` prints this note; docs/invariants.md's `## kvantum` table gains a row naming the new test.

**Tests.** Extend `tests/test_apply_theme.py` beside the existing `test_missing_kvantummanager_prints_a_note_and_exits_0` stub class with a new test class driving `select_kvantum_theme` through the same stub-`kvantummanager` machinery (same stubbing pattern `StubTools` uses): one test per env shape below, asserting exit status 0, the exact note line and, for the silent cases, that stderr carries no data-home note. Also add a small `tests/test_xdg_homes.py` class for `default_data_home`: absolute/absolute-set `HOME`, unset `HOME`, and relative `HOME`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- With a stubbed `kvantummanager` found on the stubbed `PATH` and an env whose `XDG_DATA_HOME` is an absolute non-default path (e.g. a scratch directory), the selection exits 0, the stub records the unchanged `--set org.macos8.desktop` argv, and stderr ends with exactly the note line above with both rendered paths — no other line of the apply's output changes.
- With no `XDG_DATA_HOME` at all, an empty `XDG_DATA_HOME`, or a relative one, and with the data home equal to the default, no such note appears and the selection behaves identically to today (exit 0, unchanged argv). When the compare cannot resolve both sides — an `XDG_DATA_HOME` that is empty or relative with a `HOME` unset or relative, or an absolute `XDG_DATA_HOME` with a `HOME` unset or relative (the resolved home comes from `XDG_DATA_HOME` alone but no default exists to name) — the check skips silently too.
- With `kvantummanager` absent, the existing missing-tool note and status are byte-identical to today and no data-home note is printed; with the manager present on a non-default data home and the stub broken (non-zero exit), both the data-home note and the selection-failure note appear and the status stays 0.
- `tools/xdg_homes.py::default_data_home` returns `<absolute HOME>/.local/share` given an absolute `HOME` and None for an unset or relative `HOME`, regardless of what `XDG_DATA_HOME` holds (unlike `data_home`, which answers an absolute `XDG_DATA_HOME` with no `HOME`); the existing `xdg_homes` behaviors (data home resolution, empty/relative `XDG_DATA_HOME` fallback) read back unchanged. README prose and the invariant row pass their register checks; existing apply tests keep passing with unchanged stubs; `make check` is green after the final edit.

### Diagnose the pointer selection left behind by `make uninstall` (planned 2026-11-04 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-04 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Every selection `make apply` publishes gets an uninstall diagnostic in `Makefile`'s `_uninstall` block: `kdeglobals`' color scheme (reset `plasma-apply-colorscheme BreezeLight`), the GTK `settings.ini`/`gtk.css` selections (reset `make remove-gtk`), and the Kvantum kvconfig selection (reset `make remove-kvantum`). The pointer selection has none: `make apply-cursor` runs `plasma-apply-cursortheme` (`tools/cursor_link.py::CURSOR_THEME = "org.macos8.desktop"`), which writes `[Mouse] cursorTheme` in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/kcminputrc`, `make uninstall` deletes the installed icon theme under `Makefile`'s `ICON_THEME_ID`, and afterwards Xcursor silently keeps the default pointer — the same silent-fallback gap the other three diagnostics close. `tools/cursor_config.py::cursor_theme_setting` documents exactly how kcminputrc is read (`utf-8-sig`, `[Mouse]` section, `cursorTheme` key, comments never keys), and `tools/cursor_workflow.py::remove`'s note names the reset (`run plasma-apply-cursortheme breeze_cursors to reset`) — but it only fires on an explicit `make remove-cursor`, never after `make uninstall`. Grep of `Makefile`, README.md, PLANS.md, PLANS-DONE.md and BUGS.md found no uninstall diagnostic for kcminputrc, only the removal-time note.

**Approach and files.** Makefile, one new test module, docs/invariants.md and README.md. In `_uninstall`, after the existing kvconfig guard block and reusing the already-resolved `$$config_home`, add a fourth diagnostic: when `$config_home/kcminputrc` is a regular file, an awk that mirrors the three existing awk scanners — strip the first line's UTF-8 BOM, trim each line before parsing, a trimmed `[`…`]` line switches the section, `#`/`;` lines are comments and never keys, key/value split at the first `=` with both sides trimmed, and the last duplicate's value wins — recognizes a `[Mouse]` section `cursorTheme` whose value trims to `$(ICON_THEME_ID)` and prints on stderr exactly: `uninstall: the pointer selection still names $(ICON_THEME_ID) after removal in <kcminputrc>; Xcursor applications cannot load the removed cursor theme and keep the default pointer. Reset it with: plasma-apply-cursortheme breeze_cursors` — diagnostic only, never editing the file, and unlike the two make-target resets this one names an external command because `tools/cursor_workflow.py::remove` deliberately leaves kcminputrc untouched and `make remove-cursor` owns only the `$HOME/.icons` link (it also clears nothing of the selection, so the color-scheme-style external reset is the proven pattern). `breeze_cursors` is KDE's default pointer theme, a platform-required value inherited from the existing removal note; no reference screenshot shows a pointer, so no pixel is sampled. Precede the new awk with a comment paragraph in the style of the existing `_uninstall` comment block recording the scanner semantics and the never-edit rule. The three existing awk diagnostics and their wordings, `tools/cursor_config.py`, `tools/cursor_workflow.py`, `tools/cursor_link.py` and the removal path stay byte-identical.

**Tests.** New `tests/test_cursor_uninstall_diagnostic.py`, driving `make uninstall` through `tests/support/theme_install.py::run_make` on a temp `DESTDIR` with a throwaway config home, in the pattern of `tests/test_colorscheme_install.py` and the kvconfig-diagnostic tests in `tests/test_remove_kvantum.py`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- After `make uninstall` on a host whose freshly written kcminputrc holds `[Mouse] cursorTheme=org.macos8.desktop` between unrelated lines, the run exits 0, prints on stderr the exact reset line above with the real absolute path substituted, and the file reads back byte-identical; comments and CRLF line endings around the key do not change this, and a BOM-prefixed file is still recognized.
- A foreign value (`cursorTheme=breeze_cursors`), an empty value, `cursorTheme` under any other section, a key of a different name in `[Mouse]`, and an absent or unreadable kcminputrc each print nothing and leave `make uninstall` succeeding; with both `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` unset and `HOME` unset the guard stays empty and nothing is checked; with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` relative and `HOME` absolute the check falls back to `$HOME/.config` exactly like the three existing blocks, whose shared guard ignores a relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` before falling back (the planned wording said nothing is checked, which misread the guard shared with the color-scheme block; corrected 2026-11-04 by the feature role).
- A duplicate key where our id appears on an earlier line and `breeze_cursors` on the later one is silent; the reverse order fires; a value that only trims to our id (surrounding spaces) still fires.
- The color-scheme, GTK and kvconfig diagnostic tests still pass with their exact existing wordings; `make -n uninstall` still parses. README.md documents the pointer diagnostic and its reset beside the existing Kvantum/KGTK uninstall-warning prose, and docs/invariants.md's cursor row names the new test module in its tests column. `make check` passes after the final edit.

### Add `make remove-kvantum` clearing the Kvantum selection (planned 2026-11-04 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-04 by the feature role

**Goal.** `make apply` selects the Kvantum widget theme with `kvantummanager --set org.macos8.desktop` (`tools/theme_apply_optional.py::select_kvantum_theme`), which writes the user's `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Kvantum/kvantum.kvconfig`: `[General] theme=org.macos8.desktop` (verified on this host 2026-11-04 — the file is 35 bytes, exactly that selection). Every other selected surface has a removal and an uninstall diagnostic: `make remove-gtk`, `remove-cursor` and `remove-firefox`, and `make uninstall`'s awk block prints a dangling-selection diagnostic naming each reset command (color scheme, then GTK). The Kvantum selection has neither: after `make uninstall` a Qt application silently draws Kvantum's compiled-in default, and the only route out is editing the selection file by hand. `make install` correctly leaves it alone (a selection the user wrote through System Settings must survive an uninstall), so the missing piece is a removal target plus the matching uninstall diagnostic — one change, because the diagnostic names the reset command, so neither is shippable without the other.

**Approach and files.**

1. New `tools/kvantum_selection.py`: a pure transform plus a small driver. `remove_theme(text) -> tuple[str, bool]` mirrors `tools/gtk_settings.py::remove_theme_name` for the `[General]` section and the `theme` key: strip a leading UTF-8 BOM for matching and write it back, reuse the generic line/section scanners (`_split_bom`, `_split_lines`, `_join_lines`, `_section_name`, `_key_name`, `_ENDINGS`) imported from `tools.gtk_settings` unchanged so mixed endings, comments (`#`/`;`) and a `[:no close]` header behave exactly as the GTK tests pin them; delete only lines whose key is `theme` in `[General]` whose value trims to exactly `org.macos8.desktop` (constant `KVANTUM_ID`, the same id `Makefile`'s `KVANTUM_ID` and `tools/theme_apply_optional.py::KVANTUM_THEME` name), keep every other line byte-identical with its own ending, and return the text unchanged when nothing matched. The docstring keeps the existing scanner semantics documented; `tools/gtk_settings.py`'s behavior itself must not change — its tests pin it.
2. The same module carries the driver (`TOOL = "remove_kvantum"`, exit statuses in the module docstring, `Usage::` line for direct and `python3 -m` runs): resolve the config home with `tools/xdg_homes.py::config_home`, refusing with exit 2 and the same unset/empty/relative wording style `tools/apply_gtk.py`'s home-resolution refusals use (the message names `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `HOME`); serialize with `tools/file_lock.py::exclusive_flock` over the config home's parent directory, `LOCK_TIMEOUT = 60.0` mirroring `apply_gtk.py::_config_lock`, timing out with exit 2; refuse (exit 2, naming the path, before opening the target) a `Kvantum` directory or `kvantum.kvconfig` path in the config home that is a symbolic link, in the precedent of `tools/symlink_refusal.py` and `apply_gtk`'s symlink refusals; publish with `tools/atomic_write.py` after a successful read, so a mid-run failure leaves the previous file intact; and create nothing — an absent config home, absent `Kvantum/` directory or absent `theme` key exits 0 without writing anything. The removal never touches the data home or the installed theme files, and never adds or removes any other kvconfig key (`kvantummanager` owns the rest of that file).
3. `Makefile`: a public `.PHONY` target `remove-kvantum` shaped like `remove-gtk` (`require_python_ready`, then `$(PYTHON) tools/kvantum_selection.py`; no install prerequisite, no `DESTDIR` word), its `help` echo line, and a third dangling-selection diagnostic in the `_uninstall` block inside the existing `if [ -n "$$config_home" ]` chassis: an awk over `$config_home/Kvantum/kvantum.kvconfig` that recognizes a `[General]` section `theme` whose value trims to the id (same header/trim/comment semantics as the two existing awk diagnostics, and taking the last duplicate's value like the color-scheme one), printing to stderr `uninstall: the Kvantum selection still names $(KVANTUM_ID) after removal in <path>; Kvantum applications cannot load the removed theme and keep their default style. Clear it with: make remove-kvantum` — diagnostic only, never editing the file. The two existing color-scheme and GTK diagnostics must stay byte-identical.
4. `README.md`: beside the Installing prose that documents `make remove-gtk` and the Kvantum selection (`kvantummanager --set`, the `theme/kvantum/org.macos8.desktop/` art, the `$HOME/.local/share/themes/<name>/Kvantum/` search path), document `make remove-kvantum`: it clears only our `[General] theme=org.macos8.desktop` selection in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Kvantum/kvantum.kvconfig`, leaving a foreign theme name and the rest of the file byte-identical; restart running Qt applications afterwards. State that `make uninstall` leaves that selection in place for System Settings users and names this reset when it still points at the removed theme.
5. `docs/invariants.md`: one row in the existing `## kvantum` table for the selection-removal guarantee, naming the new tests as its test and recording the provenance exception (the selection-file format, the `[General]`/`theme` key names and the id are Kvantum- and KDE-required platform values the reference screenshot set does not show; observed in the real `kvantummanager`-written file on this host 2026-11-04).

**Tests.** `tests/test_remove_kvantum.py` (transform + driver, run in-process under a throwaway config home in the style of `tests/support/apply_gtk_case.py` and `tests/support/cli_fixtures.py::run_main`), and `tests/test_kvantum_selection_make.py` (Makefile target and uninstall diagnostic through `tests/support/theme_install.py::run_make`/`uninstall` on a temp `DESTDIR`, in the pattern of `tests/test_colorscheme_install.py`). Pin: our key removed while a foreign `[General]` key, other sections' keys, comments and CRLF line endings read back byte-identical; a foreign `theme` value and a matching name under any other section untouched with exit 0 and an unchanged file; every duplicate matching line removed (the last of them included); a BOM-prefixed and an indented-header file handled; exit 0 with no `Kvantum/` directory or file created when none exists; a symlinked selection file refused without following it; an unresolvable config home exits 2 naming `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`HOME`; a lock held by another run times out with exit 2 naming `remove-kvantum`; `make -n remove-kvantum` prints the script, `make help` lists it; the uninstall diagnostic fires only when the selection still names the id (last-duplicate winner), prints the exact reset command above, does not fire for a foreign theme or an overridden earlier match, and leaves the kvconfig unedited.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- Given a `kvantum.kvconfig` containing `[General] theme=org.macos8.desktop` among foreign lines, `make remove-kvantum` exits 0 and the file reads back with our line gone and every other byte identical, including mixed line endings and a preserved BOM; a second run exits 0 and changes nothing; with no kvconfig present, it exits 0 and creates neither the `Kvantum/` directory nor the file; with `theme=KvBreezeDark` (or our id under a non-`[General]` section), it exits 0 and the file is byte-identical. A `Kvantum/kvantum.kvconfig` that is a symlink exits 2 with a message naming the path, and nothing is read from or written to the link target.
- When the removal cannot take the config-home lock within its bounded wait, it exits 2 with a message naming `remove-kvantum`; when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is relative and `HOME` is unset, it exits 2 naming both rather than guessing a path.
- After `make uninstall` on a host whose kvconfig still names `org.macos8.desktop`, the run succeeds and prints on stderr the exact `Clear it with: make remove-kvantum` diagnostic above, and the kvconfig is unchanged; a foreign selection (or an earlier `org.macos8.desktop` key overridden by a later foreign one) prints nothing; the two existing kdeglobals and GTK diagnostics still fire as their tests pin.

### Inactive windows: draw the reference's buttonless bar and `#777777` title text (planned 2026-11-04 by the director role) — done 2026-11-04 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** The user reports that unfocused windows look wrong overall and that the close box becomes invisible when hovered. The reference set settles both: in `macos8.6-screenshots/desktop_fandom.png` (2560x1442, 2 image px per logical px) the four unfocused windows ("Mac OS 8.6", "Utilities", "Apple System Profiler", "Applications") draw a flat `#DDDDDD` (221,221,221) title bar and frame and **no close, zoom or collapse boxes at all**, with centered title text whose glyph cores sample `#777777` (119,119,119; read 2026-11-04 from a lossless decode with `tools/png/loader.py`: `Utilities` bar at x=880..1745 y=110..116, title cores x=1295..1540 y=112..146; `Applications` bar x=30..815 y=872..878, cores x=350..560 y=880..915). The shipped theme instead keeps the reference's box art on unfocused windows flattened to `#CCCCCC` (`tests/test_aurorae_buttons.py::TestButtons.test_inactive_center_is_flat`) and greys titles with `InactiveTextColor=153,153,153` in `theme/aurorae/themes/org.macos8.desktop/org.macos8.desktoprc`. Focus model: Mac OS 8.6 has exactly one active window — the frontmost one — and Plasma/KWin already realizes that model (a single active client at a time; the theme only draws the inactive look), so no focus emulation is planned; matching the inactive reference drawing is the whole task.

**Approach and files.**

1. `theme/aurorae/themes/org.macos8.desktop/close.svg`, `maximize.svg`, `restore.svg`, `shade.svg`: replace every group whose element prefix contains `inactive` (`inactive-center`, and — only if the companion BUGS.md erasure fix has already added them — `hover-inactive-center`, `pressed-inactive-center`, `deactivated-inactive-center`) with fully transparent art on the same canvas. Keep `active-center` untouched. The `inactive` prefix element must stay present in each SVG: `/usr/share/kwin/aurorae/AuroraeButton.qml` (KWin 6.3.6) shows that when `supportsInactive` is false the `buttonActive` overlay draws the active art on unfocused windows, so the emptiness ships as transparent art, not a deleted element. With every inactive-state overlay painting nothing, hover and press cannot erase anything (nothing is the design), which dissolves the companion bug's symptom.
2. `org.macos8.desktoprc`: change `InactiveTextColor` from `153,153,153` to `119,119,119`, provenance `desktop_fandom.png` as sampled above (platform note: KWin renders the title color; the samples pin it; the bar's flat #DDDDDD interior held the pinned pixels used by `TestInactiveCaption`, the top rows keeping the desktop background).
3. Tests. In `tests/test_aurorae_buttons.py`: replace `test_inactive_center_is_flat` with a test that every inactive-prefix group's rendered slice is fully transparent (alpha 0 at every pixel) while keeping the `test_inactive_glyphs_survive`-era requirement only in its new vacuous form (no differing points, nothing drawn); keep `assert_unique_ids` and the self-contained checks. Add a test that each button SVG still carries exactly one `inactive`-prefix element (guards the KWin fallback above). In `tests/test_aurorae_rc.py` expect the title colour `119,119,119` (there was no prior InactiveTextColor assertion; the value had no test) via a new reference-pixel assertion re-deriving (119,119,119) and the (221,221,221) bar field from `desktop_fandom.png` through the existing `ReferenceImageCase` fixtures (README's skip-without-LFS rule applies). `tests/support/aurorae_fixtures.py::inactive_fill` keeps serving Kvantum's MDI disabled buttons, so leave it and `tests/test_kvantum_svg.py` alone.
4. `docs/invariants.md` and README. Rewrite the two Aurorae provenance rows (the buttons row that currently records the flattened `#CCCCCC` boxes and the frame row that already grounds the inactive field) to record: reference-unfocused windows draw no boxes (source `desktop_fandom.png`), shipped inactive button art is transparent so the columns and rows of the former greys are unshipped, and the continued presence of an `inactive`-prefix element is platform-required by `AuroraeButton.qml`'s KWin-fallback semantics (named source of the value). In README's Installing prose, if it mentions the greyed boxes or inactive title colour, align the wording.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- Rendering each button SVG's `inactive-center` slice yields a fully transparent image of the same canvas size; every pixel of the rendered slices is RGBA (0,0,0,0) — nothing ships for unfocused windows, matching the reference's boxless bars.
- The `active-center` slices still pass their existing reference pins (`test_close_box_matches_reference`, `test_zoom_box_matches_reference`, `test_collapse_box_matches_reference`, and `tests/test_aurorae_reference_equivalence.py`) byte-for-byte, so focused windows keep the reference art.
- Each button SVG contains exactly one element id whose prefix contains `inactive`, present only for the fallback reason documented in `docs/invariants.md`.
- `tests/test_aurorae_rc.py` expects `InactiveTextColor=119,119,119` and a new reference assertion re-derives the text-core `#777777` and bar-field `#DDDDDD` samples from `desktop_fandom.png` by exact pixel coordinates recorded in the test.
- On a live Plasma session (manual spot check, not an automated gate), an unfocused window shows a plain `#DDDDDD` bar with `#777777` centered title text and no boxes; hovering or pressing it changes nothing visible.
- `docs/invariants.md` carries the rewritten provenance for the two Aurorae rows in the same change, README's prose (if touched) stays accurate, and `make check` passes after the final edit.

In `tools/fidelity.py::main`, reject use without `--difference-runs` before source reads. After the existing minimum and maximum horizontal length filters, retain the first N eligible intervals in row-major order and compute the eligible count minus the emitted count. Pass that optional count through `tools/fidelity_reports.py::report_data` as top-level JSON `omitted_difference_runs`; `tools/fidelity_rendering.py::render_text` prints `omitted difference runs: N` immediately after the horizontal run list, including zero. Compute requested run counts and longest summaries before filtering and capping, as today. This is an output cap: retain the existing full-list segmentation, with no memory-bound claim, pagination or vertical cap. Add `tests/test_fidelity_difference_runs_limit.py` using `FidelityCliTestCase` and generated PNG fixtures like `TestDifferenceRunsMaximumLength`; document the option beside horizontal run filtering in README.md and add a tooling guarantee in docs/invariants.md. **Acceptance criteria.**
- Against a black 9x2 reference, a candidate with red-channel delta 20 at x={0,2,3,5,6,7} on row 0 and x={0,1,2,3,8} on row 1 has five horizontal intervals. Limit 2 emits exactly `(0,0,1)` and `(2,0,2)` as `{x,y,length}` records and reports 3 omitted. Minimum length 2 with limit 1 emits `(2,0,2)` and omits 2; maximum length 2 with limit 2 emits the two original leading intervals and omits 1. Contradictory length cutoffs return an empty list with 0 omitted. These outcomes catch capping before filtering and restarting the cap per row.
- Limit 5 or larger emits the complete eligible list with 0 omitted; identical images and tolerance 20 on that fixture emit an empty list with 0 omitted. Requested `difference_run_count` stays 5 and `longest_difference_run` stays `(0,1,4)` under the cap. Metrics, bounds, vertical diagnostics and verdict match the uncapped comparison, including both default failure and a passing aggregate budget. A nonzero-origin crop retains crop-relative coordinates. Text and JSON describe the same intervals and omitted count; omission of the new option adds neither metadata nor text.
- Zero, negative, fractional and non-ASCII limits, and a missing value, fail with status 2 and empty stdout. A valid limit without `--difference-runs` fails before image access with a diagnostic naming both flags. Help and README distinguish the report-count cap from the per-interval length cutoff and explain the full-list allocation. `make check` passes after the final edit.

### Offer an explicit keyboard-swap removal command (planned 2026-11-04 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-04 by the feature role

**Goal.** Let a user reverse the modifier swap selected by `make apply` with `make remove-keymap`, preserving their other XKB options. README currently offers only manual reversal in System Settings. Searches of the current helper, Makefile, Planned entries and finished-plan archive found no keyboard-swap removal command; the finished removal-guide entry documents the manual route.

**Approach and files.** Add `--remove` to `tools/apply_keymap.py::main` and a removal branch in `_apply`. Split and trim the comma-separated value from `_read_options`, remove exact `OPTION` tokens (including duplicates), and retain the remaining nonempty tokens in their original order. If the swap is absent, return success without writing configuration or emitting a reload. Otherwise pass the remaining comma-joined value, including an empty string when the swap was the sole option, through `_write_options`; retain `ResetOldOptions=true` so KWin clears its previously active options when applying the reduced set. Reload only after both writes succeed. Keep the current default apply path. Adjust `_reload`'s fallback notes to describe keyboard-option changes taking effect at next login, so removal does not claim that a swap will be enabled. This is explicit token removal, not restoration of a saved configuration or a claim of ownership of a pre-existing swap.

Add a public `.PHONY` `remove-keymap` target in `Makefile`, guarded by `require_python_ready` and `refuse_destdir`, invoking the helper with `--remove`; list it in `help`. Extend `tests/test_apply_keymap.py` using `StubTools` and the existing command-order/failure fixtures; add a Make dry-run assertion for the new target there. Update README's Installing and Removing the theme instructions and the keyboard-option row in `docs/invariants.md`. These five files are the scope; no automatic uninstall behavior or new dependency. Keep added behavior and tests within a few hundred lines.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Given `caps:escape,ctrl:swap_lalt_lctl,compose:ralt,ctrl:swap_lalt_lctl`, removal writes `caps:escape,compose:ralt`, writes `ResetOldOptions=true`, then signals reload. A similarly named token such as `ctrl:swap_lalt_lctl_extra` survives. Tests independently specify the expected retained options, catching a substring-removal or wrong-branch bug.
- Given only the swap, removal writes an empty Options value and enables option reset before reload. Given an empty value or options without the swap, it exits 0 without writes or reload; a repeated removal against the resulting configuration has that same no-op outcome.
- A failed read performs no writes; a failed Options or ResetOldOptions write performs no reload and returns the existing required-command failure status. A successful removal with missing or failing reload emitters exits 0 and explains that the keyboard-option changes take effect at next login. The default apply behavior remains covered by its existing tests.
- `make -n remove-keymap` names the helper's removal flag without an install step; a nonempty DESTDIR is refused before configuration changes. `make help` and README identify the command as removing this specific swap while leaving other options, and explain that it cannot restore previous keyboard settings. The invariant row names the removal coverage, and `make check` passes after the final edit.

### Fidelity comparison metrics: separate crop geometry from comparison state (planned 2026-11-04 by the organize role) — done 2026-11-04 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tools/fidelity_metrics.py` is the largest production Python module (265 lines). Its `compare()` function is a single large pipeline that validates images, builds channel deltas, accumulates metrics, locates the maximum, counts threshold mismatches and derives their bounds. Keeping this pipeline together with the independently reusable crop geometry makes the module harder to navigate and couples crop-only callers to comparison implementation.

Keep `Metrics` and `compare()` in `tools/fidelity_metrics.py`, which owns comparison results and calculations; import and re-export the geometry names there to preserve existing imports such as `tools.fidelity_metrics.crop`. Keep the comparison state local to `compare()`; do not introduce a second abstraction for its intermediate channel data.

**Files.** `tools/fidelity_metrics.py`, new `tools/fidelity_geometry.py`, `tools/fidelity.py`, `tests/test_fidelity_metrics.py`, and `docs/invariants.md` if the existing fidelity tooling invariant needs its module ownership updated. Update README or other markdown references only where they describe the moved ownership.

**Acceptance criteria.** The two production modules have the stated responsibilities; existing imports continue to resolve; grep across source, tests and markdown finds no stale ownership or moved-name references; `make check` passes. ### Platinum GTK 4 dialog render surface: pin the rendered headerbar close button 1:1 (planned 2026-11-03 by the plan role; independent of every refused entry in this queue — it touches only `tests/test_render_surface.py` and the `## tooling` row of `docs/invariants.md`, no CSS sheet, tool file or `tests/test_gtk*` module any waiting entry owns, so it can run alongside any of them; it is a pin of the landed capture, not a CSS restatement — the refused CSD-shell and window-shell entries refuse *restates* that would undo the landed Aurorae outline, and no `## Planned` entry, PLANS-DONE.md record or `docs/invariants.md` row claims the GTK capture's close-button cell — the landed Cancel and shell-edge records name it an unpinned candidate of their own) — done 2026-11-04 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed `TestGtkDialogRender` gate byte-compares four cells of its pooled 480x360 zenity `--entry` capture: the entry field, the OK and Cancel push buttons and the window's top shell edge. The same capture paints the headerbar close button — the landed `headerbar windowcontrols button.close` rule paints the shipped `window-close.svg` asset (a 13x13 canvas whose `active-center` group is pinned byte-identical to the Aurorae `close.svg` source by `tests/test_gtk_title_buttons.py`) at `background-size: 13px 13px`, `background-position: center`, centred in the 16px min hit area, at the headerbar's right end. The landed Cancel and shell-edge records deliberately left it out — "The headerbar close button ... remain[s] an unpinned candidate of its own." Grep confirms no backlog entry or archived record claims that candidate for the GTK capture. Close it if it renders pixel-aligned: after this entry the same live capture byte-compares the shipped SVG art's rendered pixels, so a change to the shipped asset or the close-button recipe that zenity really renders fails `make check` instead of only the asset-equality declaration checks — one more "Declaration checks do not establish rendered pixels" gap closed the way the other four pins closed theirs.

**Approach and files.** Two gates, in order, in `tests/test_render_surface.py`:

1. **Pixel-alignment gate first — the run's Go/No-Go.** The 16px hit area centres the 13px art at a nominal 1.5px horizontal and vertical offset (`(16-13)/2`), and the 22px headerbar floor adds its own centring offset; GTK may round that to an integer pixel grid or draw a blended, resampled image. Before pinning anything, the feature run renders a fresh consecutive pair of full `tools/render_surface.py out1.png out2.png --gtk-dialog` runs (a third consecutive run reproducing bit for bit under `cmp`, recorded like the OK pin's determinism record), locates the close button's rendered art at the headerbar's right end, and checks that the art renders on an integer pixel grid: a 13x13 block of crisp `active-center` colours with no half-blended edge row or column. If it does, proceed to step 2. If it does not — blended edge pixels, an off-grid resample, stock's glyph circle or any other foreign paint in the cell — the close button is not pinnable under the shipped recipe, and the run records that finding in its summary and stops: no crop constant, no new test, and the `## tooling` row's provenance cell is amended only to record the finding. Pinning blended pixels would mean sampling the capture itself, which the landed pins' recipe-derived byte-compare contract forbids.

2. **The pin.** Add a module-level `CLOSE_BUTTON_CROP = (x, y, width, height)` measured on that bit-identical pair, with the measurement, the alignment finding and the determinism record written into the constant's comment and the `## tooling` row's provenance cell, and add `TestGtkDialogRender::test_draws_the_close_button_cell_1_to_1` beside `test_draws_the_window_shell_edge_cell_1_to_1`: read the pooled capture through `_DialogGate::candidate_image`, crop `CLOSE_BUTTON_CROP`, and byte-compare each pixel against an expected map re-derived from `render_slices(parse_svg(<the shipped assets/window-close.svg>))["active-center"]` — the same machinery `tests/test_gtk_title_buttons.py` uses (`support.gtk_fixtures.PACKAGE` for the asset path, `support.svg_case.parse_svg` and `svg_assertions.render_slices`, both already imported at the top of `tests/test_render_surface.py`) — placed at the integer offset the alignment gate measured, never sampled from the capture itself. The test's comment records the crop position, the asset's provenance (the reference-grounded Aurorae `close.svg` `active-center` group), the measured integer offset and the two-run determinism pair (host, capture size, crop, `cmp` agreement) the way the OK pin's comment records the action row's. A one-pixel crop or offset slip, a recoloured or swapped asset (the maximize or minimize art standing in for the close art), a resampled or blended art, or a stray stock paint fails the byte-compare by dictionary equality.

**Scope boundary.** No new render mode, client, flag or pool entry — the landed `--gtk-dialog` capture is only read again, so the render plumbing (`tools/render_clients.py`, `tools/render_surface.py`, `tools/render_setup.py`, `tools/render_workflow.py`), the skip guards, CI workflow and README prose need nothing; `tests/test_readme_render_gates.py` sees no new gate class. No CSS declaration changes — no GTK 3 or GTK 4 sheet, Kvantum, Firefox, artwork, install or dependency change; in particular this entry does not touch the 16px hit area, the `background-position`/`background-size` arms or the shipped asset (whether a fractional-offset render that fails the alignment gate warrants steering the engine to a native-size render or re-deriving the art at the engine's drawn size is a separate restatement decision, not this pin's). The landed entry-field, OK-button, Cancel-button and shell-edge pins (`ENTRY_FIELD_CROP`, `OK_BUTTON_CROP`, `CANCEL_BUTTON_CROP`, `WINDOW_SHELL_EDGE_CROP` and their tests) stay byte-unchanged; the kdialog gates and every `tests/test_gtk*` module stay byte-unchanged; the CSD window shell is already pinned by the landed shell-edge pin, and the title text is the only candidate this entry leaves unpinned (a glyph-bearing region, out of scope like the button labels).

**Acceptance criteria.** If the alignment gate passes: reading `tests/test_render_surface.py` shows `CLOSE_BUTTON_CROP` with its measurement provenance commented and `test_draws_the_close_button_cell_1_to_1` beside the shell-edge test; deleting the test, cropping one pixel off the cell, shifting the expected map one pixel off the measured integer offset, substituting the maximize or minimize asset's slices for the close art's, or re-deriving the expectation from the capture's own pixels fails the new test by dictionary equality. If the alignment gate fails: no crop constant and no new test exist, `tests/test_render_surface.py` stays byte-unchanged, and the run's summary and the `## tooling` row record the blended-render finding. Either way the four landed pins stay byte-unchanged and green, the `## tooling` row carries the close-button sentence (a pin record or the not-pinnable finding), `tests/test_invariants.py` accepts the amended row, and `make check` is green after the final edit.

Probed 2026-11-03 with `gresource` extracting `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` from `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0` (libgtk-3 3.24.49) under a scratch directory, the resource declares the grouped base arm `stacksidebar row.needs-attention > label, .stack-switcher > button.needs-attention > label, .stack-switcher > button.needs-attention > image` with `animation: needs_attention 150ms ease-in; background-image: -gtk-gradient(radial, center center, 0, center center, 0.5, to(#3584e4), to(transparent)), -gtk-gradient(radial, center center, 0, center center, 0.5, to(rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.769231)), to(transparent)); background-size: 6px 6px, 6px 6px; background-repeat: no-repeat; background-position: right 3px, right 4px;` — the toolkit's radial-gradient spelling on the label and image nodes, animated by the resource's own `@keyframes needs_attention` block — plus three residual size/position arms following that base: the `:backdrop` twin (`background-size: 6px 6px, 0 0`), the `:dir(rtl)` twin (`background-position: left 3px, left 4px`) and a late bare `stacksidebar row.needs-attention > label { background-size: 6px 6px, 0 0; }` arm. One stock counter-arm already clears the active and checked states alone (`.stack-switcher > button.needs-attention:active/:checked > label/image` carries `animation: none; background-image: none;`), so only the unselected sidebar row and the unselected page's button pulse. Grep confirms the shipped GTK 3 sheet names no `needs-attention` token at all, no landed rule touches these labels' `background-image` or animation (the landed `stackswitcher > button` face groups paint only the button node, and the landed list-row focus restatement targets `list row:focus`), no `PLANS.md` `## Planned` sibling, `PLANS-DONE.md` finished record or `docs/invariants.md` row covers them, and no landed GTK 3 family scan reads the `needs-attention` token — so today an attention-marked row or page button paints and animates stock's pulsing dot inside the landed tab-recipe faces, in conflict with the landed motion policy that removed stock animation on the row, tab, button and entry families.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, insert one dated (2026-11-03) adaptation comment — naming the missing needs-attention reference surface and recording the value source without naming any toolkit or library brand and without any hex literal, because `TestGtkTheme::test_imports_nothing_and_does_not_mention_adwaita` rejects toolkit names and `TestGtkTheme::test_only_palette_hex_literals` scans the raw sheet text — then exactly ONE grouped rule whose selectors are the three byte-equal stock twin spellings `stacksidebar row.needs-attention > label, .stack-switcher > button.needs-attention > label, .stack-switcher > button.needs-attention > image` declaring exactly `animation: none; background-image: none;`, spelled so the rule wins by later source order at equal specificity against the stock theme resource (the standing GTK 3 cascade premise the landed selection and disabled-selected records use). Byte-equality is what makes it win: the stack switcher's stock arm spells the widget as a CLASS selector (`.stack-switcher`), so a type-spelled `stackswitcher` restatement would answer with one fewer class token and lose — the byte-equal spelling is required, matching how stock wrote the arm. The three residual stock arms then paint nothing anywhere: their `background-size`/`background-position` declarations govern an image the restated rule removed, the resource's `@keyframes needs_attention` block loses its last user, and the stock active/checked counter-arm keeps its own clearing value — deliberately undeclared, so stock holds that state. No GTK 4, Kvantum, Firefox, artwork, install or dependency change.

In `tests/test_gtk_theme_views.py`, add `TestGtkThemeViews::test_needs_attention_badges` beside `test_stack_switcher_tabs`: assert with `assert_rule_group` (tests/support/gtk_rule_cases.py) that each of the three byte-equal spellings maps to exactly `{"animation": "none", "background-image": "none"}` and occurs exactly once in `self.selectors`; assert source order — `self.selectors.index(".stack-switcher > button.needs-attention > label")` is greater than `self.selectors.index("stackswitcher > button:checked:hover")` (both anchors are grep-unique in the GTK 3 sheet); and add one family scan over the whole parsed sheet: `{s for s in self.rules if "needs-attention" in s}` equals exactly those three spellings — the landed sheet carries no other `needs-attention` hit today (verified by grep), so the scan kills renamed and stray variants, including a skipped residual `:backdrop`/`:dir(rtl)`/bare-sidebar arm accidentally restated with real size or position values. `parse_css` never sees the removed gradient values (the restated rule carries only `animation: none` and `background-image: none`), so the suite needs no new GTK 3 value parsing.

Append one dated row at the end of the `## gtk` table in `docs/invariants.md` naming `TestGtkThemeViews::test_needs_attention_badges`, recording that a `needs-attention` classed stack-sidebar row or stack-switcher label or image keeps the landed inherited paint with no stock pulse animation, that no collected reference screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows GTK needs-attention badges (the standing GTK-scope adaptation premise — the clearing follows the landed row/tab `animation`/`transition` removals), the dated gresource probe above with the exact removed values quoted for full library attribution, and that the three residual stock arms are inert without an image while the stock active/checked counter-arm already clears its own states. Declaration checks do not establish rendered pulse absence or animation runs.

**Scope boundary.** The `window.assistant .sidebar > label` padding and highlight arms, the `stacksidebar row > label` side paddings and the `placessidebar` label paddings are separate unlabelled-spacing candidates. The landed `stackswitcher > button` face groups, the `list row:focus` outline and all landed `@keyframes spin` rules stay byte-unchanged; the GTK 4 needs-attention entry above owns the GTK 4 sheet's own three spellings.

**Acceptance criteria.** Reading the shipped GTK 3 sheet shows exactly one `needs-attention` group sitting after the landed `stackswitcher > button:checked,\nstackswitcher > button:checked:hover` face group and before the landed `tab:backdrop, tab.reorderable-page:backdrop,` block, holding exactly the three listed byte-equal selectors and the two listed declarations and nothing else; deleting the group, renaming a selector off its byte-equal stock twin (the `stackswitcher` type spelling substituted for stock's `.stack-switcher` class spelling included — the twin loses the cascade to stock's two-class arm, and the family scan still passes on a renamed spelling, so the byte-equal spelling, count-1 and source-order assertions must each hold), dropping one of the three spellings, adding a fourth spelling or a third declaration, or giving the rule `background-size`/`background-position` values fails `test_needs_attention_badges` by dictionary equality, count 1, the family scan, or the comment gates (`test_only_palette_hex_literals` catching a quoted hex literal, `test_imports_nothing_and_does_not_mention_adwaita` catching a toolkit name) respectively. The landed `test_stack_switcher_tabs`, `test_row_selection_backdrop`, `test_list_row_focus_outline` and `test_places_sidebar`, plus `TestGtkTheme::test_only_palette_hex_literals` and `test_imports_nothing_and_does_not_mention_adwaita`, stay byte-unchanged and green, `tests/test_invariants.py` accepts the new `## gtk` row, and `make check` is green after the final edit.

### Platinum GTK 4 plain spinbutton steppers: restate the stock horizontal stepper arms with the landed push-button recipe (planned 2026-11-03 by the plan role; mirrors the landed GTK 4 OSD steppers record — `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::test_osd_spinbutton_steppers` — onto the plain non-`.osd` arms that record's scope boundary named a separate unclaimed candidate, it extends no landed test: no strand of the landed OSD steppers or OSD entry-fields work touches it, every restated selector is non-`.osd`, the landed `test_osd_spinbutton_steppers` family scan pins only `.osd`-carrying spellings while the new scan excludes them, and the insertion seam sits in the plain spin-button family, pages before the OSD region, so either merge order with any claim on the OSD records leaves the cascade and the register right) — done 2026-11-03 by the feature role

**Goal.** Every plain GTK 4 spin button — one outside the landed OSD overlay band — still paints stock's ghost steppers. Stock GTK 4 (`/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css`, probed below) declares seven plain horizontal stepper groups the landed sheet never names: `spinbutton:not(.vertical) > button.image-button.up:not(.flat), …down:not(.flat)` with a transparent face (`background-image: none`, no background colour), a left-edge translucent separator `rgba(205, 199, 194, 0.3)` whose `:dir(rtl)` twin flips the edge, a `:hover` twin recolouring to `#2e3436` on `#ebe8e6`, a `:disabled` twin at `rgba(146, 149, 149, 0.3)` on a transparent face, an `:active` twin on translucent black `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)` with an inset `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2)` shadow, and two `:dir` corner arms rounding the outer ends `0 5px 5px 0` / `5px 0 0 5px`; and the dark resource declares byte-twin groups with dark-palette values. Each arm's class-and-pseudo-class specificity outranks the landed generic `button` group per-property, so a horizontal stepper today is an unpainted ghost with a faint separator, exactly the symptom the landed OSD steppers record just cured under the overlay band. The landed OSD vertical steppers inherit their face from the landed generic `button` restate, and stock's plain vertical arms (`spinbutton.vertical > button`, `…button.up`, `…button.down`) declare only geometry and the shared-edge asymmetry — up: no bottom border; down: no top border — that the landed linked-group records deliberately preserve (the `## gtk` rows pinning trailing-edge border style `none` in both toolkits), so the vertical side needs nothing and this entry leaves it stock. Grep confirms no plain `spinbutton … button` selector in the shipped GTK 4 sheet and none in `docs/invariants.md` outside the landed `.osd` rows.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, insert immediately after the landed `spinbutton.vertical > text.warning:focus-within, spinbutton.warning:focus-within:not(.vertical), entry.warning:focus-within` group and before the treeview-embedded-entry adaptation comment one dated (2026-11-03) adaptation comment naming the missing plain-spinbutton-stepper reference surface (no collected screenshot shows a GTK spin button's steppers in any state — the standing GTK-scope adaptation premise), quoting the seven probes below and naming the landed `test_osd_spinbutton_steppers` records as the sibling precedent, then SEVEN groups whose selectors are the byte-equal stock twins, so later source order beats each stock arm at equal specificity for every restated property. The recipe per group is exactly the landed OSD steppers record's dictionary (the landed `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::test_osd_spinbutton_steppers` `base` spec): a raised `#DDDDDD` `FACE` field, `background-image: none`, a 1px `#000000` border, `border-radius: 0`, the full-button etch `box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #999999`, `color: #000000`, `outline-color: #000000`, `text-shadow: none`, `-gtk-icon-shadow: none`. The seven groups: (1) the horizontal base twins declaring the full recipe — stock's `min-height: 16px`, `margin: 0` and zero vertical paddings stay in force here (the OSD base arm declared no geometry, which is why that record wrote none); (2) the `:dir(rtl)` separator twin declaring the full recipe; (3) the `:hover` twin declaring the full recipe (a byte-equal repeat of the face is what stock's hover recolour needs); (4) the `:disabled` twin declaring the recipe with `color: #888888` (`ETCH_DARK`) replacing black and no `outline-color` — the landed disabled colour, clearing stock's translucent grey label and transparent face; (5) the `:active` twin declaring the recipe with `box-shadow` swapped to the inverted bevel `inset 1px 1px #999999, inset -1px -1px #FFFFFF` — stock's plain horizontal family carries an `:active` arm the `.osd` family lacks, and the inverted bevel is the landed pressed semantics; (6)–(7) the `:dir(ltr):last-child` and `:dir(rtl):first-child` corner twins declaring the full recipe (the landed OSD corner arms carry it too, and its `border-radius: 0` clears stock's 5px outer corners). Stock's vertical arms and their geometry stay byte-unchanged in force (the landed face paints them; the shared-edge mechanism is preserved on purpose), as do the landed `.osd` stepper and entry-field groups directly below the seam, the `row.spin` families, and the inner-`text` field arms. No GTK 3 change (the GTK 3 sheet's own plain stepper family is a separate unclaimed candidate — the GTK 3 sheet names only `.osd spinbutton … button` groups today); no Kvantum, Firefox, artwork, install or dependency change.

### GTK 4 `window.solid-csd`: recolour the no-compositor window frame with the shell outline (planned 2026-11-03 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-03 by the feature role

**Goal.** A GTK 4 window that reaches the stock `window.solid-csd` arm — GTK's built-in frame for environments whose compositor cannot draw CSD shadows, where the toolkit paints the frame itself instead of deferring to the window manager — today shows stock Adwaita chrome: a `#cdc7c2` gray border, a 4px content gutter and a three-layer light inset bevel (`inset 0 0 0 4px #cdc7c2, inset 0 0 0 3px white, inset 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8)`; the backdrop arm swaps the `white` layer for `#f6f5f4`). The landed CSD shell restatement covered every other top level but this one — its bound family and its scope boundary explicitly left `window.solid-csd` untouched — so such a window still renders a light-gray Adwaita beam under Platinum. This plan closes that arm with the same outline language the landed shell pins: a hard 1px `#000000` frame active, `#555555` backdrop, no bevel, no soft shadow, square corners kept.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, inside the landed CSD tail block, insert after the `window.csd.dialog.message:backdrop` group and before the landed `window.maximized, window.fullscreen` group — matching the stock arm order, where the `solid-csd` arm and its `:backdrop` sibling precede `window.maximized` — one dated (2026-11-03) adaptation comment plus two restated groups. The comment names the three facts that warrant the border mechanism: no collected reference screenshot shows any GTK window shell, so the colours re-derive the shipped square Aurorae chrome (`#000000`/`#555555` pinned by `tests/test_aurorae_frame.py`); stock's own `.solid-csd` titlebar/headerbar arm (`margin-left/right/top: -1px`) expects a 1px window border to cover, so painting the outline as the window border keeps that geometry intact, whereas an inset `box-shadow` ring or an outside-spread ring would clip those negative-margin headerbars or vanish entirely in the no-compositor environments the arm exists for (an outside ring is clipped to the window bounds there); and the stock values probed this date from the `gresource` extract of `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-4.so.1` (libgtk-4 4.18.6), in its "Window Decorations" section: `window.solid-csd { margin: 0; padding: 4px; border: solid 1px #cdc7c2; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 4px #cdc7c2, inset 0 0 0 3px white, inset 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8); }` and `window.solid-csd:backdrop { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 4px #cdc7c2, inset 0 0 0 3px #f6f5f4, inset 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8); }`. The groups each declare only what must change from stock, exactly:

```
window.solid-csd {
  padding: 0;
  border: solid 1px #000000;
  box-shadow: none;
}

window.solid-csd:backdrop {
  border-color: #555555;
  box-shadow: none;
}
```

The landed 36354e81 bugfix tail arms are superseded and removed in the same change: they sat at the sheet tail after the maximized and tiled flats (out-ranking them), restated an outset `box-shadow` ring that a compositor-less window cannot paint outside its clipped bounds, and left stock's beige 1px `border` in force, so this entry replaces those twins with the groups above at the pre-maximized stock position. `margin: 0` and `border-radius: 0` stay stock-declared and are not restated. The backdrop group's appended source position and its 0-2-1 specificity beat both the stock `window.solid-csd:backdrop` bevel triple and the restated base arm, so neither returns when the window loses focus. In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, edit `TestGtk4Theme::test_csd_window_shell` in place: add to its `expected` dict `"window.solid-csd": {"padding": "0", "border": "solid 1px f-string BLACK", "box-shadow": "none"}` and `"window.solid-csd:backdrop": {"border-color": f-string INACTIVE_OUTLINE, "box-shadow": "none"}` (using the suite's `BLACK` and `INACTIVE_OUTLINE` constants, expecting `support.gtk_css.parse_css` to store the `border` shorthand under its `"border"` key as declared); extend the family-set assertion so the parsed top-level shell selectors additionally equal those two `window.solid-csd*` spellings; and add order assertions that `self.selectors.index("window.solid-csd")` follows `self.selectors.index("window.csd")` and precedes `self.selectors.index("window.maximized")`, and that `window.solid-csd:backdrop` follows `window.solid-csd`. Extend the guarantee sentence and provenance cell of the GTK 4 CSD shell row in the `## gtk` table of `docs/invariants.md` to cover the solid-csd top level, recording this probe date and source, that the border-painted outline (not a box-shadow ring) is the mechanism and why, and that declaration and source-order checks do not establish rendered pixels. GTK 3 stays out: selecting a GTK 3 theme replaces the stock stylesheet entirely, so no GTK 3 stock arm hides beneath the shipped sheet, and the landed record's reasoning binds here too. No artwork, install, Firefox or dependency change.

**Acceptance criteria.** Reading the shipped GTK 4 sheet shows the two `window.solid-csd*` groups each holding exactly the declarations above and no other property, sitting between the `window.csd.dialog.message:backdrop` and `window.maximized` groups; every other landed rule is byte-unchanged apart from removing the superseded tail solid-csd arms named in the approach. `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_csd_window_shell` passes with the two new expected dictionaries, the enlarged family set, and the order assertions; deleting one of the two groups, renaming a selector off its stock twin, changing `border` to `border-color` or to an inset-shadow ring, dropping the `box-shadow: none` line, or moving either group after `window.maximized` fails that test (the stock bevel or backdrop recolour would out-rank the square frame). The other GTK 4 test functions are untouched by the change: `make check CHECK_TESTS='test_gtk4_theme'` passes, `tests/invariants.py` accepts the extended `## gtk` row, and `make check` is green after the final edit.

### Platinum GTK 4 window shell: restate the compositor-less solid-csd frame with the landed Aurorae outline (planned 2026-11-03 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-03 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed GTK 4 CSD window-shell restatement (`PLANS-DONE.md`, 2026-11-03) pins the Platinum shell across the normal, popup, message-dialog, maximized, fullscreen, tiled, SSD and tooltip top levels but deliberately left `window.solid-csd` out — the arm GTK applies to a CSD window that cannot get a shadow-capable visual (an X11 session without compositing is the usual route). Today such a window still paints stock Adwaita chrome instead of the landed square hard outline: a 1px beige border, a 4px inset beige bevel with an inner white edge, or the `#f6f5f4` backdrop variant. Clearing it closes the shell family: after this restatement every stock `window`-node arm stock assigns its own chrome carries the landed Aurorae outline.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, insert immediately before the landed `window.maximized` group one dated (2026-11-03) adaptation comment recording the missing compositor-less GTK reference surface, stock's beige bevel (probe below) and the Aurorae outline provenance, then these two groups with byte-equal stock-twin selectors: `window.solid-csd` declaring exactly `padding: 0; border: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #000000;` and `window.solid-csd:backdrop` declaring exactly `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #555555;`. Stock's `margin: 0` and `border-radius: 0` already equal the Platinum values and are not restated; the inset ring is required geometry here — a compositor-less window cannot paint an outset shadow outside its allocation, which is why stock itself uses inset shadows in this state — and the 1px `#000000` active and `#555555` backdrop values are the landed `window.csd` / `window.csd:backdrop` literals. The insertion point preserves stock's own cascade semantics exactly: the arms sit after the landed `window.csd` and `window.csd:backdrop` groups (so source order settles any class conflict the same way stock does) and before the landed maximized/fullscreen and tiled flats, so a maximized/fullscreen solid-csd window keeps no shadow and a tiled solid-csd window keeps the later outset outline. No GTK 3 change: selecting a GTK 3 theme replaces the stock stylesheet entirely, so the GTK 3 `.solid-csd decoration` arm never applies and the shipped GTK 3 sheet already controls its shell pixels (the same reason the refused GTK 3 squaring entry above was refused). Match the sheet's existing declaration spelling (how other landed groups write `border: none` and padding) so the suite's parsed dictionaries read cleanly.

### Reference-pixel sampler: cumulative displayed palette coverage (planned 2026-11-03 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-03 by the feature role

**Goal.** Show how much of a sampled surface the displayed palette explains as colors accumulate, without making users sum individual fractions. Source and finished-plan searches found individual color fractions but no cumulative histogram diagnostic. This is independent of the waiting fidelity diagnostic.

**Approach and files.** Added the boolean `--color-cumulative-fractions` option with histogram-mode validation next to the existing color-fractions check, integer-first running accumulation over emitted colors in report order in `tools/sample_report_histogram.py::_histogram_result`, the `cumulative_fraction=VALUE` text suffix between the individual fraction and position fields, focused CLI tests in `tests/test_sample_histogram_cumulative_fractions.py`, `TestSampleOptionValidation` extension, README documentation and a dated invariant row. Coverage is page-local: excluded, filtered, skipped and trailing colors never enter the numerator.

**Acceptance criteria.** Implemented page-local cumulative coverage per the plan.
- An offset 4x2 crop with ordered color counts 3, 2, 2, 1 reports cumulative fractions `0.375, 0.625, 0.875, 1.0`; tied count-2 colors retain ascending tuple order. Surrounding pixels do not affect these values. `--top-colors 2` reports `0.375, 0.625`, and adding `--color-offset 1` reports `0.25, 0.5`, with the existing original palette totals and omitted-pixel values retained. This catches accidental inclusion of skipped colors or normalization by displayed pixels.
- Excluding the count-3 color reports `0.25, 0.5, 0.625`; count/fraction filtering likewise contributes only emitted counts. An empty filtered result or a page beyond the palette emits an empty colors array. A single-color crop ends at `1.0`; a three-pixel crop with three distinct colors ends at exactly `1.0`, demonstrating integer-prefix division rather than summed rounded fractions.
- RGB mode merges opacity variants; RGBA mode keeps them separate in existing count/tuple order, including stored RGB beneath zero alpha, and opaque input uses alpha 255. Combined individual fractions and spatial diagnostics retain their independently expected values. Without the flag, no cumulative field or text suffix appears. With it alone, individual fraction fields remain absent and the existing summary-field conditions remain intact.

### Reference-pixel sampler: count horizontal matching segments (planned 2026-11-03 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-03 by the feature role

In `tools/sample_report_search.py::_search_match`, enable horizontal collection for this flag while retaining lists only when `--match-runs` requests them; expose `match.run_count` only on request, after `finish`. These six files fit one implementation run; no vertical-count option belongs in this entry.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- An offset 4x3 crop at (2,1) with match masks `1101`, `0000`, `1111` reports JSON `match.run_count=3` and text `matching run count: 3`, with pixel count 7. Enabling the full horizontal list yields starts (2,1), (5,1), (2,3) and lengths 2,1,4. Minimum run length 3 leaves one listed run but still reports count 3; maximum length 1 likewise leaves one listed run and count 3. Coordinate limit 1 and an offset beyond the matching-pixel count leave the segment count 3. Existing longest-run and vertical-list reports agree with their uncombined results.
- A fully matching 3x2 crop reports 2 segments; a fully matching 1x3 crop reports 3, a matching single pixel reports 1, and no matches report 0. Matches on opposite row edges stay separate. Cropping excludes surrounding matches. Adjacent unequal RGB values within tolerance form one segment; a pixel outside tolerance splits it. Exact-alpha filtering can split otherwise adjacent matches, preserves stored RGB under zero alpha, and treats opaque RGB input as alpha 255.
- Count-only output contains neither horizontal nor vertical run arrays unless separately requested. A focused collector fixture with horizontal enabled and `collect_runs=False` observes separated matches, calls `finish`, and sees the literal expected count with an empty stored run list. Omitting the flag omits its JSON field and text line. Text/JSON and package/direct-script invocations agree; help lists the option.
- Without `--find-color`, the flag exits 2 with empty stdout and the dependency diagnostic before image access; guard `os.open`, `read_png_size` and `read_png` in this test. Existing earlier validation diagnostics retain precedence. Run `make check` after final edits.

### Theme apply: separate optional integrations from required selections (planned 2026-11-01 by the organize role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Clarify ownership in `tools/apply_theme.py`: its required selection loop is part of applying the installed theme, while `_run_best_effort`, `_select_kvantum_theme` and `_reconfigure_kwin` each implement optional external integrations with distinct missing-tool and failure policies. Keeping the optional command policy beside orchestration obscures which failures can change the apply status.

**Approach and files.** Keep `tools/apply_theme.py` responsible for CLI parsing, required selections, locking, scratch lifetime and exit status. Move `_run_best_effort`, `_select_kvantum_theme` and `_reconfigure_kwin` into a focused `tools/theme_apply_optional.py`, along with their optional tool constants and imports; expose one function that performs the optional selections in the existing Kvantum-then-KWin order. Preserve the current note wording, timeout/log names, return status and direct-script/package import behavior. Update `tests/test_apply_theme.py` and any direct helper references, then search source, tests and markdown for stale ownership references. Files: `tools/apply_theme.py`, new `tools/theme_apply_optional.py`, relevant apply tests, and `docs/invariants.md` only if the documented ownership needs correction.

**Acceptance criteria.** The optional commands still run under the existing data-home lock and scratch directory, after all required selections; either optional tool being missing, failing to start, timing out or exiting nonzero remains a note and leaves apply status unchanged. Existing command order, arguments, diagnostics and log filenames remain the same. Unit coverage exercises the extracted boundary, direct-script and package imports work, and `make check` passes.

### Reference-pixel sampler: locate emitted histogram colors (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Show where dominant palette colors occur without a separate `--find-color` invocation per color. `tools/sample_reports.py::report` emits histogram counts, while its find-color branch computes bounds for one selected RGB predicate. `tools/sample_arguments.py::build_parser` has no histogram-bounds option. Source option searches and related planned/archived sampler entries cover counts, top-color limits, single-color lookup and alpha grouping, rather than per-histogram-color bounds. This is independent of the queued fidelity budget.

**Approach and files.** Add boolean `--color-bounds` in `tools/sample_arguments.py::build_parser`; in `tools/sample.py::main`, reject it without `--histogram` with status 2 and empty stdout before image reads. In `tools/sample_reports.py::report`, keep the existing counting and sorted/top-color selection, then, only when requested, scan the decoded region once more to accumulate min/max coordinates for the emitted color keys. Reuse `_positioned_region_pixels` and, for `--alpha`, `_region_alpha`: RGB mode groups opacity variants together; alpha mode uses exact RGBA keys, including uncomposited RGB beneath transparency and opaque fallback 255. Retain bounds state only for emitted keys, without lists of matching pixels or additional image reads. Each emitted JSON color gains `bounds: {"x": X, "y": Y, "width": W, "height": H}`; append `  bounds=X,Y,W,H` after the existing text color fields. Bounds use absolute image coordinates and enclose disconnected occurrences within the requested region; they do not imply a solid rectangle. Keep ordering, counts, top-color summaries and omitted-option output intact. Add `tests/test_sample_histogram_bounds.py` using `support.cli_fixtures.CliTestCase` and `support.png_fixtures`, document the option in README.md's sampling section, and add a dated tooling guarantee in `docs/invariants.md`. These six files bound one run; no dependency, decoder or theme-art changes are needed.

**Acceptance criteria.** Independently specified fixtures assert text and JSON bounds for a single pixel, a uniform region, and disconnected occurrences whose extrema lie on different rows. A crop with nonzero origins in both axes excludes same-colored outside pixels and reports absolute coordinates. Cover tied counts and `--top-colors 1`, limits at/above the distinct count, unchanged summaries, RGB grouping across opacity variants, RGBA separation at alpha 0/128/255, preserved transparent RGB and opaque fallback. Without the flag, existing histogram output remains covered by its regressions. Misuse with plain sampling, runs or find-color returns 2 with empty stdout before header or row reads. Assert one bounded PNG decode, direct-script JSON and help text; a helper spy should show the additional bounds traversal is skipped without the flag. Run `make check` after the final implementation/documentation edit.

### Fidelity gate: cap the worst channel delta alongside aggregate budgets (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Allow an aggregate error budget to tolerate small differences while rejecting an isolated severe error. `tools/fidelity_metrics.py::Metrics.max_delta` already reports the worst absolute channel delta; `tools/fidelity_reports.py::budget_verdict` now gates it alongside MAE, differing fraction and RMSE. The RMSE budget remains supported.

**Implementation.** Added `--max-delta N` with ASCII integer validation from 0 through 255. The gate combines each supplied budget, uses the already computed raw RGBA maximum, and keeps default output unchanged when omitted. JSON records `thresholds.max_delta`; text displays the cap before tolerance. Added CLI coverage, documented raw alpha and transparent RGB behavior in README.md, and updated the fidelity invariant. Verification: `make check` passed after the final edits.

### Fidelity gate: accept an explicit RMSE budget (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Let a comparison constrain concentrated channel errors with the root mean square error already computed by `tools/fidelity_metrics.py::compare`. `tools/fidelity.py::main` exposes MAE and differing-fraction budgets; `tools/fidelity_reports.py::budget_verdict` checks those two metrics, while `render_text` already prints RMSE. Searches for `max-rmse` and RMSE-budget terms in source, tests and planned/archived entries found no such gate. This is independent of the waiting sampler alpha-filter plan.

**Approach and files.** Add `--max-rmse F` to `tools/fidelity.py::main`, with a `max_rmse` validator in `tools/fidelity_arguments.py` reusing `_finite_float` and `_channel_amount` to accept finite plain ASCII numbers in 0..255. Extend `tools/fidelity_reports.py::budget_verdict` with an optional trailing `max_rmse=None` parameter: compare the existing full-precision `metrics.rmse <= max_rmse`, require each supplied budget to pass, and use the current no-differing-pixel fallback only when no budget is supplied. Pass the new value by keyword. Extend `report_data` with a defaulted keyword parameter without moving existing positional parameters; add `thresholds.max_rmse` only when supplied. In `render_text`, insert `max-rmse=F` formatted to four decimals before `tolerance=` on the verdict line only when supplied. Preserve omitted-option text and JSON shapes. Update the CLI synopsis/help and README.md's Fidelity checking budget explanation: RMSE uses the existing raw channel bytes, including alpha as computed today, is independent of tolerance, and is not perceptual error. Add `tests/test_fidelity_rmse_budget.py` using `support.fidelity_cli_case.FidelityCliTestCase`, and update the aggregate-budget tooling row in `docs/invariants.md` with the implementation date. The run touched the six listed files; no metric computation, image decoder, render gate invocation or dependency changes were needed.

**Acceptance criteria.** Use independently calculated small PNG fixtures to show a sparse large error passing MAE but failing RMSE; an RMSE-only budget replaces the strict default; and combinations fail whenever any supplied budget fails. Pin exact equality and just-below thresholds with an exactly representable RMSE fixture, zero on identical/different images, and the upper bound 255. Cover alpha-only differences, opaque RGB inputs (the CLI decodes alpha), nonzero candidate/reference crops excluding an outside error, and tolerance 255 still allowing an RMSE-budget failure. Assert full-precision JSON threshold, matching text verdict/status, and omitted-option output compatibility with the existing schema and verdict line. Invalid negative, over-255, nonfinite, fractional-malformed, non-ASCII and missing values return 2 with empty stdout before image reads; ordinary decimal fractions remain valid. Exercise direct-script JSON invocation and help text. Expanded tests also pin MAE/RMSE interactions, exact threshold equality, raw transparent RGB, missing arguments and help output. Existing budget/report regressions stayed green under `make check`.

### Reference-pixel sampler: filter color-location bounds by exact alpha (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Locate a color's visible or transparent artwork bounds without merging pixels of different opacity. `tools/sample_reports.py::report` currently searches RGB alone; `tools/sample.py::main` decodes alpha only for `--alpha`, which it rejects with `--find-color`. Searches of sampler source/tests and planned/archived headings found RGB color location, RGB tolerance, and alpha-aware samples/runs/histograms, but no alpha filter for color location. This is independent of the queued fidelity diagnostic.

**Approach and files.** Add optional `--match-alpha N` in `tools/sample_arguments.py::build_parser`, accepting a plain ASCII integer from 0 through 255 using the existing numeric-validation conventions. In `tools/sample.py::main`, reject explicit use without `--find-color` before image reads, including zero, and request bounded `read_png(..., alpha=True)` when the filter is supplied. Retain the existing `--alpha --find-color` rejection: this new option supplies a search predicate rather than changing sample output. In the find-color branch of `tools/sample_reports.py::report`, traverse `_region_alpha` alongside `_region_pixels` when requested and count a pixel only when its alpha equals N and its RGB satisfies the existing color-tolerance predicate. Missing alpha is 255; preserve RGB beneath transparency without compositing. Add integer `alpha` inside JSON's `match` object and an `alpha: N` text line after the optional tolerance line only when the filter is supplied. Retain absolute enclosing bounds and null/none for no match. Add `tests/test_sample_match_alpha.py` using `support.cli_fixtures.CliTestCase` and existing PNG fixtures, document the filter under README.md's Sampling reference pixels, and update the find-color invariant in `docs/invariants.md` with the implementation date. These six files bound one run; no decoder change, new dependency or theme value is needed.

**Acceptance criteria.** Independently enumerated fixtures with equal RGB and alpha 0/128/255 pin exact filtering, disconnected matches, nonzero multi-row region origins, exclusion outside the region, and absent-match bounds. Cover opaque RGB fallback and truecolor `tRNS`; combining RGB tolerance with the filter must still require exact alpha equality, including at tolerance 255. Text and JSON agree on target alpha, counts and bounds. Omission retains RGB-only counts and omits the added field/line; mocks prove alpha decoding is requested only when needed and preserves the requested bottom-row bound. Invalid negative, over-255, fractional, non-ASCII, malformed or missing values, and use without find-color (including histogram/runs), return 2 with empty stdout before header/row reads. Retain the alpha/find-color conflict, read/bounds/containment errors, and exercise direct-script JSON invocation. Run `make check` after the final implementation/documentation edit.

### Reference-pixel sampler: distinguish alpha levels in palette histograms (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Count transparent artwork colors without merging identical RGB values that have different opacity. `tools/sample.py::main` explicitly rejected `--alpha --histogram`; `tools/sample_reports.py::report` counted RGB tuples despite `_region_alpha` supplying bounded alpha samples with an opaque fallback.
