Updated parser help, histogram and alpha tests, README sampling documentation and the histogram/top-colors invariants. No decoder change or dependency was needed.

**Acceptance criteria.** Tests cover alpha 0/128/255, RGB beneath transparency, tie ordering, an offset multi-row crop, opaque RGB and truecolor tRNS; text/JSON schemas; bounded alpha decoding; top-color truncation and totals; unchanged RGB-only behavior; and direct-script JSON. `make check` passed after the final edits.

### Reference-pixel sampler: measure transparency boundaries in scanline runs (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Measure transparent artwork's contiguous RGBA bands without counting individual pixel output. `tools/sample.py::main` rejects `--alpha --runs`; `tools/sample_reports.py::_color_runs` merges adjacent equal RGB values irrespective of alpha. **Goal.** The close button GTK draws at the end of an editable notebook tab still ghosts its glyph: both toolkit resources claim the close button's ink at 30 % alpha — GTK 4 as `rgb(from currentColor r g b / calc(alpha * 0.3))`, GTK 3 as `alpha(currentColor,0.3)` — and each claim sits on a selector one element token longer than the landed `button.flat` restatements can answer, so close tabs on Platinum would read a ghost stamp on the already landed opaque raised flat face (the landed plain flat entries restate `button.flat` faces but never claim the tab-specific ink the stock arms out-rank them on), and a disabled close button inherits the ghost instead of the landed insensitive grey. ### Platinum GTK 4 plain suggested-action buttons: restate the stock blue family with the landed push-button recipe (planned 2026-10-31 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-31 by the feature role

**Goal.** A GTK 4 push button carrying the `suggested-action` class must draw the landed Platinum push-button face in every armed state — base, hover, press, checked, keyboard focus and disabled — instead of the stock blue gradient family.

**Grounding.** `grep -n "suggested" theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` matches only the landed square-pill container group at the sheet's mid-section, whose `menubutton.suggested-action.pill` member declares `border-radius: 0` and nothing else — no plain `button.suggested-action` state rule exists in the sheet, and no `PLANS.md ## Planned` entry, `PLANS-DONE.md` finished record, `BUGS.md`/`BUGS-FIXED.md` heading or `docs/invariants.md` row names the plain suggested-action family (the landed GTK 3 OSD suggested-action and destructive-action plans restated only the `.osd`-scoped arms; the landed plain disabled/backdrop plan's scope boundary reserves the plain variants as candidate plans of their own, confirmed by `PLANS-DONE.md`'s "families for later" record). Probed with `gresource` on 2026-10-31 from `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-4.so.1` (libgtk-4 4.18.6, extraction under a scratch dir), the stock plain family is: `button.suggested-action` with white text, `outline-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8)`, `border-color: #15539e`, a `linear-gradient` `background-image`, a `0 1px 2px` drop shadow and `transition-property`/`transition-duration: 300ms`; a second base arm with `outline: 0 solid transparent; outline-offset: 4px`; `button.suggested-action:focus:focus-visible` with `outline-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8); outline-width: 2px; outline-offset: -2px`; `button.suggested-action:hover` with a fresh gradient and `border-color: #185fb4`; `button.suggested-action:active, button.suggested-action:checked` with `image(#1961b9)`; `button.suggested-action:disabled` repainting to the stock greyed face `image(#faf9f8)` with `color: #929595`; and `button.suggested-action:disabled:active, button.suggested-action:disabled:checked` with `image(#2f80e3)`. Each of these selectors carries one class more than the landed `button`, `button:hover`, `button:active, button:checked`, `button:focus:focus-visible`, `button:backdrop…` and `button:disabled…` groups, so it outranks them and no sheet-order tie decides any arm. No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK suggested-action button at all (the GTK scope's standing adaptation premise), so each arm reuses the landed plain push-button recipe of the same sheet — the recipe precedent the landed `.osd button.suggested-action` plan set byte-for-byte follows, including the erased suggested colour distinction.

background-image: none; border-color: #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA; color: #000000; outline-color: #000000; transition: none` (the base arm must restate `transition: none` because the stock base's 300ms outline animation outranks the landed `button` group's lower-specificity one); `button.suggested-action:hover` declaring exactly `background-color: #DDDDDD; background-image: none; border-color: #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA; color: #000000; outline-color: #000000` (a hover arm needs the full recipe because the stock hover gradient and white text outrank the landed `button:hover` face group); `button.suggested-action:active, button.suggested-action:checked` declaring exactly `background-image: none; border-color: #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #AAAAAA, inset -1px -1px #FFFFFF; color: #000000; outline-color: #000000` (the landed sunken face); `button.suggested-action:disabled, button.suggested-action:disabled:active, button.suggested-action:disabled:checked` declaring exactly `background-image: none; border-color: #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA; color: #888888` (the one-rule insensitive restatement the landed disabled/backdrop plan set — a disabled control takes no press, and the plain `button:disabled` `-gtk-icon-filter: opacity(0.5)` dimming stays in force here because no restated arm names the property); and `button.suggested-action:focus:focus-visible` declaring exactly `outline-color: #000000` beside the landed plain arm's own value. No geometry, artwork, padding or dependency change; no other rule in the sheet is touched.

In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, add `TestGtk4Theme::test_suggested_action_plain_arms` beside `test_button_hover_icon_filter` (test anchoring, not a line number): with `assert_rule`, the restated dictionaries assert `self.rules["button.suggested-action"]` equals `{"background-color": FACE, "background-image": "none", "border-color": BLACK, "box-shadow": BUTTON_BEVEL, "color": BLACK, "outline-color": BLACK, "transition": "none"}`; `button.suggested-action:hover` equals the same dict without the `transition` key; `button.suggested-action:active` and `button.suggested-action:checked` equal `{"background-image": "none", "border-color": BLACK, "box-shadow": INVERTED_BUTTON_BEVEL, "color": BLACK, "outline-color": BLACK}` (the landed sunken-face constants from `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, so a change to the landed face must be mirrored here or the test fails); each of `button.suggested-action:disabled`, `button.suggested-action:disabled:active` and `button.suggested-action:disabled:checked` equals `{"background-image": "none", "border-color": BLACK, "box-shadow": BUTTON_BEVEL, "color": DISABLED_TEXT["color"]}`; and `button.suggested-action:focus:focus-visible` equals `{"outline-color": BLACK}` (the tie test also asserts it equals `self.rules["button:focus:focus-visible"]["outline-color"]`). ### Platinum GTK content-view surfaces: restate the stock base field on GTK 4 and clear the stock hover icon highlight in both sheets (planned 2026-10-31 by the plan role; independent of the landed GTK 4 push-button hover icon-filter entry (— done 2026-10-31, now in `## Done` below) — the entries touch `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` and `docs/invariants.md`, but every edit appends tail text or inserts beside a different neighbour: this entry appends its two GTK 4 `.content-view` blocks after that entry's `button:hover` block at the sheet tail, adds `TestGtk4Theme::test_content_view_field_and_hover` beside `test_view_background` while that entry adds its test beside `test_button_checked_hover_and_active`, appends one `.content-view:hover` block at the tail of `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` that touches no `button` selector, adds `TestGtkTheme::test_content_view_hover` beside `test_content_view_background`, and appends its own `## gtk` invariants row; a `button:hover` tie and a `.content-view:hover` tie are decided independently in source order because no selector of either entry carries a token of the other, and the landed `test_content_view_background` counts only exact `.content-view` and `.content-view:backdrop` selectors, so either queue order leaves both cascades and the tables right)
— done 2026-10-31 by the feature role

**Goal.** A GTK container carrying the `content-view` class (GTK's `GtkIconView` and grid-style content containers add that class) must paint the landed Platinum white field in every state the toolkit repaints: on GTK 4 the shipped sheet names the class nowhere, so stock's grey field and its hovered-icon brightening both show; on GTK 3 the landed white base and backdrop group never covers stock's hover arm, so hovering an icon view still asks the toolkit to highlight the item icons.

**Grounding.** `grep -n "content-view" theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` matched nothing before the appended rules landed and now prints only the appended dated comment and the two `.content-view` blocks it added; before landing `grep -n "content-view:hover" theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` printed the landed base group at `.content-view, .content-view:backdrop` only, so no hover arm existed in either sheet. Probed with `gresource` on 2026-10-31: `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-4.so.1` (libgtk-4 4.18.6) declares `.content-view { background-color: #e6e3e0; }` and a separate `.content-view:hover { -gtk-icon-filter: brightness(1.2); }` arm (its `.content-view:backdrop` arm does not exist — grep over the extracted resource shows no `:backdrop` compound), so both a grey container fill and a hover icon brightening take effect that the landed `.view, list` group only fixes for the plain view classes. `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0` (libgtk-3 3.24.49) declares the same base and a `.content-view:hover { -gtk-icon-effect: highlight; }` arm the landed GTK 3 group never touches, so hovering a GTK 3 icon view applies stock's separate icon-highlight effect (a property axis distinct from the `-gtk-icon-shadow` reset the landed GTK 3 push-button arm clearance already records and pins on `button`, proving the parser handles `-gtk-icon-effect`). No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK icon view or content-view container, so the base field reuses the landed white view field (pinned by `assert_view_background` through `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py::VIEW_BACKGROUND` and by the landed `TestGtkTheme::test_content_view_background`) and the two hover clearances follow the sheets' established `none` convention for stock interaction recolours on states no reference shows.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, append at the sheet tail (after the landed `button:checked:hover, button:checked:active` block and after any rules other entries have added since) one dated (2026-10-31) adaptation comment naming the missing content-view reference surface, the GTK 4 probe above and the landed `.view, list` group as the field source, then a `.content-view` rule declaring exactly `background-color: #FFFFFF; color: #000000;` — the stock twin selector ties stock's base grouping at equal specificity, so the appended later source order wins, and stock's `.content-view .tile` members carry their own selectors, which need nothing from this rule. Then `.content-view:hover` declaring exactly `-gtk-icon-filter: none`. In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, append at the sheet tail one equally dated comment naming the GTK 3 probe (base and backdrop already restated by the landed group, so only the hover axis survives here) and the landed GTK 3 push-button clearance as the `none` convention source, then a `.content-view:hover` rule declaring exactly `-gtk-icon-effect: none`. In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, add `TestGtk4Theme::test_content_view_field_and_hover` beside `test_view_background`: `assert_rule(".content-view", VIEW_BACKGROUND)` (import `VIEW_BACKGROUND` from `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, already exported there and used through `GtkSharedControlCases::assert_view_background`) and `assert_rule(".content-view:hover", {"-gtk-icon-filter": "none"})`. In `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, add `TestGtkTheme::test_content_view_hover` beside `test_content_view_background`: `assert_rule(".content-view:hover", {"-gtk-icon-effect": "none"})`. Append one row at the end of the `## gtk` invariants table in `docs/invariants.md` naming both new tests, the two dated gresource probes, the missing reference surfaces and the declaration-only coverage stating the GTK 4 sheet gains its first content-view declarations while GTK 3 gains only the hover clearance.

**Acceptance criteria.** Deleting either appended rule, renaming a selector to anything but its exact stock twin (`.content-view` on GTK 4; `.content-view:hover` in both sheets) or changing any declared value fails the new test in the affected suite. The landed `test_view_background` (both suites), `test_content_view_background`, `test_button_text_and_icon_shadows`, `test_links`, `test_only_palette_hex_literals` and `test_no_universal_selector` stay green: the appended values reuse literals already in each sheet (`#FFFFFF`, `#000000`, `none`), add no universal selector, and the exact-dict expectations of `test_content_view_background` and the shared `assert_view_background` still hold because the new selectors are separate keys in `tests/support/gtk_css.parse_css`'s per-selector dictionaries. On GTK 3 the landed `test_button_text_and_icon_shadows` guard is untouched: `strip_comments(self.css).count("content-view")`-style exact counts in that test name `button` selectors only. Run `make check`. It merges before or after any other waiting entry in either order.

**Scope boundary.** The stock `.content-view .tile` base and state arms (GTK 3 and GTK 4: `:active`, `:selected`, `:disabled`, the GTK 4-only `:backdrop`), the 32px `.content-view .tile check…`/`iconview.content-view.check…` tile-check family with its GTK 3 `:not(list)` variants (10 stock arms across both toolkits, the whole check treatment), the content-view rubber-band member selectors of the stock `rubberband` groups, GTK's `GtkFlowBox`/`GtkGridView` child classifications, and the disabled/backdrop label-grey reuse stay out — each a candidate plan of its own if a later inspection shows a residue. No artwork, geometry, metric or dependency change.

### Platinum GTK 3 OSD scale thumbs: restate the stock `.osd scale slider` arms with the landed scale-slider recipes (planned 2026-10-30 by the plan role; independent of any meter restatement that merges first — it restates only slider-node selectors, neither entry styles the other's selectors, both entries extend `test_osd_overlay_bands`'s scope filter and append at the sheet's tail with append-only edits, and any merge order leaves the cascade correct, as the approach spells) — done 2026-10-30 by the feature role

### Platinum GTK 3 OSD entry and spin-button fields: restate the stock dark field arms with the landed entry recipe (planned 2026-10-30 by the plan role; independent of the waiting Firefox toolbar-fields plan — it appends four field rules to the GTK 3 sheet, adds one test beside `test_osd_overlay_bands` in `tests/test_gtk_theme.py` and a row in the `## gtk` invariants table, while that entry edits the Firefox chrome sheet, `tests/support/firefox_chrome_cases.py`, `tests/test_firefox_theme_shell.py` and the `## firefox` table; no shared file, selector or test) — done 2026-10-30 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed GTK 3 OSD container plan repainted every stock OSD overlay
container with the light infobar band, but the fields inside them are still
stock dark: the theme's GTK 3 sheet declares nothing for the `.osd` entry arms
(grep: the sheet's only `osd` rules are the landed container block), so the
toolkit's installed resource supplies them — four grouped arms painting
`entry` and horizontal `spinbutton` fields translucent dark with white text
and black text-shadows inside a container the theme now draws `#DDDDDD`.
Restate all four arms to the landed entry recipe, so an OSD field is a
Platinum field like every other entry.

**Verified facts (probed 2026-10-30, `gresource extract
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0
/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css`, libgtk-3 3.24.49).** The
resource's four `entry`-overriding OSD field arms, each a grouped
spinbutton/entry rule: `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical), .osd entry` (`color:
white`, `rgba(0,0,0,0.7)` border, `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` background (a field the
landed light container band contradicts), `background-clip: padding-box`,
both text and icon shadows `0 1px black`); its `:focus` sibling (same field,
`#3584e4` border-colour and an `inset 0 0 0 1px #3584e4` ring); its
`:backdrop` sibling (same dark field, shadows cleared); its `:disabled`
sibling (`rgba(71,71,71,0.5)` field, `#919190` text). No collected reference
screenshot shows a GTK OSD overlay or a field inside one, so this is a
platform adaptation reusing the landed entry recipe — pinned by `ENTRY_FIELD`
in `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py` (`WHITE` face, `BLACK` square border,
inset `GREY` etch, `BLACK` text), the landed focus outline pinned by
`tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_entry_focus_outline` and
`...::test_horizontal_spinbutton_focus_outline` (the dotted-outline trio
`outline: 1px dotted #000000; outline-offset: 0; -gtk-outline-radius: 0;`,
reused from `button:focus` per the landed header comment), and the disabled
text grey pinned by `...::test_disabled_text`, whose `DISABLED_TEXT["color"]`
(`tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, the `ETCH_DARK` value `#888888`) is
re-derived from the colour scheme's `[Colors:Button] ForegroundInactive`. The
arm selector sets and state names are GTK-required (they mirror the toolkit
resource's own grouped rules).

box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999; color: #000000; text-shadow: none;

### Platinum GTK 3 OSD entry and spin-button fields: restate the stock dark field arms with the landed entry recipe (planned 2026-10-30 by the plan role; independent of the waiting Firefox toolbar-fields plan — it appends four field rules to the GTK 3 sheet, adds one test beside `test_osd_overlay_bands` in `tests/test_gtk_theme.py` and a row in the `## gtk` invariants table, while that entry edits the Firefox chrome sheet, `tests/support/firefox_chrome_cases.py`, `tests/test_firefox_theme_shell.py` and the `## firefox` table; no shared file, selector or test) — done 2026-10-30 by the feature role

**Landed 2026-10-30 by the feature role.** Two anchors needed correcting while landing, in the same change: the `## gtk` invariants row names `test_entry`'s actual home (`tests/support/gtk_rule_cases.py::GtkSheetRuleCases::test_entry`, the shared base class) in the provenance cell, because the register parser resolves Test-cell references only against tests defined in the named module; and `test_osd_overlay_bands`'s scope filter now excludes the restated `.osd entry`/`.osd spinbutton` field arms, which contain `.osd` and entered the filter's container set. Everything else landed as written.

**Goal.** The landed GTK 3 OSD container plan repainted every stock OSD overlay
container with the light infobar band, but the fields inside them are still
stock dark: the theme's GTK 3 sheet declares nothing for the `.osd` entry arms
(grep: the sheet's only `osd` rules are the landed container block), so the
toolkit's installed resource supplies them — four grouped arms painting
`entry` and horizontal `spinbutton` fields translucent dark with white text
and black text-shadows inside a container the theme now draws `#DDDDDD`.
Restate all four arms to the landed entry recipe, so an OSD field is a
Platinum field like every other entry.

**Verified facts (probed 2026-10-30, `gresource extract
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0
/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css`, libgtk-3 3.24.49).** The
resource's four `entry`-overriding OSD field arms, each a grouped
spinbutton/entry rule: `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical), .osd entry` (`color:
white`, `rgba(0,0,0,0.7)` border, `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` background (a field the
landed light container band contradicts), `background-clip: padding-box`,
both text and icon shadows `0 1px black`); its `:focus` sibling (same field,
`#3584e4` border-colour and an `inset 0 0 0 1px #3584e4` ring); its
`:backdrop` sibling (same dark field, shadows cleared); its `:disabled`
sibling (`rgba(71,71,71,0.5)` field, `#919190` text). No collected reference
screenshot shows a GTK OSD overlay or a field inside one, so this is a
platform adaptation reusing the landed entry recipe — pinned by `ENTRY_FIELD`
in `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py` (`WHITE` face, `BLACK` square border,
inset `GREY` etch, `BLACK` text), the landed focus outline pinned by
`tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_entry_focus_outline` and
`...::test_horizontal_spinbutton_focus_outline` (the dotted-outline trio
`outline: 1px dotted #000000; outline-offset: 0; -gtk-outline-radius: 0;`,
reused from `button:focus` per the landed header comment), and the disabled
text grey pinned by `...::test_disabled_text`, whose `DISABLED_TEXT["color"]`
(`tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, the `ETCH_DARK` value `#888888`) is
re-derived from the colour scheme's `[Colors:Button] ForegroundInactive`. The
arm selector sets and state names are GTK-required (they mirror the toolkit
resource's own grouped rules).

**Approach and files.** (1) In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`,
append after the landed OSD container block (the `toolbar.osd` grouped rule
that currently closes the sheet) a dated provenance comment naming the
missing reference surface, the gresource probe above and the reuse of the
landed entry recipe, followed by exactly four grouped rules: `.osd
spinbutton:not(.vertical), .osd entry` declaring `background-color: #FFFFFF;
background-image: none; border: 1px solid #000000; border-radius: 0;
box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999; color: #000000; text-shadow: none;
-gtk-icon-shadow: none;` (the landed `ENTRY_FIELD` five declarations verbatim
plus the stock-normal arm's own `text-shadow` and `-gtk-icon-shadow` shadow
claims cleared); the same seven declarations on `.osd
spinbutton:focus:not(.vertical), .osd entry:focus` plus the landed focus trio
(the border shorthand replaces stock's `#3584e4` border-colour and the

`.osd spinbutton:backdrop:not(.vertical), .osd entry:backdrop` (stock's

just shadow clears); the same seven on `.osd spinbutton:disabled:not(.vertical),
.osd entry:disabled` with `color: #888888`. Do not touch the landed
`entry`/`spinbutton:not(.vertical)` rules, their focus rules, the landed
disabled-text rule or the landed OSD container block — each restated arm is

base-field rules keep governing outside `.osd`. From the same probe, scope
notes for later surface plans (recorded here, not this change): the
spin-button's inner transparent text node `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical)
entry`, its button row `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical) button(:hover/:
backdrop/:disabled)` and its dir/last-child radius arms, and the vertical
`.osd spinbutton.vertical button:first-child` family. (2) In
`tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, add `TestGtkTheme::test_osd_entry_fields` beside

landed `ENTRY_FIELD` spec with `background-image: none`, `text-shadow: none`

`tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_osd_entry_fields` and the tests

`...::test_disabled_text`); the provenance cell records the missing reference

reused `ENTRY_FIELD` spec, the GTK-required arm selectors and states, and the
close-out that declaration checks do not establish rendered pixels. Trim no
landed row; `tests/test_invariants.py` parses the register.

**Acceptance criteria.** The GTK 3 sheet ends with the four grouped arms whose
complete parsed dictionaries are exactly the ones above; changing any of the

### Platinum Firefox toolbar fields on Firefox 153.6: bind the field paint to the class-only urlbar background band and paint the live `#searchbar-new` with the landed field recipe (planned 2026-10-30 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 3 OSD-overlay plan — it rewrites the landed urlbar rule and its field tests in `theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userChrome.css`, `tests/support/firefox_chrome_cases.py` and `tests/test_firefox_theme_shell.py` and edits the `## firefox` invariants row, while that entry appends rules to the GTK 3 sheet, adds a test beside the gtk suite's `test_app_notification_band` and appends a row in the `## gtk` table; no shared file, selector or test) — done 2026-10-30 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed `#urlbar-background` rule never matches anything in the
currently installed Firefox ESR 153.6.0esr, so the address field draws stock
today, and the toolbar search field that Firefox actually shows —
`<html:moz-urlbar id="searchbar-new">` under the default
`browser.search.widget.new=true` — has never been painted. Bind the field
paint to the band Firefox really renders (a class-only `.urlbar-background`
div under each urlbar host) and give the live search widget the same
unfocused Platinum field recipe.

**Verified facts (probed 2026-10-30, installed Firefox 153.6.0esr,
`/usr/lib/firefox-esr/browser/omni.ja`).** The urlbar background div comes
from `chrome/browser/content/browser/urlbar/UrlbarInput.mjs`'s `#markup`
template as `<html:div class="urlbar-background"/>` — class only, no id —
and a grep over the fully extracted `omni.ja` chrome tree found no element
with `id="urlbar-background"` (the id is assigned nowhere in
`UrlbarInput.mjs` or any member), so the landed `#urlbar-background`
selector matches nothing in this Firefox. The band's stock paint lives in
`chrome/browser/skin/classic/browser/urlbar-searchbar.css`:
`.urlbar-background` (appended after the focused colour-scheme arms)
draws `background-color: var(--urlbar-background-background-color)`, a
token-formed border and `var(--urlbar-background-border-radius)`, its
`.urlbar:is([focused], [open]) > &` sibling paints focus/open variants, and
`.urlbar[breakout-extend] > &` re-draws the band as the results bubble's
ground (box-shadow breakout). Both toolbar fields are the same widget:
`browser.xhtml` says `<html:moz-urlbar id="urlbar" class="urlbar" ...
sap-name="urlbar">` (the address field) and
`<html:moz-urlbar id="searchbar-new" class="urlbar" ...
sap-name="searchbar">` (the search field, around line 6585), while
`defaults/preferences/firefox.js` line 273 pins
`pref("browser.search.widget.new", true)` — under that default
`urlbar-searchbar.css`'s `@media -moz-pref("browser.search.widget.new")`
block holds `#searchbar { display: none }` and the landed
`#searchbar:not(:focus-within)` recipe is dead code here (it stays live
for a user who turns the pref off, so the plan keeps that rule and its
test entry untouched). The `SmartbarInput.mjs` markup also carries a
`class="urlbar-background"` div under a smartbar host, which is why the
new selector binds the class to the two `moz-urlbar` ids instead of the
bare class. No collected reference screenshot shows Firefox chrome, so
this reuses the landed field recipe's provenance exception: white face and
black 1px square border from the landed `#urlbar-background` declarations,
pinned palette from `tests/support/platinum_palette.py` (`WHITE`, `BLACK`).

**Approach and files.** (1) In
`theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userChrome.css`, replace the
landed `#urlbar-background` rule (before the `.urlbarView-row` block) and
its "Paint only the unfocused classic search field" companion comment with
one dated provenance comment — no reference shows Firefox's toolbar
fields; the id wound up class-only in Firefox ESR 153.6 (`UrlbarInput.mjs`
markup, checked against the extracted `omni.ja` on 2026-10-30); the default
search widget is `#searchbar-new`; the recipe reuses the landed field recipe
— followed by exactly one grouped rule:
`#urlbar:not([focused], [open]) > .urlbar-background, #searchbar-new:not([focused], [open]) > .urlbar-background`
declaring the landed four declarations — `background-color: #FFFFFF
!important; border: 1px solid #000000 !important; border-radius: 0
!important; box-shadow: none !important;`. The `:not([focused], [open])`
guard keeps Firefox's focus ring and the open results bubble's ground
paint (the landed results-row work deliberately left the bubble's own
paint alone); no `color` declaration — the field text stays Firefox's, as
it did under the landed `#urlbar-background` rule, and the classic
`#searchbar:not(:focus-within)` rule keeps its color line. Rewrite the
sheet header's search-field provenance paragraph (ending
"`#searchbar-new` stays Firefox's."): record the 153.6 id-to-class change,
the default pref with the `omni.ja` members named above, and that the
live `#searchbar-new` now takes the same unfocused recipe; change the
header's three "`#urlbar-background`" convention mentions (menu corners,
arrow panels, search field) to the class form. (2) In
`tests/support/firefox_chrome_cases.py`, delete the `"#urlbar-background"`
entry from `REQUIRED_RULES` and add the two new selector keys with the same
four-`!important` declaration dictionary; keep the
`"#searchbar:not(:focus-within)"` entry. `parse_css` splits the grouped
selector list, so both keys see the same rule. (3) In
`tests/test_firefox_theme_shell.py`, replace
`test_search_field_paint_is_scoped_to_the_unfocused_classic_field` with a
scope test that asserts the set of parsed selectors containing
`urlbar-background` equals exactly the two new keys, that each equals
`REQUIRED_RULES`, and that the `searchbar` set equals
`{"#searchbar:not(:focus-within)", "#searchbar-new:not([focused], [open])
> .urlbar-background"}` so the classic rule is still there once; update
`test_header_names_provenance_and_preference`'s expected strings
(`"#searchbar-new stays Firefox's"` and the surrounding phrases) to the new
header wording.
(4) In `docs/invariants.md`, in the `## firefox` table's standing
`userChrome.css` row: replace the sentence that leaves "the newer
`#searchbar-new` widget [to] stay Firefox's" with one stating both toolbar
fields wear the landed white face/square black border unfocused, focused
and open states stay Firefox's, and the classic `#searchbar` keeps its
landed rule for users who disable the default pref; add a dated
provenance text to that row's provenance cell recording the 2026-10-30
probe above (the class-only markup, the default pref, the dead landed
selector found) and the close-out that declaration checks do not
establish rendered pixels; update the test-name cell, which still names
`test_search_field_paint_is_scoped_to_the_unfocused_classic_field`, to the
replacement test.

**Acceptance criteria.** The sheet carries no `#urlbar-background` selector
and carries exactly the two new field selectors with the four landed
declarations; `REQUIRED_RULES` holds both; changing either selector,
deleting the rule or unguarding the focus/open states fails the replacement
scope test; `test_search_field_paint_is_scoped_to_the_unfocused_classic_field`
no longer exists under that name (its replacement pins the new scope);
`test_palette_is_exact`, `test_selectors_are_not_universal`, the classic
search-field entries in `REQUIRED_RULES` and landed `.urlbarView-*` tests
stay green. Scope is the four files named above and nothing else: no GTK
sheet, no new asset, no new palette literal beyond the landed `#FFFFFF` and
`#000000`, no dependency, no `!important` beyond the landed declarations.
The classic `#searchbar:not(:focus-within)` rule keeps its landed text.
`make check` passes.

### CI runs one interpreter, Python 3.13, so local parity is possible (planned 2026-10-30 by the director role; resolves the open BUGS.md entry "CI parity cannot run its Python matrix in the local worktree"; the user directed the simplification on 2026-10-30) — done 2026-10-30 by the feature role

**Goal.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` currently runs a two-version matrix
`['3.10', '3.12']`, but the development environment offers only Python 3.13
(no 3.10/3.12 interpreter or version manager is installed), so no local run
can reproduce the matrix. The user has decided to simplify CI to a single
interpreter, Python 3.13 — the version actually used for development — so
`make check` and `make check-references` locally run the exact matrix CI
runs.

**Approach.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, replace the matrix list with the
single value `['3.13']`. Rewrite the matrix comment: it currently justifies
checking "that floor and the version the project is developed on, so a
newer-only API cannot pass CI and then fail on a supported interpreter";
say instead that the workflow pins Python 3.13 (the development
interpreter, per the user's 2026-10-30 parity decision) while the Makefile's
own floor check still refuses anything older than 3.10 at run time — the
workflow no longer exercises a second interpreter, and that trade-off is
the user's accepted decision. The `actions/setup-python` step, the render-
tool install step and the two `make` steps stay untouched; do not hand-edit
`tumwater.json` or anything outside the named files.

Update the pinning test
`tests/test_ci_workflow.py::TestCIWorkflow::test_workflow_checks_the_python_floor_and_development_version`:
it currently asserts the parsed matrix equals `['3.10', '3.12']`; change the
assertion to `['3.13']` and rename the test to match what it now pins,
`test_workflow_pins_the_python_development_version` (update the `assert`
message the same way; unittest will fail with a clear regex-mismatch message
if the matrix or its quoting changes).

Update the README's "Validating the reference set" paragraph, which says the
workflow runs "on Python 3.10 (the project's floor) and 3.12": it must say
the workflow runs on Python 3.13 and keep the unchanged statement that the
Makefile targets require Python 3.10 or newer (that floor and its wording in
`Makefile`'s `require_python_version` and the "PYTHON=path Python 3.10+"
usage line stay exactly as they are).

**Closing the bug.** On landing, this makes the BUGS.md entry "CI parity
cannot run its Python matrix in the local worktree" moot: the workflow no
declares no second interpreter, so its matrix reproduces locally. Delete the
entry (including its 2026-10-29 Needs-review note) from BUGS.md and record
it in BUGS-FIXED.md as closed "— fixed <landing date> by the feature role",
naming the workflow simplification as the fix.

**Acceptance criteria.** `grep -n "3.10" .github/workflows/ci.yml` and the
same for `3.12` find nothing, the matrix reads `python-version: ['3.13']`
under the unchanged `strategy: fail-fast: false` block,
`test_workflow_pins_the_python_development_version` passes and the old test
name no longer appears under `tests/`, the README paragraph names 3.13 and
still mentions the 3.10 Makefile floor, the bug record has moved from
BUGS.md to BUGS-FIXED.md in the stated form, and `make check` passes.

### Platinum Firefox scrollbars: recolour the chrome and page scrollbars with the scrollbar band and thumb (planned 2026-10-30 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 3 drag-and-drop plan — it edits the two Firefox sheets, their suites and the `## firefox` invariants table while that plan edits the GTK 3 sheet, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py` and the `## gtk` table, and neither entry names a selector or test the other changes) — done 2026-10-30 by the feature role

**Goal.** Every scrollable Firefox surface still draws a non-Platinum scrollbar: the
browser chrome paints the toolkit's platform scrollbars (GTK's overlay bars on this
host) and web pages paint their theme's own trough and thumb, neither of which is
the theme's flat `#EEEEEE` band under a `#DDDDDD` thumb. The GTK sheets already
carry that scrollbar recipe; the landed Firefox sheets style tabs, menus, panels,
tooltips, the find bar and five about-pages but declare nothing about scrollbars,
so the Firefox look is inconsistent with the GTK one on the most common surface
of all. Give both Firefox sheets one scrollbar guarantee: `scrollbar-color` on the
chrome `:root` block recolours the UI scrollbars, and a top-level `:root` rule in
`userContent.css` recolours page scrollbars, both thumb `#DDDDDD` over trough
`#EEEEEE`.

**Verified facts (checked 2026-10-30, Firefox ESR 153.6.0esr).** Grep over
`theme/firefox/`, `tests/`, `PLANS-DONE.md`, `BUGS.md` and `docs/invariants.md`
returns no `scrollbar-color` match: no landed, planned or fixed entry covers
Firefox scrollbars. `unzip -p /usr/lib/firefox-esr/omni.ja
chrome/toolkit/res/scrollbars.css` shows the toolkit's `scrollbar`, `thumb`,
`scrollbarbutton` and `scrollcorner` parts are native anonymous nodes carrying
only `-moz-default-appearance: scrollbar*` declarations (no class or id to
brand), plus `@media (-moz-overlay-scrollbars)` arms that fade inactive chrome
bars: the colour sweep is the standard `scrollbar-color` two-tone property
(CSS Scrollbars Styling Level 1, supported since Firefox 64; geometry, band
width, fade and stepper visibility stay the toolkit's). No collected reference
screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a Firefox scrollbar, so both values
are a platform adaptation reusing the reference-grounded desktop-theme scrollbar
art: the flat `#EEEEEE` trough pinned by
`tests/test_desktoptheme_scrollbar.py::TestScrollbarReference` and grounded in
`setup_emaculation.png` by
`tests/test_colorscheme_reference.py::TestReferenceAnchors.test_view_background_alternate`,
and the `#DDDDDD` thumb face of the same artwork pinned by the same module (the
palette constants `TROUGH` and `FACE` in `tests/support/platinum_palette.py`).
The adaptation's limit must be recorded: `scrollbar-color` carries exactly two
colours, so the thumb's raised `#FFFFFF`/`#999999` bevel, the 1px black trough
and thumb outlines and the step boxes have no property equivalent and
stay unpainted — the painted scrollbar keeps the toolkit's geometry and gains
only the two faces. Page-anonymous scrollbars on sites that set their own
`scrollbar-color` keep that author paint; the origin order puts user-origin
`!important` values ahead of normal author styles.

**Approach and files.** (1) In `theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userChrome.css`,
append to the landed `:root` block (the variable-rule ending before the
`#navigator-toolbox` rule) one declaration `scrollbar-color: #DDDDDD #EEEEEE
!important;` inside it, and one dated provenance comment paragraph naming the
absent reference surface, the toolkit probe above and the adaptation's limit
(two faces only; the thumb bevel, the outlines and the steppers are out of
reach), both faces defined by the desktop-theme pins. (2) In
`tests/support/firefox_chrome_cases.py`, extend the `REQUIRED_RULES[":root"]`
table with `"scrollbar-color": f"{FACE} {TROUGH} !important"` — the shell suite
parses the whole chrome sheet and byte-asserts that table, so the landing is
pinned. (3) In `tests/test_firefox_theme_shell.py`, add
`TestFirefoxChromeShell.test_root_colors_every_chrome_scrollbar` beside
`test_required_rules` asserting `self.rules[":root"]["scrollbar-color"] ==
f"{FACE} {TROUGH} !important"`. (4) In
`theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userContent.css`, after the telemetry
body's closing brace append a dated provenance comment and the sheet's one
top-level rule

```
:root {
  scrollbar-color: #DDDDDD #EEEEEE !important;
}
```

byte-exact. (5) In `tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py`, add
`TestFirefoxContentTheme.test_root_colors_the_page_scrollbars` that asserts
`self.text.count(":root {") == 1`, that the top-level block is present as the
exact three-line form above, and that no `self.bodies` value contains
`scrollbar-color` (the paint stays one top-level sweep; the per-body suites and
`test_no_rule_paints_page_chrome` parse only their own bodies and see none of
it). (6) In `docs/invariants.md`, in the `## firefox` table, append two rows
(one per sheet side, the chrome row first, before the trailing validation
notes): the chrome-side row's guarantee — the chrome UI scrollbars take the
Platinum `scrollbar-color` on the sheet's `:root` block — with the test column
naming `tests/test_firefox_theme_shell.py::TestFirefoxChromeShell::test_required_rules`
and `...::test_root_colors_every_chrome_scrollbar`; the content-side row's
guarantee — every page scrollbar's thumb and trough take the two Platinum faces
through the sheet's one top-level `:root` rule — with the test column naming
`tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py::TestFirefoxContentTheme::test_root_colors_the_page_scrollbars`
and `...::test_palette_is_exact`. Each row's provenance cell names the missing
reference surface (no collected screenshot shows a Firefox scrollbar), the
probe (`unzip -p /usr/lib/firefox-esr/omni.ja chrome/toolkit/res/scrollbars.css`
on 2026-10-30, plus the Firefox-64-supported standard property), the desktop
theme scrollbar pins that ground the two values, and the limitation note (bevel,
outlines and steppers out of the property's reach; geometry stays the toolkit's;
author-origin scrollbar styles on a page keep their paint). Trim no landed row;
`tests/test_invariants.py` parses the register.

**Acceptance criteria.** Both sheets carry the two-face `scrollbar-color` pin:
the chrome `:root` block declares it inside the landed variable set (so
`test_required_rules`, `test_root_colors_every_chrome_scrollbar`,
`test_palette_is_exact` — whose hex set already contains `#DDDDDD` and
`#EEEEEE` — and `test_sheet_has_no_at_rule_or_import` all hold), and the content
sheet carries exactly one top-level `:root` rule whose body is exactly the
pinned declaration while every at-rule body and every at-rule count stays as
landed (`stripped.count("@") == 6` and the body set unchanged). Because
`scrollbar-color` is an inherited property set on the root, every scrollable
box in each document picks it up unless it or a page sets its own style, so
browser popups, sidebars, the library and content scrollbars render a `#DDDDDD`
thumb on a flat `#EEEEEE` trough. Deleting any pinned declaration or changing
either face fails a pinned test; adding a second top-level `:root` rule or a
`scrollbar-color` inside any body fails the content test. Scope is the two named
sheets, the two suites plus `tests/support/firefox_chrome_cases.py` and
`tests/support/firefox_content_cases.py` registers, and `docs/invariants.md`;
no geometry, width, stepper or PDF-viewer-specific rule ships here, the GTK
sheets stay untouched, and `make check` passes.

**Correction 2026-10-30 by the feature role:** the plan's content-test anchor
assumed the sheet contained exactly one `:root {` substring; the landed
about:preferences body already carries an indented `:root {` rule, so
`test_root_colors_the_page_scrollbars` counts column-zero `^:root {` lines

planned).

### Platinum GTK 3 drag-and-drop feedback: repaint the header drop arm with the selection fill (planned 2026-10-30 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 4 drag-and-drop plan — it edits the GTK 3 sheet and `tests/test_gtk_theme.py` while that plan edits the GTK 4 sheet and `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, and it answers the single stock GTK 3 drag arm that the sheet's landed row, header and rubberband rules leave untouched, so no existing selector it names is changed) — done 2026-10-30 by the feature role

**Goal.** During a GTK 3 drag onto a tree view, the sheet's styled header leaks stock paint:
dragging a column over a header button floods that button in the stock accent fill with
white text and a white inset ring — none of it Platinum, and the state variants re-leak it
under the cursor. The sheet styles `treeview.view header button` rows and selection and the
rubberband but declares no `.dnd` rule, so the stock arm colours every tree-header drop
surface. The drop state must read as the theme's selection: repaint it with the
reference-grounded `#CCCCFF`.

**Verified facts, method and values (checked 2026-10-30).** The sheet carries no dnd rule
or test (grep over `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` and
`tests/test_gtk_theme.py` for `dnd` returns nothing), and the GTK drag-and-drop planning in
`PLANS.md` covers only the GTK 4 sheet. The stock inventory re-derived by gresource
extraction on 2026-10-30 —
`gresource extract /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0
/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` — is a single arm, one grouped rule
covering `treeview.view button.dnd` and the legacy `treeview.view header.button.dnd`
spelling, each with `:active`, `:selected`, `:hover` and plain variants, declaring exactly
`padding: 0 6px; color: #ffffff; background-image: none; background-color: #3584e4;
border-style: none; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #ffffff; text-shadow:
none; transition: none;` (grep confirms no other `dnd` selector in that resource: GTK 3 has
no `dndtarget` node and no `dnd tab` arm, so no other surface is covered here). No
reference screenshot shows any drag-and-drop feedback, so every value here is a platform
adaptation: the adaptation reuses the pinned `SELECTION` constant `#CCCCFF` from
`tests/support/platinum_palette.py` — the same value the sheet already applies to selected
rows (`treeview.view:selected`, `list row.activatable:selected`) and text selections — so
the elevated drop state answers the toolkit's accent-family semantics with the theme's
selection family, and no new palette value, artwork or dependency is needed. The stock
`padding: 0 6px` and `transition: none` on the arm stay undeclared, so that transient state
keeps the stock's own geometry and transition choices, mirroring the waiting GTK 4 plan.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, insert directly
after the `treeview.view:selected:backdrop, list row.activatable:selected:backdrop` rule
(the rule ending before the `list row:focus` comment block) a dated adaptation comment and
one grouped rule. Comment convention follows the landed row-selection commentary: name the
absent reference surface, that the stock GTK 3 paints this state with its accent family,

names out of the comment text, as `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`'s
`test_imports_nothing_and_does_not_mention_adwaita` and palette-content assertions require.
The rule covers twelve selectors: `treeview.view button.dnd`, `treeview.view
button.dnd:hover`, `treeview.view button.dnd:active`, `treeview.view button.dnd:selected`,
`treeview.view header.button.dnd`, `treeview.view header.button.dnd:hover`, `treeview.view
header.button.dnd:active`, `treeview.view header.button.dnd:selected`, `treeview.view
header button.dnd`, `treeview.view header button.dnd:hover`, `treeview.view header
button.dnd:active` and `treeview.view header button.dnd:selected` — the stock pair of
spellings plus the sheet's own landed header chain — declaring exactly `background-color:
#CCCCFF;` `background-image: none;` `color: #000000;` `text-shadow: none;` `box-shadow:
none;` `border-style: none;` `border-radius: 0;`. The state variants mirror the stock arm
list, otherwise the stock `:hover` variants outrank a plain `.dnd` rule and re-leak the
accent under the cursor. In `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, add `TestGtkTheme` tests beside
`test_row_selection_backdrop`, using the shared `assert_rule` helper and the imported

`test_no_dndtarget_node_declared` asserting the sheet text contains no `dndtarget` match,
pinning that the GTK 3 inventory stays the single header/button arm. In
`docs/invariants.md`, append one row under `## gtk`: no collected screenshot shows GTK

state reuses the pinned `#CCCCFF` selection instead of the stock accent values, a platform

**Acceptance criteria.** The dnd rule exists in the GTK 3 sheet with exactly the pinned

### Platinum GTK 3 scroll areas: clear the stock overshoot edge glows (planned 2026-10-30 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 4 scroll-edge plan — it edits the GTK 3 sheet and `tests/test_gtk_theme.py` while that plan edits the GTK 4 sheet and `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, so no file or rule text overlaps) — done 2026-10-30 by the feature role

**Goal.** In GTK 3 applications using the installed Platinum theme (`make apply-gtk` sets `gtk-theme-name=org.macos8.desktop`), the stock theme paints radial over-scroll glows: translucent shade-coloured corner fades ("overshoot", the `overshoot.top`/`.bottom`/`.left`/`.right` child nodes of a scrolled window, drawn with two radial `-gtk-gradient` background images). No collected reference screenshot of Mac OS 8.6 shows any such band; Platinum scroll fields are flat, running to the frame, so the glows must render nothing.

`/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` inside
`/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0` (extracted with `gresource`) declares scroll-edge
painting in exactly eight arms: `scrolledwindow overshoot.top`, `scrolledwindow
overshoot.bottom`, `scrolledwindow overshoot.left` and `scrolledwindow overshoot.right`
and the same four with `:backdrop`. Each paints radial gradients on `background-image` and
is otherwise neutral (`background-color: transparent; border: none; box-shadow: none;`);
the dark and inverse variants compiled into the same library spell identical selectors with
different palettes, so the arm set is theme-variant independent. A grep of the extract shows

rodata — so, unlike the GTK 4 sheet work, there is no undershoot family to neutralize. The
cascade differs from GTK 4: this GTK 3 sheet is a standalone named theme that imports
nothing (`tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_imports_nothing_and_does_not_mention_adwaita`),
so it is the only theme stylesheet GTK 3 loads and its rules replace the stock arms rather
than racing them; the arm selectors are still copied verbatim so each rule reads beside the
stock text it replaces. No palette value is new: every declaration is
`background-image: none;`. In-sheet comments must not contain the stock library's name —
`test_imports_nothing_and_does_not_mention_adwaita` rejects it — so the provenance comment
names "the stock GTK 3 resource in libgtk-3" and the library path, and

selectors). The new rules sit beside the landed scrollbar adaptations, so the existing
scrollbar, thumb-minimum and overlay assertions pass untouched. In `docs/invariants.md`,
append one row under `## gtk`: no collected screenshot shows a GTK over-scroll glow; the
eight-arm inventory (including the four `:backdrop` versions and the absence of any
undershoot arm) comes from the stock `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css`

**Acceptance criteria.** All eight stock overshoot arms listed above are matched by

spinbutton:not(.vertical)`, `.linked:not(.vertical) > entry`, `.linked > button`) and restore it
on `:last-child`, and its vertical variants drop `border-bottom-style` over the same members
(`.linked.vertical > ...`, lines 403-417 of the extract). This plan adopts that selector and
side-sharing scheme with the sheet's own values: the shared seam stays the landed 1px black
(`button`'s `border: 1px solid #000000`), and no `border-radius` or `-gtk-outline-radius`
declarations are needed because every member already declares radius 0. Members keep their
landed bevels (`button`'s `inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA`) — the seam shows the
following member's highlight shoulder beside the shared black line, which this plan records as
the decided adaptation rather than a design question. No reference screenshot in
`macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a GTK linked group, so this is a platform adaptation; the stock
resource sources the selector spelling (the `linked` class is GTK-required), while the values are
the landed button/entry declarations. Two landed GTK 3 recipes already style specific linked
containers and must win over the new strip: the file chooser's path bar (`.path-bar > button`,
tab recipe; the `GtkPathBar` node carries the `linked` class with the folder buttons as direct
children) and the stack switcher (`stackswitcher > button`; its node carries the `linked` class
per the landed stack-switcher plan's PyGObject probe). The strip selector
`.linked:not(.vertical) > button` out-ranks `.path-bar > button` on specificity ((0,2,1) vs
(0,1,1)), so the protection re-asserts the outlines with a higher-specificity rule:
`.path-bar.linked > button:not(:last-child), stackswitcher.linked > button:not(:last-child)`
((0,3,1)), which restores `border-right-style` and `border-bottom-style` regardless of the
block's file position. A focused member's propagated seam color (the stock file re-colors the
following member's border under `:focus` and `:drop(active)`) and right-to-left direction
subtleties stay out of scope; no collected screenshot shows either.

sentence to the provenance header comment immediately before the closing `*/`: "A linked group
shares one black border between its members; no reference screenshot shows a GTK linked group,
and the linked class is GTK-required." (2) Append, after the `placessidebar
row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row` rule that ends the file, a `/* Linked groups share one black
border between members; the stock GTK 3 scheme sources the selector spelling
(2026-10-29) */` — corrected 2026-10-29 by the feature role: the plan's original
text named the stock theme inside the CSS, but `test_imports_nothing_and_does_not_mention_adwaita`
rejects that name in the sheet, so the shipped comment says "the stock GTK 3 scheme"
and keeps the library name in the invariants row instead
comment plus the rules: a horizontal strip rule naming `button`, `entry`,
`spinbutton:not(.vertical)` and `combobox > box > button.combo` under
`.linked:not(.vertical) >` with `border-right-style: none`, the same selector list with
`:last-child` restoring `border-right-style: solid`, the same two rules over

the standalone-sheet check (`TestGtkTheme.test_imports_nothing_and_does_not_mention_adwaita`).
In `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, add three `TestGtkTheme` tests: `test_linked_members_strip_their_trailing_border`
(asserts `border-right-style: none` on the four horizontal strip selectors and

(asserts both `:last-child` rules) and `test_linked_protection_keeps_the_path_bar_and_stack_switcher_outlines`
(asserts the protection rule's two declarations and that `.path-bar > button` still declares
`border: 1px solid #000000`, keeping the landed tab recipe intact). In `docs/invariants.md`,
append a row under `## gtk`: no collected screenshot shows a GTK linked group, so this is a

### Separate Firefox profile transaction rollback from the installer (planned 2026-10-29 by the organize role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** Make the boundary between Firefox profile transaction mechanics and install/remove policy explicit. `tools/install_firefox.py` is the largest production Python module (347 lines); it currently combines CLI/profile-lock orchestration, install/remove decisions, and rollback behavior for partially published profile files. In particular, `_restore_file`, `_restore_user_js` and the rollback handler inside `_apply` manage recovery state while `firefox_user_files.py` owns the underlying reads and writes.

**Target structure.** Add `tools/firefox_transaction.py` to own rollback state and handlers: move `_restore_file` and `_restore_user_js` there, and expose one transaction operation that receives the ordered sheet destinations with their prior contents, the `user.js` path/prior/published contents, and the write operation. It publishes the two sheets followed by `user.js`, and on a write exception or interrupt restores published state and combines restoration diagnostics using the existing `ConfigError`. Keep source loading, destination validation, refusal of foreign sheets, profile locking, install/remove policy, and CLI handling in `install_firefox.py`. Keep path resolution and file reads/writes in their existing profile/file modules. Update installer imports and focused transaction tests (currently in `tests/test_install_firefox.py`) to exercise the extracted API; do not change install or rollback behavior.

**Acceptance criteria.** The new module contains the rollback bookkeeping and recovery handler; `install_firefox.py` delegates publication and recovery while retaining validation and policy. Existing failure and interrupt cases continue to verify restoration of old files, removal of newly created files, and combined diagnostics. No stale references to moved helpers remain in source, tests or documentation, and `make check` passes.

### Platinum GTK file chooser: paint the places sidebar band and its rows as the menu-bar face with the landed list-row selection in GTK 3 and GTK 4 (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; independent of the queued about:telemetry furniture plan — that one touches `theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userContent.css` and `tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py`, this one the GTK sheets and their suites, and their `docs/invariants.md` edits only append one new row each, so either order merges; the chooser's path bar landed in PLANS-DONE.md and its file list, column headers, entries, buttons, action bar and paned handle are already covered by the landed generic rules, so the places sidebar is the chooser's remaining surface) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** After the landed path-bar plan, a GTK file chooser's places sidebar — the left column `GtkFileChooserWidget` shows in both toolkits — still paints stock: the band keeps Adwaita's near-white `#fbfafa` face (GTK 3 with a `#f9f9f8` backdrop face; GTK 4 with a grey `#cdc7c2` right border), GTK 3 greys the rows in backdrop (`placessidebar row:backdrop { color: #929595 }` and `placessidebar row:backdrop:selected { color: #fcfcfc }`), a selected row in an inactive GTK 3 window turns Adwaita blue (`row.activatable:selected:backdrop { background-color: #3584e4 }`, outranking the landed selection rule, which has no backdrop arm), and the sidebar's "New bookmark" row keeps Adwaita's link-blue text in both toolkits. This plan paints the sidebar band as the landed flat menu-bar face — `#DDDDDD`, black text, flat backdrop, no border — and pins the chooser-specific row arms, introducing no new hex and editing no landed rule.

**Verified facts (checked 2026-10-27, PyGObject probes with GTK 3.24.49 and GTK 4.18.6 plus the stock sheets extracted from the installed libraries' gresources).** A GTK 3 `Gtk.FileChooserDialog` builds `paned.horizontal > placessidebar[frame, sidebar] > viewport.frame > list > row[activatable, sidebar-row]` rows (one carries `sidebar-new-bookmark-row`); the chooser's header strip holds the `path-bar` (landed) beside a `search` entry (landed), the file list is `treeview.view` (landed) and the bottom bar an `actionbar` (landed). A GTK 4 `Gtk.FileChooserWidget` builds `paned.horizontal > placessidebar[sidebar] > scrolledwindow > viewport > list[navigation-sidebar] > row[activatable, sidebar-row]` rows (plus one `sidebar-new-bookmark-row`); its root `filechooser` node's other paint — the `pathbar` (landed), the `columnview.view` file list (landed), the search `entry` (landed) and the root `actionbar` band (landed) — is covered by landed rules. Stock paint, from the GTK 3 gresource `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` and the GTK 4 gresource `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css`: GTK 3 paints `.sidebar { border-style: none; background-color: #fbfafa }` with `.sidebar:backdrop { background-color: #f9f9f8 }`; GTK 4 paints `.sidebar { background-color: #fbfafa }` with `.sidebar:not(separator):dir(ltr) { border-right: 1px solid #cdc7c2 }`; GTK 3 paints `placessidebar row:backdrop { color: #929595 }`, `placessidebar row:backdrop:selected { color: #fcfcfc }`, `row.activatable:selected:backdrop { background-color: #3584e4 }` and `placessidebar row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row { color: #3584e4 }`; GTK 4 paints `placessidebar .navigation-sidebar > row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row { color: #3584e4 }`. The landed generic arms already paint rest, hover (transparent) and selection (`#CCCCFF`, black text, square): `list row.activatable:hover` and `list row.activatable:selected[:hover]` outrank stock's `row.activatable:hover` and GTK 4's `.navigation-sidebar > row:hover/:selected/:selected:hover`, so only the band face, the backdrop arms, the GTK 4 right border and the new-bookmark text remain stock. The sidebar's inner `list` already stays transparent because stock's `.sidebar list { background-color: transparent }` (0,1,1) beats our landed white `list` rule (0,1,0); stock's `placessidebar > viewport.frame { border-style: none }` likewise already clears the inner viewport's frame against our landed `.frame` rule in GTK 3. `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_disabled_text_follows_the_entry_text_rule` already establishes that our theme sheet loads after the stock base and wins equal-specificity ties by order, so tie-overrides need no `!important`.

**Grounding (platform adaptation, steward clarification 2026-10-25).** No reference screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a GTK widget, and Mac OS 8.6's Finder has no sidebar at all, so the band reuses the reference-grounded flat menu-bar/window face `#DDDDDD` with black text (the landed `window, .background` face) and a flat `#DDDDDD` backdrop mirroring the landed headerbar's inactive face; the rows reuse the landed `list row` recipe whose `#CCCCFF` selection is the pinned `[Colors:Selection]` of `tests/test_colorscheme_reference.py::TestReferenceAnchors::test_selection_background` and whose squareness extends the landed `border-radius: 0` selection. The `placessidebar` node name, the `sidebar`, `frame`, `navigation-sidebar` and `sidebar-new-bookmark-row` classes, the stock row geometry (the 36px min-height, stock paddings and margins) and the drag-over indicator (`:drop(active)` arms, painted green by stock) are GTK-required; the rows' geometry and the drag indicator stay stock. Recorded, not planned here: the same GTK 3 `:backdrop` arms grey or blue every generic list row in an inactive window (our landed row rule has no backdrop arm outside the sidebar) — a natural subject of a later plan deciding whether the landed row recipe grows backdrop arms generally.

**Approach.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, append after the landed `.path-bar > button` block at the sheet's end:

```css
/* A file chooser's places sidebar takes the flat menu-bar face with black
   text in backdrop, and its rows keep the landed selection and drop
   Adwaita's link blue. */
.sidebar {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  color: #000000;
}

.sidebar:backdrop {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  color: #000000;
}

placessidebar row:backdrop {
  color: #000000;
}

placessidebar row.activatable:selected:backdrop {
  background-color: #CCCCFF;
  color: #000000;
}

placessidebar row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row {
  color: #000000;
}
```

`.sidebar` ties stock's `.sidebar` face on specificity and wins by coming later; `placessidebar row:backdrop` (0,1,2) and `placessidebar row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row` (0,1,2) tie and win the same way; `placessidebar row.activatable:selected:backdrop` (0,2,2) beats stock's `row.activatable:selected:backdrop` (0,2,1). GTK 3 keeps the landed `.frame` sunken black box around the chooser's sidebar (the `frame` class is on the `placessidebar` itself) and stock's `placessidebar > viewport.frame` clear.

In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, append at the sheet's end after the landed `pathbar` block:

```css
/* A file chooser's places sidebar takes the flat menu-bar face and drops
   the stock grey right border; its new-bookmark row drops Adwaita's link
   blue. */
.sidebar {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  color: #000000;
  border: none;
}

.sidebar:backdrop {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  color: #000000;
}

placessidebar.sidebar:not(separator):dir(ltr),
placessidebar.sidebar:not(separator):dir(rtl) {
  border: none;
}

placessidebar .navigation-sidebar > row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row {
  color: #000000;
}
```

The border-clearing rule spells the stock arms `.sidebar:not(separator):dir(ltr)`/`:dir(rtl)` through the `placessidebar.sidebar` node so it ties (0,3,0) with stock's border-right rule and wins by coming later; plain `placessidebar.sidebar { border: none }` (0,1,1) would lose to (0,3,0) and is spelled only as part of that rule. GTK 4 needs no row backdrop arms: stock's `.navigation-sidebar > row` has none, so the landed selection and transparent hover hold in backdrop too.

In `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, add `TestGtkTheme.test_places_sidebar` mirroring `test_path_bar_tabs`'s `assert_rule` idiom with the spec-module constants (`FACE`, `BLACK`, `SELECTION` from `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, which re-exports the pinned `platinum_palette.py` values):

Both suites' existing exact-set and palette tests (the sheets' `@define-color` register and hex checks in `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`/`tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`) must stay green without edits — the new rules reuse only `#DDDDDD`, `#CCCCFF` and `#000000`.

In `docs/invariants.md`, in the `## gtk` table, append one row after the current last row (the tree-header row) before the trailing validation notes: the guarantee in one sentence — both GTK sheets paint the file chooser's places sidebar band (`placessidebar`, the `sidebar` class) as the flat `#DDDDDD` menu-bar face with black text and a flat `#DDDDDD` backdrop, clear GTK 4's stock grey right border, keep GTK 3's rows black-texted in backdrop with the landed `#CCCCFF` square selection in backdrop, and paint the `sidebar-new-bookmark-row` black while the rows' geometry and drag-over indicator stay stock — with the test column naming `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_places_sidebar` and `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_places_sidebar`, and the provenance cell naming the missing reference surface (no reference screenshot shows a GTK widget; the Finder has no sidebar), the reused face (the landed `window, .background` band) and row selection (`widgets/listitem.svg`'s flat fill, `test_selection_background`), the gresource and PyGObject probes above, the GTK-required node and class names, and that declaration checks establish no rendered pixels. ### Firefox Platinum content: paint about:telemetry's page furniture — the category sidebar rows, the section-filter search field and store menu and the ping-picker panel — with the landed nav-row, line-edit, menulist and panel recipes (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; the recorded first half of the about:telemetry work — the data payloads, the sections' tables, the histogram bars, the copy buttons and the raw-JSON viewers, are the natural subjects of a later plan whose reuse of this plan's furniture recipes and this page's remaining surfaces is decided then, so no design question is left open here; independent of the queued about:networking sidebar plan — the two touch the same sheet and test module, so all anchors below are rule texts and symbol names, never line numbers) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed `userContent.css` sheet paints the about:downloads list, the about:config field, the about:preferences pane, the about:support tables and buttons and the about:networking tables and buttons; Firefox's about:telemetry page keeps its stock paint entirely. This plan paints the page's furniture: its `#categories` sidebar rows (including the dynamically added `.category-subsection` rows), the `.header` strip's `#search` filter field and `#stores` store menu, and the floating `#ping-picker` panel each take the landed recipe byte-for-byte, reusing only values the sheet and test module already pin, so no new constant and no new hex is introduced and no landed rule changes. The sections' data payloads stay stock here.

**Verified facts (checked 2026-10-27, Firefox ESR 153.5.1; probe scratch at `/tmp/tum-scratch-omz/omni`).** `chrome/toolkit/content/global/aboutTelemetry.xhtml` is the light-DOM page (no `attachShadow` in it, its `.css` or its `.js`): `div#categories` holds fourteen static `div.category.category-no-icon` rows each wrapping `span.category-name`, the first carrying `class="category category-no-icon has-data selected"` at load, and `aboutTelemetry.css`'s `.category:not(.has-data) { display: none }` hides every row until data exists, so the paint need not special-case the badge. `aboutTelemetry.js` flips the selection with the CLASS, never an attribute (unlike about:networking's `[selected]`-attribute-only rule): `current_button = document.querySelector(".category.selected"); current_button.classList.remove("selected"); selected.classList.add("selected")`, and `showSubSection` does the same with `.category-subsection.selected`; the subsection rows appear only when JS adds them (aboutTelemetry.css gives `.category.selected > .category-subsection { display: block }`), so the handles are `#categories > .category.selected` and `#categories .category-subsection.selected`. The stock row paint comes from `chrome://global/skin/classic/global/in-content/common-shared.css`, whose `#categories > .category`, `:hover`, `:hover:active`, `.category.selected` and `:focus-visible` arms are the very arms the sheet's landing about:networking body already overrides with `!important`. The `.header` strip (aboutTelemetry.css) holds `h1#sectionTitle`, `label#storesLabel`, `select#stores` (hidden until the JS displays a store list) and `input[type="text"]#search` in `div#sectionFilters`; `#search` sits outside `.main-content`, so the landing table-field arm does not reach it. `#ping-picker` is a fixed-position panel `aboutTelemetry.css` paints `--background-color-box` on `--border-color` with `border-radius: 2px` and `box-shadow: 0 1px 3px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.25)`; it is stock white-on-white in the light scheme and our square black outline replaces that shadow. Grep for `telemetry` in `theme/firefox/`, `tests/`, `PLANS.md`, `PLANS-DONE.md`, `BUGS.md` and `BUGS-FIXED.md` returns nothing: neither a landed nor a planned entry covers this page. `tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py::TestFirefoxContentTheme::test_sheet_has_the_downloads_config_preferences_support_and_networking_at_rules` asserts the five-body body set and `stripped.count("@") == 5`, so this plan's sixth body must extend that test; its `test_no_rule_paints_page_chrome` iterates every body's selectors against `FORBIDDEN_PAGE_CHROME = ("body", "h1", "hgroup", "main-content-title")`, which the furniture selectors below avoid, and `test_palette_is_exact` already contains every hex below, so neither needs edits.

**Grounding (platform adaptation, steward clarification 2026-10-25).** No reference screenshot shows Firefox's about:telemetry (the same missing surface the landed about:networking row of `docs/invariants.md` records): the sidebar rows reuse the landed nav-row values — transparent rest, flat `#CCCCFF` black-text hover/active and selected faces, `border-radius: 0` — whose `#CCCCFF` is the pinned `[Colors:Selection]` of `tests/test_colorscheme_reference.py::TestReferenceAnchors.test_selection_background` and whose squareness extends the landed list-row `border-radius: 0`; `#search` reuses the landed line-edit field byte-recipe (`FIELD_RULE` in `tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py`, grounded in `widgets/lineedit.svg` and pinned by `tests/test_desktoptheme_lineedit.py::TestLineEdit` and `TestLineEditReference`); `#stores` reuses the landed pane menulist byte-recipes (`PANE_MENULIST_RULE` and `PANE_MENULIST_HOVER_RULE` in the test module, spelled explicitly so the button recipes cannot silently retarget the pane); `#ping-picker` reuses the sheet's white face and black square outline over the stock rounded ember-cast panel (the Finder's plain white pop-panel shape, no `#CCCCFF` involvement). The `.selected`-class selection and the JS-added subsections are Firefox-required; the rows' stock 42px minimum height and padding, the `:focus-visible` outline and the page's `#sectionTitle` heading, `#storesLabel` label, home-section headings and links (page chrome) stay Firefox's.

**Approach.** In `theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userContent.css`, append after the landing about:networking body's closing rule a sixth `@-moz-document` body, in the same illustration-comment-plus-rules shape:

```css
@-moz-document url("about:telemetry") {
  /* The category sidebar rows, the section-filter field and store menu
     and the ping-picker panel take the landed flat nav-row, sunken
     line-edit, raised menulist and white panel paints; the sections'
     data payloads are the recorded natural subjects of a later plan
     (see the header's provenance paragraph). */
  #categories > .category {
    background-color: transparent !important;
    color: #000000 !important;
    border-radius: 0 !important;
  }

  #categories > .category:hover,
  #categories > .category:hover:active {
    background-color: #CCCCFF !important;
    color: #000000 !important;
  }

  #categories > .category.selected,
  #categories > .category.selected:hover,
  #categories > .category.selected:hover:active {
    background-color: #CCCCFF !important;
    color: #000000 !important;
  }

  #categories .category-subsection {
    color: #000000 !important;
  }

  #categories .category-subsection.selected {
    background-color: #CCCCFF !important;
    color: #000000 !important;
  }

  #search {
    background-color: #FFFFFF !important;
    color: #000000 !important;
    border: 1px solid #000000 !important;
    border-radius: 0 !important;
    box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999 !important;
  }

  #stores {
    background-color: #DDDDDD !important;
    color: #000000 !important;
    border: 1px solid #000000 !important;
    border-radius: 0 !important;
    box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA !important;
  }

  #stores:hover {
    background-color: #CCCCFF !important;
    color: #000000 !important;
    box-shadow: none !important;
  }

  #ping-picker {
    background-color: #FFFFFF !important;
    color: #000000 !important;
    border: 1px solid #000000 !important;
    border-radius: 0 !important;
    box-shadow: none !important;
  }
}
```

Our `!important` arms beat the stock `common-shared.css` declarations and aboutTelemetry.css's panel paint; specificity settles the rest/hover/selected order, with the selected arms the last row rules so a selected row stays `#CCCCFF` under hover and press.

In the same sheet's header comment, append one provenance paragraph after the landing about:networking paragraph: about:telemetry's furniture — the `#categories` sidebar rows, the `.category-subsection` rows, the `#search` field, the `#stores` menu and the `#ping-picker` panel — is painted by a `@-moz-document url("about:telemetry")` body whose rules aboutTelemetry.js outweigh (selection is the `.selected` class, subsections are JS-added), the rows, field, menu and panel reusing the landed about:networking/about:preferences recipes (the `#CCCCFF` selection of `test_selection_background`, the line-edit recipe of `widgets/lineedit.svg` with `TestLineEdit` and `TestLineEditReference`, the pane button/menulist byte-recipes `PANE_MENULIST_RULE` and `PANE_MENULIST_HOVER_RULE`, and the sheet's white face and black square outline for the panel, whose rounded shadowed stock shape is Firefox's own light-scheme paint and no reference screenshot shows this page); the sections' data payloads and the `#sectionTitle` heading and other page chrome stay Firefox's — the payloads being the recorded natural subjects of a later plan.

In `tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py`, extend the module register after the networking rules —
